Commander keen is simple platformer, it's about a guy, Keen. From my current understanding he is just a dude who travels to random planets and shoots aliens  with his little laser gun, he also has a pogo stick which makes him jump higher. This pack included Keen 1,2,3,4 and 5. The first ones look really old, but the fourth and the fifth looked a lot cleaner and a lot newer.  All of the games play pretty similarly and have the game character and weapons. But I didn’t really finish any other Keen game except Keen 5, so I might be wrong because some things are different later in game. But in Commander Keen 5 you have to collect four diamonds to open doors to continue within the level, then you have to find a key that opens the door to the end of the level, later you have to destroy something what looks like the power source for the space ship you are stranded on. In the game you will encounter various enemies, some are robots some are 'energy enemies', the robots can be killed the 'energy enemies' can only be stunned or can't get hit at all. You have one life, so if you get hit once you are done for, yet you can save everywhere you want, so that isn't a big problem or a hard part about this game. All in all it’s just an old school platformer, that is as unforgiving as any other old game and needless to say the game is also very fun!
After playing this game again after so many years, it made me realize that Commander Keen 4 is way superior to Commander Keen 5, because the fourth installment had way more variety. And when I look back at the levels of Commander Keen 5 I realized that they game wasn't really that special. It was just the fact that it was the first game I ever played and finished, what made it so great. The nostalgia made me love this game.

Most of the negative reviews here are because of technical issues that are solvable on most systems. Fullscreen works by pressing ALT+Enter (maybe not while in the menu or title screen or cutscene, but ingame), widescreen support is available via a hack. On some systems, the resolution may be limited to 640x480 or 800x600, but that is not the normal behaviour. You should get the highest 4:3 resolution closest to your native resolution without a patch. XBox controllers are not officially supported because this game uses directinput for controller support, which is the predecessor to xinput. If you have one of the recent Logitech gamepads (F310 for example), you can choose between directinput and xinput via a hardware switch on the controller, then map the controller keys correctly (setup controller) and the game works out of the box. If you have to use an xbox compatible controller, you have to fiddle around to get the trigger keys working. This is because the trigger keys are analog and on the same axis on the xbox compatible controllers, but are two seperate digital keys on the older standard. Please note that this game was developed before the xbox compatible controllers had been invented! It would have been nice of Capcom to have this version revamped like they did for PS3 and XBox, but they have not.  It is not optimized for the PC and it is an old game, but I still think it is awesome.

If DOTA and LOL isn't your cup of tea, please - try this one. It's unique 2D MOBA centered around aim, map awareness, teamplay and old-school platforming. The plethora of characters with unique, well designed skills (each naut has 2 main skills assigned to 2 buttons + AA, jump and team commands - it's that simple, yet hard to master) and gameplay itself makes this game addictive and ton of fun.
You can try different builds, every skill can be upgraded in a different way, same for AA and utility row (movement, more hp, regen etc.). Game build up on these characters and their role in story. They are all in game (as companions), doesnt matter on which one you play. And all of them make very different gameplay.
*Lucas - 10th Legion grandmaster's son. Knight using sword and shield, greatsword and protective/heal spells.
*Katarina - Rebel girl, daughter of Lucas'es father and witch. Using dual pistols, musket and support spells (including summon spirit hound).
*Anjali - Archon girl, spirit of the fire. Using spear and martial art in human form and fire spells in Archon form. Support spells in 3rd stance.
*Reinhart - Descendant of Merik. Using "steampunk" devices to boost his magic. Using various spells in all stances - lightings, traps, teleport and many more.
There isnt many positives in DS3, and there is many negatives. But its not bad game, biggest problem is, its named Dungeon SIege - this game definitely isnt Dungeon Siege. But how i said, if you forget everything about DS 1+2 and give DS3 a try, i belive you will enjoy it.

This game is essentially a Flash game with great graphics and Roman inspired visuals. The game play is an exceedling over-managed experience, even for something that is a console port where such games are common, although not to this extreme. It's a corridor shooter with a knife.
The best thing about the game are the graphics and the setting. The Roman-inspired backdrops are quite good; but you can't interact with anything in the world--beyond the infrequent over managed color-coded "click the Y button now" item. Don't worry about missing those or not figuring out what thing to click as there is only 1 way through every phase/level--remember, it's a corridor shooter in the worst sense.
The gameplay is dry, repetitive, and gets old fast; which is saying something for a 9 hour game. There's no camera customization options so you're stuck with the too close yo-bro-step-back default over-the shoulder camera. Might be a limitation of the engine, of the devs to add custom/zooming viewbox code, or simply console-SoP.
Regardless, probably around 7 hours in you might be finding it boring and/or irritating and want to accelerate to the end. Why? It's easy to delete, right? Well, gameplay is an excuse to show lots of cutscenes that make use of a really cool graphics engine we developed (seriously why else make games); and I think the character animation and corresponding voice-sync is indeed great. But ultimately it becomes irritatingly obvious that gameplay second, engaging interactive world second, engaging story second, everything second to showing off the cutscenes of our graphics engine.
The voice acting is quite excellent.
If you are at all a Rome aficonado, note carefully that this game takes place in alternative universe with no bearing on anything historical beyond some names that teens who skipped history class might still recognize from the multiple-guess tests they failed. In fact, those teens may have written the story for Ryse ([sic], should be Rise but friends of those same teens run the marketing department, fo' reelz).
If you can accept this minimal suspension of disbelief (ok, not minimal, but come on...game), you might want to pick up the game at a steep steep discount on top of a discount just to have a couple hours of fun swinging your spatha or coordinating some pila throwing with the other legionaries and maybe looking at all the lorica segmentata that is, well, everywhere. If Romans are your bag and you can do that, I'd definitely get it on that discount. It's all the sophistication of a Flash game or Candy Crush, but still...Romans.
Let's say $9-$12? Add an extra $1 if you will try multiplayer. Briefly.

Sigh - this game should be so much more than what it is. The developers clearly worked hard on important areas such as visuals and sound, but then completely dropped the ball when it came to gameplay and longevity.
The graphics are lush. If your machine can handle it, you'll be treated to some spectacular eye-candy. Level design is also impressive, plenty of detail in the environment making it very immersive - It really is top notch stuff and you'll want to spend time just taking it all in. The game really delivers in this area.
Gameplay on the other hand is where Ryse: Son of Rome falls massively short. Once you've gotten used to the clunky combat system ( which btw, is a blatent rip of the recent Batman games, but nowhere near as polished or satisfying) you've pretty much won the day. Your enemies from start to finish will be repetitive and identical in every way bar their looks. LEFT CLICK, RIGHT CLICK, LEFT CLICK, LEFT CLICK to destroy them all - four at a time. The AI in Ryse is pretty shocking, at best. By far the best the combat system has to offer is the execution mode, where you've sufficiently knocked enough sh*t out of a Barbarian to press E, and with two or three well timed mouse-clicks finish the poor furry-thong wearing peasant in a gory fashion. Depending how well you clicked your mouse, this will either up your health, XP, damage capability or 'focus' - whichever you have selected at the time. You're forever on a one-path mission, you'll forego seeing a lot of envionment detail because the game wants you to walk straight past it all.  Easy, frustrating and ultimately boring.
Even with the long, numerous yet pretty cut scenes, the game has no longevity at all. You'll complete it in under ten hours, even if you're slow and die a lot. That, to me, is unforgivable given the game is still retailing at £35, though it brought an end to the boredom. There are other points I should probably pick up on, but I can't be arsed, so allow me to summarise;
Graphics - 9/10
Environment - 8/10
Sound - 8/10
Storyline - 6/10
Gameplay - 4/10
Longevity - 5/10
Overall I'd score Ryse: Son of Rome, a disappointing 6/10 - the game has some fantastic assets, but is ultimately let down by sloppy development.

This is by no means a great game, but it is a great spectacle. Impressive visuals, glorious executions, and all for the glory of Rome. The plot is one that is enjoyable, though fairly simple, and the combat, though also simple and painfully color coded is still fun especially when you get your juices flowing... juices being the blood of all your dismembered enemies. The combat is similar to the Batman/AssCreed style of games, except dumbed down significantly. You start the game with four buttons and by the gods you will end the game with those four buttons while getting some minor upgrades (mostly to combat stats like health) over the coarse of the game.
The bads of the game are short, that is, the game is relatively short even by most modern game standards, but does not feel rushed which is a nice but I still wouldn't have minded a little additional fleshing out. The other major issue is the rather dull boss battles which all consist of essentially rolling out of the way of a slow big attack and then counter 2-4 faster smaller attacks then executing a properly timed parry on the final attack to get in about two attacks. This process is repeated about 10-20 times per boss, depending on the boss making them more of obstacles of your patience than your gaming skill.
All in all still an enjoyable game for those who are fond of Roman things like pillums and shields and the Colloseum and killing axe weilding barbarians. I recomend you get it, but I recomend you get it on sale.
Overall Rating: 8.5/10

Victoria II is the most interesting and addicting grand strategy game that I've ever played hands down. It covers every aspect of the era. Currently as I'm writing this review I have 536 hours in Victoria II and I only plan to see that number go higher as I continue to play this amazing game.

From the start of Rise and Shine you're greeted with an amazingly beautiful hellish landscape in which our titular hero Rise (who is 10 by the way) has to fight his way out of his wartorn home armed with a talking gun and a whole lot of respawns. Moments after he's greeted by a Space Invaders-esque alien who tries to act as a diversion only to be brutally gunned down, a giant robot flying in threatening to annihilate our protagonist. Despite this being a dramatic moment, Rise's home is a place known as Gamearth where pretty much every video game trope applies so the Space Invaders Red Shirt dies in a pixelated mess, a bunch of birds (and a flappy bird) fly from the background, and some text saying that the giant mecha is level 999 which sets the mood perfectly. Rise and Shine is completely straightfaced while simultaneously loaded with (really obvious) sight gags and small asides along the way. It works, though whether or not you get a laugh out of it could vary.
In any case, Rise and Shine is beautiful, very beautiful. Animations and sprites are robust as are the scenaries around you. As you blow robots and space marine faces to bits, it all looks stunning. There's very little repetition and things keep moving forward with a combination of action puzzles and action action. The developers do a great job keeping the game fresh enough and speeding things along to the conclusion so you don't feel like you're doing the same thing the whole game. Which brings up another point, the climactic battle with the mecha occurs in the first third of the game, roughly twenty minutes in. Meaning that when I say speeding things along, I mean speeding things along. You'll fight hard, die again and again, and then you'll be at the end very suddenly. And in a sad way, it seems to just accelerate too fast making the end feel like an anticlimax. Not that there isn't a climax, the final boss is pretty grand, it's just you'll reach the end, things will feel off, like things were rushed, and then that'll be it. It's over and some things just won't feel as resolved as they should be.
In any case, is Rise and Shine good? Oh certainly, it's fun, a joy to watch, and keeps moving forward with itself while sticking to run and gun action. Is it a game I can recommend at full price? Well, the game oozes style and effort and that's certainly deserving of its current price, but I can imagine that if you're looking for just gameplay there's very little replayability other than a Deathless run and some secrets which can then make it pretty diffcult to justify a high recommendation. Still, if you're looking for a bit of a challenge and some great hand drawn art, you've got a nice game in Rise and Shine.

Rise & Shine has a good look, funny albeit cliched story, okay humor and interesting gamplay ideas.  Its downfall comes from issues with input.  It's mixes twin-stick and cover shooting.  I would say this is ill-advised but whatever.  It requires you to use its various twinstick elements to fight off enmies and avoid the one-hit kills.  Think Super Meat Boy except instead of traversing difficult stages, you're taking out groups of enemies or firing at targets.  However, having to draw your weapon, aim then fire with twin-stick controls in a twitch scenario is not.... good.  Add to that the controls are often unresponsive, with the aim trigger (R) pulling out but not fast enough and you cannot begin firing until it's out.  Often, the gaps in between bullet barrages while under cover do not even last long enough for you to get your gun out to fire.  You can SHOOT the enemies bullets but you have a limited clip, meaning you have to go back under cover to reload your gun, Shine, then start the whole process over again.  I often found it much better to just engage the targets directly and take them down fast.  However, there are also other enemies who react to you not being under cover by flying over to you and giving you an undodgable 1-hit-kill as if to punish you for not playing the game the way the devs intended.  I have beel playing shooters since the mid-80's.  I've played good ones; I've played really, REALLY bad ones; But rarely have I played a shooter that has such BAFFLING choices as this one in its design.  Maybe some other players will have better luck with controller responsiveness, but not I.  I tried it using Mouse and Keyboard (I hate M&K for platforming shooters), an X-Box 360 Hori Pad and a standard XBox One controller and all of them felt WRONG.
I cannot recommend this game based on my own experiences.

Billy Blazcowicz takes his grandfather's approach to interacting with Nazis, and applies said approach to the entire universe.
-Episodes 4 and 5 hold up extremely well to this day.  The platforming is silky smooth, the areas varied and colorful, and the pogo stick allows for some creative approaches to completing levels.  Secret of the Oracle and the Armaggedon Machine are just flat out fun, and are worth the $5.00 alone that this pack costs.
-Episodes 1-3 have aged a bit less gracefully, but personally I love these games.  Episode 1 was the first game I ever played, and really got me into the world of id software (and pc games in general).  Keep in mind too that the engine powering these games was revolutionary at the time, with these being the first legitimate sidescrollers available on the pc (John Carmack kicking♥♥♥♥♥with engine design before the Wolfensteins, Dooms, and Quakes came along).  Think of these as a nice bonus to the still excellent gameplay found in episodes 4 and 5.
Anyway, this pack is certainly worth its $5.00 price tag.  Romero's creativity and excellent design sense, combined with Carmack's engine work made for some great games back then, and its nice to see how well these hold up to this day.

One of the first games I've ever played was Commander Keen. We only had the first and fourth episodes of the game and the two were the first games I remember beating by myself. Thanks to Steam,  was able to get the the other episodes, except for episode six which I have no idea where to get. I was gonna talk about both Vorticon and Galaxy games, but they are pretty different so I'll talk about the first series first.
Story
You play as Billy Blaze, an 8-year old boy, who is your normal super genius of an IQ of 314 by day, but when he's parents are gone and his babysitter is asleep, he becomes Commander Keen. As he tests out his new rocket ship (that he made himself out of scrap) he goes to Mars and explores. He gets back to his ship all the important parts are gone and he go look for them starting his first real adventure.
While the plot is simple, it does set up the world the game takes in, and there's a good bit of lore in the help menu, like the us accidentally killing the Yorps treating human toys as relics. I also really like the idea of the villain. I won't talk about till I review the next game but I'll say he's one of the most evil, insane people I've seen.
Gameplay
Standard platformer stuff. It was one of the first platformers on DOS that had actually side scrolling so that's interesting. There's also a pogo stick which you can find and keep which lets you jump higher. I must also mention that while you do have an option to fight, you don't have to. If you know what your doing, you can get through episode 1 without killing any of the boss enemies(Except for the last but that's unavoidable).
I do have two nitpicks, the first involves using your gun: You have a limited ammo which isn't too bad, but to use it you have to press the buttons for jumping and the pogo stick at the same time. While this isn't to bad for most fights, the final boss may be a problem as you have to jump to get at his obvious weakpoints. The second is that you are killing people. I don't mean evil aliens I mean people. Even babies. I even saw one enemy type with blood coming  out of him when he died. Really makes the game more brutal than it needs to be.
Presentation
Being a dos game before proper sound and music was used, the sound effects are not good. Some are very painful to listen and are constant. I ended up turning the sound off after a while. The art is a different story. While the design in episode 1may seem bland, playing 2 and 3 really make it stand out a bit more and helps with the world building. Epi. 1 is very simple and basic, with lots of red and a grey or black background with different colored blocks  scattered around. 2 has a more detail background and is more blue. 3 has a lot of color with blue skies, pink wallpaper, green grass with brown dirt and lots of grey when in a militarily building.
Verdict
While it hasn't aged well in some parts, it's still a fun game which I would recommended to anyone interested in platformers
8/10
(Goodbye Galaxy)
Part two of the trilogy that was never finished.
Story
Some time after the defeat of the Grand Intellect, Billy is working on a radio to get messages from space. During his testing, he intercepts a transmission from the Shikadi, who plan to destroy the galaxy for the Gannalech. He goes to see the oracle but a page informs him that the ones who operate it have been kidnapped and imprisoned to the Shadowlands. Commander Keen goes to these lands to find the council members and stop the Shikadi.  Another straight forward story. There's a bit more humor in it  and Keen has more of a personalty being someone likes to save the day, tries to avoid being in trouble and gets annoyed when people get his name wrong.
Gameplay
Gameplay is the same for the most part with a few tweaks such using door and grabbing ledges. There's a bigger emphasis in fighting enemies this time with deadly enemies, but it's okay as Keen has made a stun gun so you not on a killing spree. Of course this doesn't apply of bugs. The levels are also longer and harder but you can save in levels, which make this one of the first games I know which made lives completely useless. Also there's pong.
Presentation
Sounds improved. it's a lot softer and less grating. and there's music and it's pretty good. Art is also better with more detailed scenery and all the different creature you meet.
Verdict
I couldn't get episode 6 so the series end here for me. It's a good game that was unfortunately ended too soon.
9/10

Let's have a look on one of Capcons most action loaded games Devil May Cry 3 : Dantes Awakening Special Edition for the PC.
Platform: PC
Publisher: Ubisoft
Developer: Capcom
Genre: Fantasy Action Adventure
Release Date: Oct 16, 2006
Story: The story so far plays earlier than the orginal Devil May Cry game for the PS2. Its's about the half devil Dante Sparda who tries once again to save the world from the influence of the devil possesed Arkham
and his horde of undead creatures from hell. In this game there is also some very cool new character introduced named Vergil Sparda who is actually Dantes evil twinbrother and most fearsome foe.
Virgil works together with Arkham in order to open the gate of hell which was closed long years ago by Dantes father the legandary Devil Knight Sparda. So Dante starts his journey to climb up the unholy tower of evil called "The Temen-Ni-Gru" which is summoned by Arkham in order to connect the human world to the demon world. On his way up he crosses lines with a strange woman called Lady who tries to shoot him on sight.
The whereabouts of the Temen-Ni-Gru as well as the identity of lady seem very dark and unclear. What the end offers... i can't tell, just play to find out :D 8/10
Gameplay: DMC3-Se is a third perspective fantasy action adventure which combines very fast gameplay with lots of combos and various puzzles throughout the game. The fighting system is devided in "styles" which
Dante can switch between Missions and also level them up to perform even greater combos. There are also special obiects called orbs to collect as well as a very great varaety of fire and melee weapons throughout the game. 8/10
Controls: This is one of the main problems with the PC version of DMC3-Se because its totally bugged and you need a patch in order to convert the right keyboard comands to some gamepad. 4/10
Graphic: This is unfortunately another minus for the PC port as you will see some graphics in ingame arent drawn very correctly as the PS2 version and also some parts of the game seem pretty greyscale due to the direct X output of your PC, nevertheless the FMV movies are really great. 7/10
Sound: I have to mention that the sound is absoluty awesome. DMC3-Se brings some very good soundtrack and very nice soundsamples combined with very thrilling metal music. 9/10
My Review: First of all I have to say that I have played only the PC version of DMC3-Se hench I am writting this review for the PC version of that great game.
The game starts right of in Dantes office with one of the most impressive and action loaded FMV movies I saw so far. After the nice introducing of the control tutorial you are directly thrown into action to kick some demon butts. You will learn very fast the combos and special attacks if you play the first time through this game. Actually you can change between 4 styles called Trickster, Gunslinger, Royal Guard and Swordmaster. As the names describe, each style is bound to some very cool and unique special attack and combos. For example if you like using long range weapons than you can choose Gunslinger for improving your shoot abillities but if you prefer short range you can go along with Swordmaster. All in one I really liked the style system and the idea of combining different styles. So after you have killed tons of demons and alot of other evil guys you will be introduced step by step through very cool FMV movies to the story of this game which is in my opinion really great. The game is divided in 20 Missions, and you will come across some very cool and though bosses, one remarcable of them will be Dantes twinbrother Virgil who actually seems to interfere with Dante on purpose. The boss fights are one big plus in this game because they really deliever some thrilling and decent difficulty (at least if you play on very hard or Dante must die mode). What I really liked about this game is the character developement its really different from DMC2 which was... to put it bluntly "it sucked". I would generally say that the difficulty in this game is fair and really depends on what scale you play. I beat this game on hard mode in 9 hours but some other guys sure need between 15 - 20 hours. Also after beating the entire game you can unlock Vergil as a playable character, and this is included in the Special edition only as well as some other nice feature I will mention beneath.
So what are the differences between the original Devil May Cry 3 : Dantes Awakening and Devil May Cry 3 : Dantes Awakening Special Edition you may ask ?
Well here they are:
Difficulties:
- Easy mode
- Hard mode
- Very Hard mode
- Dante Must Die mode
- Heaven or Hell mode
Playable Character:
- "Vergil" is playable after beating the game once with Dante. He brings his own uniqe styles as well as flying swords as his long range weapons.
Extra Mode:
- "Bloody Palace" is available after beating the game once with Dante, its some kind of battle arena where you are thrown in with a limited supply of orbs and must fight random enemies and bosses.
Extra Outfits:
- 4 new costumes for Vergil unlockable
- 6 new outfits for Dante unlockable
Gallery:
-you can unlock diverse Artwork and CGI work form DMC3 here
Demo Digest:
- You can preview all Ingame Movies from here
- There is also some timelimit in the end of the game where you can beat 100 enemies in order to unlock a hidden ending
Miscellaneous:
- There are different locations in the game where you know can fight Jester (its that annoying clown BTW)
- Lady wears some fency new suit depending on the outfit you choose in Ingame
- There is a yellow and gold option at the beginning of the game which allows to use the yellow orbs as restore point after dieing.
These are the differences available in the Special Edition of DMC3 as well for the PS2 version as for the PC version which was only released as the Special edition by the way.
FInal Words: DMC3 SE sure is some special game for fans of the Devil May Cry series as well as for action fans who like fast and flashy gamplay combined with metal music and gothic ambience. I was very pleased about the importation of this game to the PC and really forgot fast about the undeveloped control settings which is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥indeed for people who wants to play the PC version on a gamepad. All I can say is that you should stick with the PS2 version if you are a die hard fan of DMC as for me I also liked the PC version therefore I give this game a 7 out of 10.
Endrating: 7/10

Bias:  I have played quite a bit of regular ole Ark, and I like it just fine.
So as of this review, I've been in 2 matches so far.
Which brings me to my first problem:  The lobbies.  A free-for-all needs 25 players for a ranked match, and even when 25 players were in the lobby, many times, the game failed to start.  I would have played more, had the lobbies functioned a little better.  I also suspect that some people are abusing the finickyness of the lobby system to disrupt normal gameplay.
Once you get in a game, you are placed in a giant bubble in the sky, where you can talk smack, plan your plans, or otherwise occupy your time.  It is important that you make your character, make your tribe, and possibly your flag, as soon as you can.  Press L to form a tribe, by the way, for those who don't know.  I am hoping that the devs can get this whole rigamarole straight, as it's probably driving people away from the game.  Perhaps an out-of-game way to craft your character, flag, and set up a 'quick tribe' to use once you get in a match?
After a period of time, you are descended to the playfield via a beam, where you are free to run amok.  In my first match, I mostly played stealth and lasted quite a while, until I encountered a man taming a trike.  I felt good during the fight, like I was winning, but the trike woke up and he whistled it onto me, and I died, caught between a trike and a hard place.
Second match, I stealthed to an area with several good specimens of beast, and tamed myself an ape.  With that ape, I then went ape, killing 3 other players.  The fourth player was able to mount his anky and overcome my element of surprise, and his trike and stego ended up finishing me off.  I was close, though.
That is all pretty good.
I recommend this game with the expectation that it will improve over time.  Ark was nearly unplayable when it came out, due to FPS issues, and now, even on my modest old computer that most would be embarrassed to own, I can play it at 40 FPS.   Ark: SOTF does run a bit poorer than that, but with a little tweaking, it ran well enough for me to score numerous kills and make numerous direct hits with bows, spears, and slingshots.
Some people will be surprised at the suddenness with which one can die, but I enjoy that aspect, as even a guy on a rex can be killed by bugs when he stops to drink or loot a fallen enemy.
I haven't tried the tech path of play yet, but it suspect it's risky until the end, when it all pays off.  4-5 combatants I've faced were hidden, attempting to make guns and armor to counteract dinosaur mount power.  At least 2 of them made it farther than me.
Which brings to another point:  When you die, you are immediately ejected from the game into the menu.  I appreciate why spectating is a bad idea, but at least having a scoreboard to see who won a match would be nice.
In the lobbies, you can see your own simplified stats, but I can't figure out a way to vew other people's stats.   Related to the above point, it would be nice to know who you were up against, as well.  Maybe something to note how often a person has killed using their mount, vs melee weapons, vs ranged weapons, etc.  I would like to know if a player in a match is an axe murderer or if they want to skulk in the shrubs waiting to bushwack the 2nd to last tired competitor with a shotgun to the face.
In a nutshell:
This is a game that is still in development.  It has some problems that may be game breaking for some.  It is based off of Ark:  Survival Evolved, and has most of the elements of that game, including crafting and heavy inventory management, so it has a learning curve.  It demands a lot of your system, and may not play at framerates that some are used to.  It is frustrating not being able to get into a game from the lobby.
That being said, it has a lot of potential, was fun for the 2 matches I've played, and it has freaking dinosaur shotgun giant ape cannibal with a spear fights.

The amount of negativity this game has accumulated is crazy. I'm not going to stand here and tell you guys it is super innovative or ground-breaking stuff but it appears some people have forgotten a simple fact. Football Manager 2017 is still the best football management simulator out there by a country mile. If what you want is a well built management game, I don't see too many issues with this.
I suppose I'll quickly get the problems I do agree with out of the way first. The price is too high considering how little innovation there is. £34.99 is asking a lot when the game is not all that different from FM16. Add the extra £3.99 for the in game editor too and it has to be said, S.I might be pushing their luck a little. On top of this I will also concede that the game needs refining in places. There's silly little things which should just not be a problem which are. For example, if you sign a player who can't get a work permit and then try to loan him out, it's not uncommon for the player to then complain that they feel they are too good to be loaned out. Clearly in this case you should be able to talk to the player and explain to him that he needs to get a work permit elsewhere. However, this is a little bug which can be irritating at worst. It does not destroy the experience although I will admit I also feel it's something that S.I should patch ASAP (which I suspect they won't).
With that out of the way, let's address the two things I'm sick of reading. FIrst of all, being bad at the game does not make the game bad. The amount of times I've read 'I CONCEDED IN THE 90TH MINUTE AFTER DOMINATING THE GAME THIS SUX WTF' is ridiculous. That happens in football, you know? Look at Burnley vs Liverpool this season. Liverpool were the better team in every description and yet Burnley took a 2-0 win. It's frustrating but not unrealistic necessarily. Also, if this is happening every game it's probably a tactical fault. Drop off, update your player instructions. If you're just sitting there then what do expect? No game is won by not doing anything. The second big thing is that people claim the game engine is identical to last year. I can't say I agree. I've seen a huge range of new goal types such as players actually bothering to pass across the box which just weren't present previously (at least not often anyway). Sure, players do stupid stuff from time to time but that's simply replicating real life. Only a few games ago I had my keeper miss hit a long kick straight to their striker for an open goal. Is that BS that hasn't been improved from last year? No, it's a individual error that can happen to anyone. Green's OG in the World Cup? Gerrard's slip? Terry's penalty? Errors happen and the game represents this well. Just because it gets you angry doesn't mean FM's doing anything wrong.
All in all then I'd say this. Should you buy this for £34.99? Only if you're a huge fan of RECENT TITLES. I say recent titles because it's very similar to them but not at all like games from years back. For the average guy I'd say wait for a sale which drops it down to at least £24.99 or lower. It's still a fun game which does a competent job of simulating football management as a whole. It can be a little complicated and it certainly isn't for everyone, but I still believe FM17 is a fair game at the very least.

Sigh - this game should be so much more than what it is. The developers clearly worked hard on important areas such as visuals and sound, but then completely dropped the ball when it came to gameplay and longevity.
The graphics are lush. If your machine can handle it, you'll be treated to some spectacular eye-candy. Level design is also impressive, plenty of detail in the environment making it very immersive - It really is top notch stuff and you'll want to spend time just taking it all in. The game really delivers in this area.
Gameplay on the other hand is where Ryse: Son of Rome falls massively short. Once you've gotten used to the clunky combat system ( which btw, is a blatent rip of the recent Batman games, but nowhere near as polished or satisfying) you've pretty much won the day. Your enemies from start to finish will be repetitive and identical in every way bar their looks. LEFT CLICK, RIGHT CLICK, LEFT CLICK, LEFT CLICK to destroy them all - four at a time. The AI in Ryse is pretty shocking, at best. By far the best the combat system has to offer is the execution mode, where you've sufficiently knocked enough sh*t out of a Barbarian to press E, and with two or three well timed mouse-clicks finish the poor furry-thong wearing peasant in a gory fashion. Depending how well you clicked your mouse, this will either up your health, XP, damage capability or 'focus' - whichever you have selected at the time. You're forever on a one-path mission, you'll forego seeing a lot of envionment detail because the game wants you to walk straight past it all.  Easy, frustrating and ultimately boring.
Even with the long, numerous yet pretty cut scenes, the game has no longevity at all. You'll complete it in under ten hours, even if you're slow and die a lot. That, to me, is unforgivable given the game is still retailing at £35, though it brought an end to the boredom. There are other points I should probably pick up on, but I can't be arsed, so allow me to summarise;
Graphics - 9/10
Environment - 8/10
Sound - 8/10
Storyline - 6/10
Gameplay - 4/10
Longevity - 5/10
Overall I'd score Ryse: Son of Rome, a disappointing 6/10 - the game has some fantastic assets, but is ultimately let down by sloppy development.

This is by no means a great game, but it is a great spectacle. Impressive visuals, glorious executions, and all for the glory of Rome. The plot is one that is enjoyable, though fairly simple, and the combat, though also simple and painfully color coded is still fun especially when you get your juices flowing... juices being the blood of all your dismembered enemies. The combat is similar to the Batman/AssCreed style of games, except dumbed down significantly. You start the game with four buttons and by the gods you will end the game with those four buttons while getting some minor upgrades (mostly to combat stats like health) over the coarse of the game.
The bads of the game are short, that is, the game is relatively short even by most modern game standards, but does not feel rushed which is a nice but I still wouldn't have minded a little additional fleshing out. The other major issue is the rather dull boss battles which all consist of essentially rolling out of the way of a slow big attack and then counter 2-4 faster smaller attacks then executing a properly timed parry on the final attack to get in about two attacks. This process is repeated about 10-20 times per boss, depending on the boss making them more of obstacles of your patience than your gaming skill.
All in all still an enjoyable game for those who are fond of Roman things like pillums and shields and the Colloseum and killing axe weilding barbarians. I recomend you get it, but I recomend you get it on sale.
Overall Rating: 8.5/10

I've had my eye on this game ever since I saw it land on Steam. I'm a huge history buff and the chance to play a Roman era "God of War" style game really appealed to me. It finally went on sale a week or two ago and I snapped it up for $20.
At first glance, this game is gorgeous. It was a PS4 launch title, so you can definitely tell that a ton of effort went into the art and graphics. It uses the Crytek engine, so foilage and lighting look amazing. The armor, characters and props all  look great. The scenery of the levels is also great. There is a huge variety of levels as well. From Rome to London to forests and "Normandy" style beach landings. The only real downside to the levels is their linearity. You walk a set path with all typical debris and objects blocking your way, forcing you to follow their course. Occassionaly they allow you to wonder a little bit, but in the end you're still going to end up where they want you to.
The story is so-so. The dialogue is great and the cut scenes are all done with in game models and textures so they look awesome. BUT, the story does just break down to a revenge story which is fairly simple to follow (and predict).
The combat is surprisingly simple too. I use a mouse and keyboard to control, and combat literally breaks down to left click, left click, left click, right click, press "e" to execute enemy. The combat changes a little based on the type of enemy you fight. Sometimes you have to do more right clicking. There are really only like 5 or so enemy types, not counting bosses (which are really just bigger versions of normal enemies). There aren't combos or moves to do, it simply devolves to breaking their block, then hitting them with the sword. In my honest opinion, I think the combat is the biggest miss in the game.
Character models are also kind of spotty. The main character and other NPCs look great. I really can't say enough about them. Their armor, weapons, design and faces all look amazing. They really do stay true to Roman armor and achitecture. They exaggerate a few things, but all in all it's very good. The biggest miss in the art department is the enemy character models. They look good for the first 15 minutes, but they look the same for the rest of the game. There are maybe a dozen barbarian enemy models and they get old fast. You do eventually run across some other enemy models, but they're just reskins of the original barbarian you first encountered. There are no weapon choices for the main character either. You get one gladius and one shield. There are pilums (a throwing spear) to find once in awhile, but when you do find them they are for a specific reason. The armor and weapons look so good, it's pretty dissapointing that you can't customize or choose different pieces of equipment at all.
There is a multiplayer option, but I didn't even get a fair chance after I realized that you have the option of purchasing different equipment with real money. It's not so bad as to call it "Pay to Win", but it's still a big turn off for me. Besides, the multiplayer is just gladiator style matchups. With combat being so simple, it comes down to who just has better timing with their strikes.
I would still give this game a 7/10. If they had expanded on the combat a bit more and added a little more variety to the enemies and bosses, this would really be a fantastic game. Get it for $20 or under if you can.

Ryse is a decent game, but as a launch title for a console (Xbox One) it's actually really good. Launch title games usually wear their polish (or lack there of) on their sleeve, and while Ryse definitely has its share of small oddities that happen while you play the game, it's honestly really well made considering
If you took the setting of God of War (the Roman empire) and took the combat from the Batman game Arkham City, you basically get Ryse. Lots of action and an incredible amount of violence. Do you like fighting? Good because THAT is 90% of the game. Once in a while you will get a break to do certain barrier shield parts where you and your team huddle together and move together and block arrows (I really liked these parts) and other times you'll get to shoot the scorpion (basically a ounted crossbow) but you're mainly fighting!
Ryse is a not spectacular game at a once $60 price tag as it's a shorter single player game (6 or so hours), it's tough to find people to play with online and the story isn't really going to bring you back for more but as I bought the game for $10, it was WELL worth it.
The game looks beautiful, but make sure you bring your most outstanding rig. Mine is a few years old and while parts of the game looked amazing, it chugged at some parts and normally I don't see that kind of thing happen. This is a Crytek game though so keep that in mind. I also had some texture issues once in a while, Texture pop in and such did happen for me, but it still looked lovely.
Also, the combat can some times be a little confusing and it gets a little old by the end of the game. Some times you're not sure who you're hitting and that can get a little irritating when you're trying to pull off a move on one guy, only to hit another ones shield and lose your combo. However, the executions are pretty satisfying.
That's really all I have to say about Ryse. It's a better than average game, and it's beatiful. Check it out when it's cheaper and you won't be disappointed!

When you have gathered your info, you can return to diplomacy and the offer will still be there.
The developers give good support and respond to threads reporting bugs on the Amplititude website. Endless Legend is easily the best turn based game of the genre since Civilization 4 & 5.
My only critism is the way the save system works. It is clear loading a save game causes the AI to behave differently than if you had played straight through. For example, the AI is meant to respond in  real time to your actions, but generally does not. However, loading a save game will give the AI the opportunity to move upon load, which can significantly disadvantage a player who relies on multiple short gaming sessions.

Great game - with caveats.
It's times like this I wish Steam had a more granular recommendation option, because there really is a lot to like about this game. It's gorgeous, the art design is amazing, the playable factions are unique and interesting and the music is also great. The beginning game is a lot of fun (if somewhat daunting for newbies), but the game starts to bog down in the late game. The problem is that the challenges don't scale as you level up, so combat becomes inconsequential, and the game goes from being a fun turn based strategy game into an excruciatingly boring "resource management" chore.
Master of Magic struck the right balance, with high level enemies and challenges to keep the player engaged. Once you've reached a high enough level in Endless Legend, there is little reason to move your armies around the map, and the game devolves into just allocating your city populations between resource priorities.
Still a very good game, if you love spreadsheets.

I'm not gonna lie, this game probably isn't worth $15, but I'm not gonna just not recommend it because of that. Sure, its a pretty short game, but I finished it and felt pretty good about having spent my money on it. The game will likely take you between 2 and 3 hours to beat, which isn't very long at all, but I enjoyed my experience with the game. The story of the game is very simple. You play as a kid named Rise, you end up getting a gun named Shine, and then have to save the planet of Gamearth. All of the characters seem very aware of the fact that they are in a game and the game is constantly referencing cliches in games. The puzzles and bosses can both be decently frustrating at first, but once you figure out what you have to do, it becomes pretty easy. You will end up dying, most likely a lot, and that is actually essential to get past certain parts of the game, which took me a while to realize. It has some pretty interesting ideas, and felt pretty good to play. Overall, I recommend the game. If the price seems a little steep to you, maybe wait until it goes on a pretty good sale, like down to $5.
Also, the game has great music, and I would love to be able to get the soundtrack for the game. If the developers see this, would you guys consider selling the soundtrack for this game? I'd love to buy it to listen to it.

Commander Keen Complete Pack is a DOS platformer from the 1990's by Apogee Software
. While the game is very much focused on being an arcade platformer game, the designers included a story explaining what was going on within the game... Interested? Read on.
Billy Blaze is your standard 8 year old boy, by standard we mean he making his own unraveling adventure in space, starting off with fighting the Vorticons and saving planet earth, then receiving news of a new threat to the Galaxy Keen rushes off to consult the Keepers of the Oracle.
It is worth noting for die-hard-Commander-Keen Fans, that not
games are present: 1 Marooned on Mars. 2 The Earth Explodes. 3 Keen Must Die! 4 Secrets of the Oracle. 5 The Armageddon Machine. are available in the Commander Keen Complete Pack.
It has already been established that the Commander Keen Complete Pack is a platformer, but in addition to standard movement controls you have a laser gun, and a Pogo Stick (being the signature item of the franchise). You can jump, and the Pogo stick gives you even higher jumps. When I was little, no one in my family knew what this game was called. So we called lovingly called it "Pogo"!
In Addition to the movement features of the game, there are various "accessory" items that help you unlock different levels, or unlock doors within a level. While in many of the games there are levels and extra's you can skip over, trying to track down all the secrets in these games really increases it's replay-ability. (Hey, keep in mind this is a DOS game developed in the 1990's, the fact that this type of game is still fun to play is pretty impressive)
There are no achievements in the Commander Keen games, however there are High Scores. As with very old classic Arcade games; you would try to get the highest score and then put in perverted messages to the poor souls who never had the mad skills you did.
The Commander Keen Complete Pack is priced at $4.99, if you sit down and actually play the game you can easily get more then 4 hours worth of game play, the games have a really nice combination of difficulty, exploration, platforming and secret area's.
Graphics is a NEW category that I'm adding exclusively for this particular review. I don't personally care about graphics in video games, I feel that bad mechanics (or Game Play) speak stronger then if you're seeing every poly in the character. But I want to emphasis that this is an old game, so if you do intend to get it without having any internal motivation, keep in mind this is a game LOOKS, SOUNDS, and often times FEELS old.
Nostalgia is a NEW category that I'm adding exclusively for this particular review. I think it's pretty safe to say that 90% of the people who have played and/or reviewed this game are all motivated by the same thing: This is a game of our past. For me personally this was the first PC Game *I ever played*. Nearly the first game in general, but Super Mario Land for the Gameboy takes first place.
If you want to take a step back and know what type of game I was playing when I was a little kid, go ahead and buy this game, then let me know what you thought about it!
Do I recommend... or not recommend... that is the question. Most people will pass up this game, and that's fine. It probably only appeals to gamers who enjoy Platformers, or those of us who played this game when we were little.
I am going to recommend this game to people who enjoy platformers, specifically Commander Keen 4 "Secrets of the Oracle", the earlier games are more of a novelty, while still often times difficult, I personally preferred Commander Keen 4 and 5, to the original Trilogy.

I can't recommend Only If highly enough to be honest. Combine the thrill you got when you first played the portal series with the highly detailed environment of most of the latest games on the market. I'm going to try and give you a nice easy list of pros and cons to help you decide whether to download this game. And even though i love the game so much, i'll remain as unbiased as i can >:D I understand that no-one wants to really read a novel for a review, so if you quickly want to find out whether its worth it, just read the dot-point titles under each category - that should give you an idea.
-Plot > The plot for Only If really grabs you from the start. It's quite the mystery, and im not quite sure why its been tagged horror, but it certainly does have some thriller/suspense elements to it. If i try and give you an idea to the plot, it will all end up being spoilers, so you'll just have to gve it a shot. It can get really intense at times
, and you have to make sure you know the environment around you if you want to stay alive.
-Environment > The graphics in the game are equivalent to most high end paid games. There is an incredible amount of detail to the world, and you'll find yourself admiring it from the very start. Trust me. They're pretty good.
-Puzzles > There is no doubt you'll find yourself wandering about trying to figure out what on Earth is going on. My only advice is that you listen very carefully to what Vinnie is saying (the man on the radio - its...er...hard to explain). Often the puzzles come in the form of riddles, and they determine how you complete each level. Once again, people complain about not clearly knowing what to do. My response: its a PUZZLE game - that's whats meant to happen :D. Often, Vinnie will have said something that points to an object in the environment you need to interact with in a particular way. Another bit of advice, when a question is asked, you may have to TYPE out your response. As another reviewer said before - when people got stuck in portal levels, noone complained there. (Shout-out to whoever that was). You'll enjoy them, trust me :)
-Achievements > There are a few easter eggs thrown about the game, as well as some pretty funny achievements. If that's your cup of tea, you'll like this. Granted, there aren't many of them, but I guess the fact that some are so darn hard to get makes up for it.
-Voice Acting > I liked the script, and the tonations of the voices. It was clever. Some people don't agree. Up to you to decide...
-Ending > That ending....oh my..... :') Remember not to just turn off the game the moment the credits turn up - you are NOT finished....
-Price > Or lack thereof. Come on people, its freeeeeeee! Just give it a shot. If you feel you wasted a few hours of your life, feel free to leave a comment here and complain about it. I promise to probably not read it ;) But yeah, just do it. It's a decent game for $0. It would still be worth it at around $10-$15+ dollars quite frankly.
-Vulgarity > Ok, so there is gratuitous swearing and many references. There is a lot of it. It is everywhere. I really don't recommend this for someone who's under the age of, i dunno, whatever age at which this would be inappropriate. You'll need to be fairly mature. You have been warned.
-Audio >  I found that at some points, the audio volume level would vary.Now this is fairly minor in terms of cons. But you might need to keep fiddling with your volume control at various points so that it doesn't get too soft/loud at times. But really, that should be fine.
-Instructionals > At certain points, you will learn new skills, such as the ability to pick things up, etc. The instruction for this (press ... to do ...) pops up in the middle of the screen in small letters. Now generally you will catch it, but if you're not ready for it, and you miss it - you will have a particularly hard time finishing the level. This only happened in one instance for me (which was the picking up things i mentioned earlier), but i simply went back to the last checkpoint, and then everything was fine.
-Ending > I can see how people might miss the actual ending because the credits show up. So, word of advice. Wait...
So, there you are. Make your own decision, but know that this really is a game worth playing, even if you don't like this sort of thing. Give it a shot. You've got nothing to lose. It's not even that big of a download from memory, so it won't take long to uninstall if you are dissapointed. Have fun!

Cobalt is a pretty great 2D Platformer with a solid storyline. I like the odd mosnters and NPC's like random pterodactyl birds and mushroom men, mixed with a bunch of mysterious Android dudes. The game works great with my Xbox 360 controller plugged into my PC, and I'd recommend trying it out. :)

I've been playing the alpha for years and if it wasn't for those gray out buttons in the main menu, I'd have said it was a finished game aleady... and boy, that release is good.
The gameplay is (and always was) super tight with a lot of depth. It's easy to learn but hard to master (you can punch grenades to send them back, well-timed rolls can deflect shots, there is a weird and awesome bulletime system in place...). Which makes this game super fun in local versus. It's a must have if you have friends coming over, like super smash bros on consoles.
Each match can be customized like crazy (which robot you're playing, stage music, available weapons,...)
I didn't play much with the solo modes yet but so far I like what I see. The story seems fun and humorous and you can upgrade/customize your character, which is something I didn't expect at all (it kinda give an RPG feel to the game). There also seem to hav a lot of little interactivity thingy which I really like (you can mount certain creatures, get a bird and see it dies by a rocket 5 seconds after,...)
I tried some of the challenges and that seems to be fun, there is a leaderboard so you can compare your score to other players and try to be the best (carefull, it's addictive as hell since a challenge doesn't take more than 30 seconds) ;)
The sound design is amazing, musics are nice and you won't believe how much diversity the devs could offer you with "blip", "bloup" and "biip" sounds.
Apparently you can unlock things, which I always appreciate.
So... well done devs. Your game was amazing 5 years ago, and you managed to make it even better now :)

First Impressions Video:
Cobalt surprised me.  I came in expecting another side scrolling shooter and found a much more intricate and complex design with some real character to it.  The graphical design is stylized and matched by ambient as well as beat heavy music.  The audio thump of weapons firing, punches connecting and robots being gibbed is satisfying every single time.
It is easy to tell that this is a labour of love.  Oxeye has been working on this game for 6 years, and it shows.  With multiple single player and multiplayer methods of playing, and the idea of having a full toolset to make your own levels is really cool.  So far, this title is an interesting diamond in the rough.
That’s not to say that it is without problems.  The review build I was provided by Oxeye seems to not recognize options changes.  I couldn’t change resolution or graphical quality.  The toolset opened to scripting errors and I did have the occasional crash when attempting to make options adjustments.
All of that said, for $20 you can do a hell of a lot worse and if it gets a large enough install base to where the multiplayer maintains an active community, I could see this game lasting quite some time to take advantage of those free updates Oxeye has promised.  I look forward to seeing what else Mojang might consider publishing.

Having played and loved the first two Dungeon Siege games this one came as quite a shock. It's a very different style of game and that's not in itself a bad thing, but the way it has been implemented here is.
As far as the good things go, the combat is excellent and a much better system (imo) than the previous games. Characters actually have some story to them, although the banter is not as good as DS2. The art, sound and graphics are also very good. And, oddly, your choices do actually have some relevance.
Unfortunately the rest is not so good. Major things like the camera, the (lack of)path/journey, the skillsets, the inventory, the loot, the overall story (the sub stories and characters are fine) and the lack of playable characters really detracts from the game. Especially the loot. Finding uniques doesn't actually matter, the stats are cryptic and you will most often replace items every 5 minutes. Characters are also horribly imbalanced. Anjali and Lucas are what you would expect, but Reinhart is a tactical nuke the further you progress and Katarina is weaker than wet paper. Why? Because of stats. Agility (Dex) which is crucial to Katarina gets worse as you level wheras Will (Int) remains the same which is crucial for Reinhart's skill spamming. Katarina is also not a good AoE character but Reinhart is all about AoE.
I could ramble on for ages but what it comes down to is this. There are plenty of other games you could buy and play and be much happier with. If you really want to get this, do it when it is on sale as this is a once through kinda game with 0 replayability other than trying out each character or playing in coop.

If you ever played the first two games in the Dungeon Siege series and enjoyed them, do not... I repeat, do not buy this game. It is in no way shape or form even close to the original. Other than that, its' a pretty O.K. semi- ordinary RPG taken over by a quasi- normal Japanese CO.

Bias:  I have played quite a bit of regular ole Ark, and I like it just fine.
So as of this review, I've been in 2 matches so far.
Which brings me to my first problem:  The lobbies.  A free-for-all needs 25 players for a ranked match, and even when 25 players were in the lobby, many times, the game failed to start.  I would have played more, had the lobbies functioned a little better.  I also suspect that some people are abusing the finickyness of the lobby system to disrupt normal gameplay.
Once you get in a game, you are placed in a giant bubble in the sky, where you can talk smack, plan your plans, or otherwise occupy your time.  It is important that you make your character, make your tribe, and possibly your flag, as soon as you can.  Press L to form a tribe, by the way, for those who don't know.  I am hoping that the devs can get this whole rigamarole straight, as it's probably driving people away from the game.  Perhaps an out-of-game way to craft your character, flag, and set up a 'quick tribe' to use once you get in a match?
After a period of time, you are descended to the playfield via a beam, where you are free to run amok.  In my first match, I mostly played stealth and lasted quite a while, until I encountered a man taming a trike.  I felt good during the fight, like I was winning, but the trike woke up and he whistled it onto me, and I died, caught between a trike and a hard place.
Second match, I stealthed to an area with several good specimens of beast, and tamed myself an ape.  With that ape, I then went ape, killing 3 other players.  The fourth player was able to mount his anky and overcome my element of surprise, and his trike and stego ended up finishing me off.  I was close, though.
That is all pretty good.
I recommend this game with the expectation that it will improve over time.  Ark was nearly unplayable when it came out, due to FPS issues, and now, even on my modest old computer that most would be embarrassed to own, I can play it at 40 FPS.   Ark: SOTF does run a bit poorer than that, but with a little tweaking, it ran well enough for me to score numerous kills and make numerous direct hits with bows, spears, and slingshots.
Some people will be surprised at the suddenness with which one can die, but I enjoy that aspect, as even a guy on a rex can be killed by bugs when he stops to drink or loot a fallen enemy.
I haven't tried the tech path of play yet, but it suspect it's risky until the end, when it all pays off.  4-5 combatants I've faced were hidden, attempting to make guns and armor to counteract dinosaur mount power.  At least 2 of them made it farther than me.
Which brings to another point:  When you die, you are immediately ejected from the game into the menu.  I appreciate why spectating is a bad idea, but at least having a scoreboard to see who won a match would be nice.
In the lobbies, you can see your own simplified stats, but I can't figure out a way to vew other people's stats.   Related to the above point, it would be nice to know who you were up against, as well.  Maybe something to note how often a person has killed using their mount, vs melee weapons, vs ranged weapons, etc.  I would like to know if a player in a match is an axe murderer or if they want to skulk in the shrubs waiting to bushwack the 2nd to last tired competitor with a shotgun to the face.
In a nutshell:
This is a game that is still in development.  It has some problems that may be game breaking for some.  It is based off of Ark:  Survival Evolved, and has most of the elements of that game, including crafting and heavy inventory management, so it has a learning curve.  It demands a lot of your system, and may not play at framerates that some are used to.  It is frustrating not being able to get into a game from the lobby.
That being said, it has a lot of potential, was fun for the 2 matches I've played, and it has freaking dinosaur shotgun giant ape cannibal with a spear fights.

"Amnesia: Memories" was an absolute delight. With this game, there was no contest between quantity and quality; it sacrificed neither, boasting five beautifully made routes with about twenty-six different endings. I got it on sale for about three dollars, but the content is easily worth as much as the usual price asks for.
The art used in the game is beatifully made, for all of the CGs, backgrounds, and character models. Everything is extremely detailed, and there are over one-hundred images to be collected for the gallery. Even the layout is aesthetically pleasing. The title screens, load screens, and text boxes all share a common theme and are easy on the eyes, unlike those belonging to more flamboyant visual novels. The only aspect of the game that wasn't very visually appealing was the air hockey mini-game, but this flaw is highly insignificant.
The plots for all routes were very engaging, and wildly different depending on the character of your choosing. The game did not bore, even as I replayed portions of it to achieve all endings. There are many interconnecting factors between the routes that increase the compelling force of the story, and plot twists are executed effortlessly. Character development was an extremely well thought out factor for this game, and made playing it an emotional journey.
In all, this game is everything you'd want out of a visual novel and more. With an abundance of high-quality content, it is worth every penny. I whole heartedly recommend it to any visual novel player with the emotional armor to withstand the realism of this game.

I encountered the anime version of this several years ago - enjoyed it, but it was mostly like a preview for getting into the game. It's not quite the same story, nor is it complete. So, I was happy to jump into the full version in game form.
Well, after almost 50 hours total, I've gotten all the good endings and several of the others (both bad and normal). I enjoyed every route, even if the character wasn't my usual "type". I started with Kent, 'cause I often like the stoic/nerdy type, which pretty much sums him up. He still has plenty of cute, awkward moments, though, and like all the others, he is deeply in love with your character. Next I went with Shin, because I liked his intensity. He's kinda grouchy, sometimes distant, but there's reason behind it. He gets jealous the most often which is a pro to me, heh. Then there's Toma, his competition, who alongside Shin was a childhood friend or brother figure. He plays the indulgent older brother, kind of a foil to Shin's sometimes tough love. But, his protective nature can sometimes make him go too far. Lastly - or so I thought - there's Ikki. I left him for last because I'm not as fond of playboy characters, but in his case, he's an unwilling playboy. And in the end, I loved each of their stories. Plenty of emotional and blush-inducing moments!
There is a fifth route once you've gotten the four good endings. Ukyo is a mysterious character that shows up here and there in the other routes, and he clearly has feelings for the protagonist, but is for some reason keeping his distance. Finishing his route addresses many of the questions that have cropped up throughout the game - thus, his story is quite different from the others. I liked that there was more to reveal about the world and circumstances in general once you've gotten through the first four routes. He's a fun character as well - probably the most awkward yet affectionate of the bunch.
The art style worked for me. It's not the most detailed, but every character has their own little flair. The sound is not bad - I quite enjoyed the voice-acting. On the other hand, the music is mostly boring and repetitive. Guess that's pretty common in these kinds of games.
The tone of the game is about average for otome games, too. Some routes deal with somewhat mundane problems (like choosing between a dream career and love), while others deal with kidnapping or murder. They're all pretty serious and tug on the heartstrings, though. The game doesn't really have gore, but it does describe some brutal events. In all, it's not a particularly dark game, but your character can be killed in each route. She also gets into some slightly...rapey situations. They don't go into detail, but there is talk of "taking by force" and such. It didn't go too far for my tastes, but if you don't like that sort of thing...uh, it must be hard to find otome games to play, 'cause they really seem to think girls are into that. Anyway, that stuff is in the minority - mostly the guys are being sweet or protective. Each one has four or five good scenes with a special CG - I could've done with more, but then, can't we always?
In between such scenes, I did get a little bored sometimes. I think it's a positive that the game isn't terribly long to get through - it doesn't go huge amounts of time between the good bits (the juicy stuff). I mean, who cares that much about seeing a girl trying to relearn her waitressing job? Especially FIVE DIFFERENT TIMES? And of course I didn't have much interest in her female friends, either, but they are still kinda cute and not too, too annoying with their squeaky voices.
Not sure this is worth full price - I got it on sale - but if you have the cash to spare, it could be a pretty good investment of your time, too.

Amnesia: Memories is an emotional rollercoaster, but surely is one of the best otome visual novels. Prepare to die a lot, in many brutal ways.
Pros:
- Characters have a lot of depth; all of them have completely different personality and story behind them.
- Every route has plenty of different endings.
- Music and voice acting are really great.
- Art in this game is gorgeous.
- Plenty of replay value; if you're an achievement and ending collector, then it's a huge plus.
- Interesting story full of mystery and emotions. Every route is tied together, but makes more sense once you unlock the last fifth world, it unraveles a lot of information, which has been lacking in the other routes.
Cons:
- Toma. Diamond world is the worst, imo. If you're easily disturbed or can't stand any kind of abuse, just force skip through that route.
- Some route outcomes might be really toxic.
If you're a fan of otomes, then this one is a must-have. For better experience go through the worlds by the listed order, that way you will be prepared for escalation of insanity.
If you're unsure about purchasing it, watch the anime first to get the idea of what's this all about, though it doesn't have as much depth and story as this visual novel; or you can just grab it on sale.
Personally, I had a lot of fun reading through all the stories, so definitely recommended. Would cry over Ukyo again.

Ok, so this is a tough review for me, because I know, that there are gamers out there, who will love Rise & Shine. But me, I despise it.
The game looks fantastic, runs well and has the most generic setting there is. Invasion, please save the planet. The gimmick is you can steer bullets with different effects. Nice touch.
Here is my problem: The game tries to kill you by random shooting patterns, out of nowhere enemies, impossible to dodge attacks and other random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, you might be able to adjust to (infinite lives and generous checkpoints), but dying every inch of the way isn't my idea of a good time, or a good game. If you are not put off by the thought that the only thing letting you survive for more than 20 seconds is your response time and the learning through the previous four to twentyseven deaths in the same screen, then this game is for you.
IF you also get along with the controls. It is unplayable with mouse and keyboard, and it is almost as bad with a controller, because you switch between bullet steering mode and moving mode. I know a lot of people personally, who love such games and praise them for the challenge they pose. To me, it is an unfair, rage inducing, hectic, unbalanced, hard to control 2D sidescroller that offers no motivation for me to go on, gameplay or storywise. But please, understand me here. I don't recommend the game for people with similar preferences like mine. I do recommend it very highly for those "the harder and unfairer, the better" people out there, because they will enjoy it a lot.

Okay so let’s take a minute to talk about Flappy bird— oh sorry I mean Rise & Shine.
But jokes aside there is so much to say and think about Rise & Shine, and everything is so divided that I feel like you’re either going to absolutely love this game or if you’re like me, you’re going to wish your insurance was better so that you could just throw your PC out of the window to get rid of it.
Rise & Shine is a side-scrolling shoot-’em-up brought to us by Super Maga Team and Adult Swim Games.
The game calls reference to so many other games that honestly it’s hard to keep track, but it’s those homages that give the game its tongue in cheek humor and style.
So let me start off with the reasons why you will probably love this game:
Rise & Shine looks simply AMAZING. Now I play a LOT of Platformers, and I can honestly say not very many of them capture the vibrant beauty and ‘aliveness’ that is Rise & Shine. The world just has such an attention to detail and your character, Rise, just fits so perfectly into it that the whole world seems to ‘spark’ with little flecks of magic that pull everything together seamlessly.
Now part of that beauty, and this feeling of joy you get when looking at the game, comes from how well they pull off the whole ‘comic book’ style that the game has, you go from a very traditional comic book look in the cutscenes to this world that just brings all of that to life. And I love it.
This is all only complimented further by a soundtrack that is, quite frankly, AAA title worthy.
And if it’s your thing, Rise & Shine awakens the same feelings in you that Flappy Bird does.
So speed completionists, and people who are suckers for games that ruthlessly punish you should get their fill here.
Now let’s move on to why I think you won’t enjoy the game:
It awakens the same feelings in you that Flappy Bird does.
Honestly, I can’t even remember a time in my life that I got this irrationally angry and frustrated while playing a game.
Oh, but I wasn’t playing, not really, all I was doing was dying.
Again, and again and again.
Don’t let the fun, childlike look of the game deceive you like it did me, this game is needlessly frustrating.
The actual game is very short, it only lasts you about 2 hours, but I can fully see someone better than me being able to beat it in an hour. Because of this I can’t help but shake the feeling that the reason the game was made to be so overly difficult was an unsuccessful attempt to hide the shortness.
The mechanics and controls are so clunky and all over the place that I couldn’t decide if using a controller or a mouse and keyboard were worse, until I eventually gave up trying to play with any tactics in mind and just started blind spraying bullets (you have an unlimited amount of ammo) in the direction of my target while wildly running back and forth praying I kill them before they kill me.
Also, did I mention that 90% of the time you will be killed by just one hit? Well, you are, so that’s fun.
This game is perfect if you’re one of those people who don’t mind dying and repeating the same stage hundreds of times just so that you can brag to the world and say you’ve beaten the game, but for me, I think I had so much expectation but sadly, it didn’t live up to much of it.
Now would I tell you to avoid the game? Well no.
Because even though this type of game is evidently just not my cup of tea, as I said at the start, I can definitely see how it is many other peoples.
However, I really think the current price tag is far too steep for such a short game, so maybe do yourself a favor and wait for a sale. But again, that’s just me, and what do I know, I just spent the last 3 hours of my life either dead or dying.
But that’s Rise & Shine for you.
Do you like games that are so frustrating that you get a cold sweat just thinking about it? Yes? Well then Rise & Shine is for you. If not, rather go play something relaxing, like Flappy Bird...

Endless Legend is similar to most 4X games, notably the Civilization genre. There are a few major differences:
1. Armies are far more personable. Each unit you create can be outfitted with equipment that can massively increase their stats based on how many strategic resources you have (think iron, oil, etc. from Civ5). This lets you create one "death stack" of 5-6 units that both get experience and equipment to allow them to defeat any group of enemies.
2. Hero units are also available that level up into skill trees you put points in. They can either lead armies or command cities improving the stats of each.
3. Combat occurs on a grid, similar to Heroes of Might and Magic, with turn based combat occuring based on the Initiative stat of each creature, it creates a whole new depth to combat allowing a weaker force to subdue a better one with good positioning.
Most everything else is  similar to Civ5, if you were disgruntled with Beyond Earth, this may be a better choice for you.

After loving Endless Space, I jumped in Endless Legend without a moment of doubt, expecting what neither Firaxis (with Civ) nor Stardock (with Elemental) have managed to produce since: a good 4X game in a fantasy universe.
From the outside, Endless Legend looks like a perfect fit: based on the Civilization formula, with more RPG elements and somehow more depth. Unfortunately, Endless Legend has rather "more complexity" than more depth, and seems to throw more complex things in that don't necessarily add more fun to the game, and without properly introducing you to the game systems you should know.
Another sad element is the technical part, which doesn't hold up. Animations are often stuttering, bugs and crashes are still very present a long time after launch, and as soon as you have uncovered many AI civilizations and a large part of the map, the game gets extremely laggy. Its very detailed world is beautiful but seems to be the game engine's demise on the long run.
In the end, you end up with a game that is unnecessarily complicated and not very fluid. Not a great experience overall, and at least not up to the expectation that Amplitude had set with Endless Space.
