"You've already seen the "Overwhelmingly Positive" user reviews, haven't you? Why are you here, then? Why do you continue to scroll through them while your memory betrays you? You enjoy reading reviews, that's why."
I'll get straight to the point. This review's main goal is to address common misconceptions.
Amount of Content:
Ground Zeroes offers 7 missions: one main story, four side missions with different objectives, two extra side missions that are aimed at the fans of the series. Each mission has two difficulty settings (hard unlocks after beating normal), secret collectibles/objectives and unlockable trials (challenges). Throughout all missions you'll be dealing with only one location: Camp Omega, which is a fairly large facility. Each mission has it's own time of day.
If you like playing your games at a medium pace and you never had contact with this game before then you'll be able to complete all 7 missions in 5-10 hours+. If you're willing to spend time to get 100% completion, get most of the rewards and read/listen to the story then you might end up with 15-20 hours+ on you. However, it's possible to speedrun all 7 mission in ~1 hour (that is, if you know what you're doing). If you buy Phantom Pain alone then you won't be able to access Camp Omega and it's missions through it as they're avilable only for those that purchased Ground Zeroes (meaning this is a prologue and not a demo). However, if you purchased both then you'll be able to visit Camp Omega with all your Phantom Pain upgrades, not to mention special bonuses.
Performance & Settings:
Runs on systems that are below minimum system requirements. Well optimized, but could've had even higher level of detail / drawing distance settings (some visible popup of small items). One common complaint are increased amounts of depth of field (blur / out of focus). It's easily "fixed" by decreasing Screen Filtering to High.
Fully playable on K&M but could've had a slightly better control scheme (currently there's some sensitivty bug when aiming while zoomed). Minority of people experiences some compatibility issues some of which were caused by bad system configurations, but some are legit and there most likely will be a compatibility fixing patch.
Metal Gear is a legendary franchise, Ground Zeroes gives you a tiny bite of Phantom Pain and from here it only gets better. If you're into stealth, "tactical espionage action", shooters or just good stories then you should certainly get it. The game gives you freedom to choose your own path and your own tactics / playing style, be it complete stealth no kill or running around shooting rockets and riding tanks.

Here is a game that got completely overlooked. Partially with good reason as it is NOTHING like the previous titles in the Dungeon Siege franchise. While the game is still a hack and slash at it's heart, there's nowhere near the amount of loot and customization typically associated with games of that nature. That doesn't mean there isn't a great game to be played here, just maybe not the one you expect.
Instead of creating a custom character at the start of your adventure you are given a choice of four different characters. Each has a completely different ability set than the other and a somewhat different adventure in terms of who you meet and when. I've played as all four and with the exception of one they are all a blast to play. I highly recommend trying out all of them whether it be in another play through (you are required to complete certain tasks, like getting to level 20, as each character) or in multiplayer. The game was made by Obsidian as well so the writing for all the characters is very solid and voice acting is pretty good.
When it comes to combat this game doesn't disappoint. It DOES, however, almost completely require a controller. You would think playing with a KB&M would fit a Dungeon Siege game but unfortunately, it doesn't. If you have a controller though, you're in for some great hack and slash combat with a fair amount of strategy (especially on the hardest difficulty).
Visually and audibly this game is pretty darn good. The music, while nothing special, fits the game enough. You won't be humming any of the tunes, but you won't be cursing the game for repetition. On the visual side, this game looks great for an isometric title. Even during cut scenes (where you see your model up close) there is a great amount of detail present and numerous visual effects that add to the level of immersion. The voice acting does Obsidian's script justice as well.
Last but not least, I have to mention  multiplayer. I played through the entire game about two times in multiplayer sessions and it is a BLAST if you have people who know how to use each character. It's almost necessary for the highest difficulty in the game to played with other people if you want to stand a chance. While the game can be enjoyed fine solo, it's at it's best in multiplayer sessions. Each player takes a different role and strategy really starts to come into play.
Overall I highly recommend Dungeon Siege III assuming you have a controller. If you have a KB&M I honestly can't recommend it as it is a pain to play that way. If, however, you have a controller and some friends to join you you are in for a treat.

This is a rather poorly made port of DMC3 for the PS2. It's not entirely unplayable as some may lead you to believe, but it's bad enough to make you want to not play the game despite how fun it is.
Most console controllers will refuse to work for the game and what DOES work will leave you wanting more, such as not being able to use one of your joysticks. You CAN download a program to fix this and it's really not the main issue with the port because it can be fixed. The real problem comes from the fact that you will have massive, and I mean MASSIVE fps drops in multiple locations resulting in it being neigh unplayable.
But in those non-large areas where fps is stable and you fix the controller up, it works rather well for a port.
I wouldn't recommend it because it's far too much work to get everything in working condition.

THAT ALL BEING SAID

This i an AMAZING game that I played years ago on the PS2.  Everything about this game is rediculous.  The combat, the story, the cutscenes, it's all over the top crazy action, and I love it.  I bought this on Steam to try to replay it with some better graphics, but unfortunately, this game was not optimized for PC at ALL.
Controller support is awful, you CAN get some of them to work, but it isn't easy, and you have to a lot of research to find out how to get it to work.
Graphics are technically better than they were on the PS2, but widescreen support is not built in, so if you are one of the normal PC users that have a 16:9 or 16:10 screen, you will have blackbars on the sides of the screen.  There is a mod to 'fix' this, but it basically just stretches the screen, so it looks awful.
Capcom didn't try very hard on the PC version of this game, which is unfortunate, because it's one of the best DMC's.  Try Devil May Cry 4 or DMC, they have way better support, so they know how to do it right, just not wortgh their effort to fix this version I guess.
TL;DR version - Great game, but badly ported.  Play the game, just not the PC version.

This is an epic pile of stupid the likes of which is hard to describe.  It opens with Britons attacking Rome (utter fiction, and pretty much impossible), then a retaliatory attack on Britannia which featured medieval castles, Tyrion's chain tower, and Orcs errr I mean "Britons."
After that, they go to York (I think they meant Eboracum) to fight King Oswald of Northumbria (who wouldn't be born for about another 600 years) and his "daughter" Boudica (who was the first century Queen of the Iceni, who ruled over the territory that became East Anglia).
Meanwhile, the Romans are running around with later period shields, rather than the oval shields that they would have had during the subjugation era of Romano-British history.
It's so ridiculously stupid it blows my mind.  And there's actually a pretty good story to be told if someone read a book or, hell, just listened to a damn podcast.  Caesar invaded twice, and both times had some pretty epic battles as well as some seriously dire circumstances.  Or you could do the real life story of Boudica, which would involve Governor Suetonius fighting the Britons, butchering the druids at the sacred groves of Anglesey, and then facing off with Boudica and her massive Celtic army that might have numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
But instead, apparently, the writers just wanted to watch Game of Thrones, look up a couple names on Wikipedia, and call it "history."
Ugh.  Somehow the developers managed to make Gladiator look accurate.  Next time, I hope they just make a Lord of the Rings game and leave history to people who know how to read.

It's a decent, if "excuse plot" game with cool mechanics and excellent multiplayer. In fact, the entire game is built entirely for multiplayer, with even the main storyline being a connection of multiplayer-ish levels against AI bots interspersed with fighting Akrid and boss fights.
Gameplay is a bit clunky-  the over the shoulder view doesn't always have your character aiming towards your reticle, and soemtimes performign actions will skew the camera - throwing a grenade for example will adjust your view- and also tweak where you're throwing your grenade, making proper aim take practice. The grappling hook, while useful as always, is a bit short, I'd say even shorter than the first game, and timing it's aim is quite the pain the♥♥♥♥♥ you get a few seconds of movement before the "claw" hits an object, and god help you if anything hits your or happens to you in that time.
The thing you will curse 90% of the time is that you will be attempting to platform or make some precise jumps or move towards an edge to hookshot to a wall, and if you just ever so slightly fall off the platform, your character will make a "safety catch" where they stop whatever they're doing and hookshot back on the ledge you came from. This overrides all other actions, including hookshotting, regardless of whether or not there's safe ground below you.  So say, you want to hop down a hole? Gotta have some distance, and JUMP down that hole, because ifyou try to just run off, you "catch" yourself. This action? It is very, very slow, and time consuming,and the only way out of it is to jump or drop, and the jump is more vertical and useless for clearing gaps, forcing you to hop back to the ledge you fell from, and try again. This makes the time trial training levels a sore pain because you'll find yourself running off a ledge just barely, and forced to waste 5 seconds pulling yourself back up, you'll make a jump and slide off the platform you land on, losing another 5 seconds, you'll hookshot a wall but inadvertently step one foot off the platform while doing so and thus lose another 5 seconds plus the time it takes to properly align yourself. In combat, this means thatyou're also completely helpless for 5 seconds because oops! Fell off a short ledge, better catch myself and let everyone shoot me dead.
Add onto this "stunlock", where being shot makes your character stop all other actions for a second- you cannot fire, you cannot run, dodge or hookshot. This makes any open firefight annoying, as you have a good deal of health but will be John Marston'd to death without even being able to dodge roll out of it. Platforming while enemies are nearby is impossible for this  very reason, and the harder time trials are all about enemies with aimbot perfect accuracy pinging you with pistols. Naturally, at a few points in the campaign you'll also be asked to platform or navigate a large battlefield quickly while being shot at, making this quite frustrating.  Certain inputs also edge out other ones, meaning timing your inputs in battle is important, or finding ways to do two things at once for maximum efficiency. For example, you can only move slowly while reloading, and cannot jump or run, and for a second after running, you can't jump or reload. However by jumping, then reloading, you'll move fairly quickly and perform a shorter reload animation.
Other than that, the gunplay feels natural, the "floaty" jump and hookshot let you pull off mean headshots from midair, with unparalleled freedom of movement while fighting.
Multiplayer is great, but finding people to play with is a bit hard, as GFWL is still on this game, and thus getting everything working takes possibly a degree in computer science, so you'll not see too many people playing this online.  The game's also not interested in things like 'safe spawning' - enemies will spawn on top of you, you'll spawn in the same area as other players, and while you get some mercy invincibility until you fire your gun, expect to spawn,  open fire on an enemy, have another enemy spawn immediately behind you and kill you.
Unlocks for weapons, skills, and character customizations are all random- you have a  lottery adn all the item boxes you find just go into money for this lottery. Endless Legend is a refreshing and fun take on Civ-style strategy games. Set in a sci-fantasy world, you can play one of several races trying to control the future of Auriga - the planet over which you are struggling.
Starting with a single city (and sometimes staying with just a single city), the game play will feel very familiar to strategy game enthusiasts. You must expand your territories to new, richer provinces with luxery and strategic resources to bolster your budding civilization. Exploration is driven by the need to find more provinces, but also a relatively unique mechanic: questing.
Your explore the map with army stacks, usually led by a hero. The heroes are the face of your empire. They have the ability to explore ruins, triggers quests, and complete the quests that are driving your race forward across Auriga. They can be specialized into exploring/combat/administration of your cities. The bonuses that they provide are significant, so having a stable of heroes that are governing your cities and leading your armies is crucial.
Combat can be auto-resolved, or it breaks out into a tactical mini-game. You can issue general orders to your troops as you fight on new terrain for every battle. You will need to balance your front line (infantry) units, damage (ranged units), high mobility units (flying/cavalry) and support (healers/buff/debuff) units in the most optimal way that you can for your race and the opponents that you are facing. Unit customization is pretty deep; it's necessary, as time goes on, to improve your hero and your frontline units with new gear. You can specialize some units into tanks; some will always go first; some will just do a ton of damage. This is one of the more engaging parts of the game, as you decide what your troops will look like. Additionally, as the result of quests and research, you can equip your heroes with very powerful unique items that change the way they fight/govern cities.
Having beaten the game on Endless Legend, I can say that the weakness of the game is the AI; at both early and late stages, the combat AI is not particulary skilled or robust. Still, they generally okay at the strategic end of things.
Winning means fulfilling one of several conditions: Technology Victory, Wonder Victory, Quest Victory, Extermination Victory, Conquest Victory, Economic Victory, or Diplomatic Victory. Generally, you can attain most of these victory conditions with any of the races, though some specialize more towards one or the other.
The game is visually unique, and quite beautiful. The world has character, as do the races and units therein. I would rate Endless Legend as the best fantasy/sci-fi strategy game out right now with its balance of strategic management and tactical combat.

Anyway, FM itself is still amazing and the love of my life (sort of), but these issues demand ranting after so much money has been spent on the game. And despite all this ranting, I am going to continue smashing the game away!

TL;DR: Recommended, still, because even with the devs out of the picture and the population somewhat...intimately small, the community is still good and the gameplay is too depending on what you like to do in a game like this and overall it would be insane to not recommend a game I enjoyed playing for thousands of hours...yes. ThousandS! I hope I´m wrong about the off Steam time...but I fear I am not :D
____________________________________________________
Depending on what class you spec into, your experience in-game will differ. Some classes can solo, some will have a really bad time without a party. That said, with the devs giving up on this game to pursue other projects, and the community being more based on nostalgia rather than new players, actually finding a party throughout the levels is going to be a challenge at this state. It was a challenge back at Steam release and that´s where the game reached some of its peak traffic. High levels can - and are sometimes even villing to help you, themselves or with their alow level chars, but if you don´t do the dungeons and quests with a party of your own levels, you will never learn how to play your role properly.  (Only dying a hundred times in Ohdar scar can really teach you a lesson in teamwork! :D)
Overall, the best aspect of the game is the crafting/gathering system. That is the part of the game that has the very distinct Runescape feel to it, but alas only some items are even worth crafting and fishing for instance is a reason to become braindead in matter of hours. Whoever maxed fishing is a god damn machine!
There is little PvP and since the classes are so poorly balanced for PvP, it sucks balls. Because some classes aren´t viable for PvP, people don´t play them. Because some classes level with more difficulty than others, people don´t play them. *cough* TANKS *cough* So yeah, unbalanced classes ruin this game a lot. Community had always been friendly - unless you are on TA in the middle of a PvP zone. You will die there. Don´t go there if you´re gonna be salty about it.
PvE content is superb. I actually even paid attention to the story for once and I am a confirmed story-skipper. Quests/daily quests do offer some variety, but not TOO much. Dungeons are fun, because they are not easy and you can have high levels in your team and still get obliterated if you don´t know how to fight a particular boss or group of enemies. Instances/arenas are there...but meh. Nobody queues for them.
Graphics are not everyone´s cup of tea, to me they always looked funny but I don´t really care about this aspect of a game. As long as it doesn´t make my eyes bleed - and it didn´t.
The in-game shop is decent, not really P2W although some shady EXP pots and chests of gold are in there (ruining the eco with the currency a bit), but I like that they mostly decided to go with vanity items (basically fancy clothes), pets, mounts etc. that don´t affect gameplay. Compared to other, known P2W MMOs out there, Eldevin is just a couple items shy of being perfect in the F2P model. It didn´t bother me, at least.
My advice is, try this for yourself. See if it´s your cup of tea. It would sure be nice to see more people around...might even make me go back to spend another thousand hours in this...oh god send help :D

Okay, let me start this review out by saying this: Steam royally screwed up what could have ben an awesome product. There is just not enough reason to justify this purchase when it is the bare minimum of what could have been done to make this a working game. The Commander Keen series is an amazing set of games, a piece of the history of PC gaming, and Steam treated this piece of history like most people treat their garbage.
To elaborate,  Commander Keen was the first PC game to have Parallax scrolling, the same kind of scrolling that Super Mario uses to be able to have a Platformer. At the time, it was a huge deal to have the entire level not be a single screen. So Commander Keen was produced to prove that a PC could support a full Platformer of many screens and levels. The game has an overworld and lets you play levels in any order, you get to shoot enemies from a distant and it is also the Nintendo Hard you would expect from a classic game, so it should be a dream for people who wish to visit a time when 2D was king. To neglect this classic trilogy and the 2/3rds of a trilogy sequel would be a shame.
Now, I am not suggesting you buy this pack. Especially if you don't know the series already. This pack is a bare minimum attempt at a quick buck off of some old shareware games.  Yes, you heard me, SHAREWARE. If you are not aware, due to age or not being a PC gamer until after Floppy Disks disappeared, Shareware was the precursor to Playable Demo games on services such as Playstation Network, X-Box Live Arcade and yes, even Steam, where you would get a part of the game on a floppy disk at no charge, to try out. In the main menu, you would often see an "Order Now!" or "Ordering Details" option that let you buy the full game's disk for a reasonable sum of money. It spread the word of companies and got them some revenue as well as positive customer feedback that people were willing to pay money for their ideas.
So, since the game (well Commander Keen 1 and Commander Keen 4 are Shareware, at least) is technically free, you would think that this pack would do something more to make you want to buy it, right? Well, you'd be wrong. In fact, this pack is actually more of a hassle than going out and downloading Commander Keen 1, 2, 3 and 4 and a DOSBox Emulator yourself. To access any game past Commander Keen 1, you have to open up your Steam window, go into your library and launch it from there. Double Clicking the Shortcut that is generated on the desktop does nothing more than launch the first game. Not even a hastily slapped together Commander Keen selection menu screen comes up, just the default steam menu with radial buttions even after going through the hassle.
So I suggest to you to save your money, go get a DOSBox Emulator, and download Commander Keen 1 to try out. You don't have to send any money and it is legal because that's how the game was released back in the day. And if you go and get the non-shareware games? Well, it's not like ID software is going to come after you for picking up a title that they don't even have the rights to anymore. Though, the one thing this pack does RIGHT is that Commander Keen 5: The Armageddon Machine has it's copy protection (having one of the items you need to complete the level not spawn at all, making the second level impossible to complete) set to working properly as if you bought the game.

The mission is simple, find Chico and Paz and get them to extraction. However we all know this is a MGS game so there is always a catch ;). The AI is some of the series best, and while this is the first time Kojima brought snake "Open World" it feels natural. This is how he intended it. This allows new and old fans to become accustomed to the new tride and true CQC styles, get familiar with the dynamic AI, and best of all teaches us how to take on missions one at a time in MGSV The Phantom Pain when it releases. I mean lets be honest here, if Kojima were to just throw us in a huge open world in TPP without training us first, ALOT of people would have felt misplaced and uncomfortable. We are used to fixed routes and blindspots and tricks and most of them wouldnt have worked in this new amazing system. So why are you still reading this? Just go buy it now while its on sale and make up your own mind.. How do you want to complete this mission? By slicing everyones neck? Slow and stealthy? Take your chances blowing♥♥♥♥♥♥up cus its fun? Or giving everyone and there mommas a shakedown on info... So many routes, so many ways to complete the objective. (Hint: you dont need to extract people in helicopters ;) )
Enjoy this teaser of whats to come and practice practice practice. Because when the Phantom Pain comes, will you be ready?

The backgrounds and character sprites were very pretty - the game is very well-illustrated and everything just looks great. I never grew tired of the backgrounds and setpieces - in fact - I'd love to see a few wallpapers based on them.
I grabbed this in a Humble Bundle - for that price, it was great. You might want to weigh gameplay vs price when picking it up, though, because even though the artwork and gameplay is great, I've completed the whole thing in about 3 hours and I have no desire to replay it.
I would absolutely recommend a playthrough for the right price, especially if you can grab it in a bundle.

Short Version:
Coming into this game expecting more of DS1/2? You'll be disappointed. Forget the Dungeon Siege name and you'll find a pretty solid game with nice couch co-op.
Long Version:
Gameplay: Clearly more geared for console (gamepad) play, enjoyable nonetheless: fights ask more out of your positioning and timing with attack/skills/dodge/block. There's a lot of enemies/loot/merchants, some quests and the 4 main jobs you'd expect on a DS game, even if under a new paint. Of course I miss using multiple party members but the AI is not that bad, my biggest problem is with the online co-op: the camera is BAD and the game doesn't allow all players to have a character, you have the host's game and everyone else is a guest using the stats/equips of the characters in it.
Story: The plot isn't winning any awards, and there are less characters and worldbuilding than in the previous DS's. The narrator isn't bad but most of the story feels like it's trying to be more epic than it is. I also felt that, for a game with choices, they should matter more than... next to nothing, lots of places could have been better/more explored. The main characters are decent and their interactions are a nice add to the experience.
Sound: A mild soundtrack with no memorable themes. Nevertheless, they fit the locations and acompany the battles, nothing felt out of place. I enjoyed the VA for all characters with a huge bias towards Katarina's, I'm a sucker for that accent @_@.
Graphics: A great improvement from the infamous derpy looking DS's graphics (which I had no problem with), love the changing armours, the spells effects, the scenarios, they all hold up to this day imo.
Disclaimer: I'm a huge fan of the DS franchise and, like a lot of people, had trouble adapting to this new style, I feel like it would have done better under a different name.

I had maaaaybe one or two otome games under my belt when I played Amnesia for the first time.
I had no idea what I was getting into.
Thus, a word to the wise: if this is your first foray into otome, be aware that you're in for a wild, wild ride. What I once dismissed as a rom-com genre is happy home to more blood and guts and homicidal maniacs than any FPS or RPG in my experience. Bare bones example of one of the many, many, many, many bad endings my hapless heroine met with:

After dying many a gruesome death in the name of love, I found myself addicted. Truth be told, I don't really find the "romances" in Amnesia romantic, but they're cathartic and the characters are fascinating. Sure, most of the leading men have control issues, and some have serious consent issues, and the plot is frankly a bit thin on the ground, but whether it's just exorcising the worst fears women live with, or if a cypher of a main character is really just a placeholder while, contrary to gender expectations, we identify with "male" controlling / angry / possessive desires, there is a great deal of satisfaction to be derived from even the bloodiest of bad endings here. There are emotions taboo and conventional to explore, and those emotions are validated without judgment, even if the validation is a little bit twisted. Simply surviving is a challenging and rewarding puzzle on its own.
This all sounds bananas, but the game is both bananas and awesome. I laughed, I died, I died some more, I got a good end. I looked up walkthroughs to make sure I got all the good and bad ends. There are many more bad than good ends.
Recommendation on play order: the game obviously wants you to like Shin and (Secret Route) best, but Ikki is, bizarrely, the least problematic for those who care about consent and respect for bodily autonomy, in my opinion. I'd recommend Ikki/Spade > Kent/Club > Shin/Heart > Toma/Diamond > (Secret Route)/Joker. It's a slow degradation from warped but cute to lots and lots and lots of death (and laughter).
On a technical note, there are some issues with achievements triggering, but overall? 9/10.

Clickr can be extremely frustrating at times, but gives you a huge feeling of relief and accomplishment when you beat a difficult level. I completed all 50 of the main levels in around three hours so there's that. I didn't have to use tutorials on anything, but since every level is the same every time, you could possibly use a walkthough if you got stuck somewhere.
After the first fifty stages, a battle mode and push mode open up. I've seen these types of stages before on some old Nintendo games and they are a little more entertaining than the puzzle levels. Unfortunately, they cost in-game points to unlock which are a pain to gather up. On the other hand, fun unlockables give the game much more depth outside of its basic puzzle component.
Lastly, the music is great but the sound effect voiceovers are annoying. Most of it got mistranslated and you keep hearing YEEEEEEE!!! YEEE!!!!! every time you get a combo and you get A LOT of combos. Luckily, you can turn this repetitive noise off, but I didn't know that at first.
I think this is one of those games that is fun to play on a plane or something without sound for an hour or two. You'll come back to it over and over until you beat those initial levels, but after that there's not much will to continue.
Rating: 5.5/10

The campaign action is just flat-out fun and never gets stale thanks to much awesomeness. For starters, there are loads of ways which you can complete stages. Want to be your team's sniper? Grab that rifle and bring it with you to the next stage. If not, grab that shield and earn bonuses for defending against bazookas and mech fire, or just jump on that gun turret over there and fire in your enemy's general direction. Go around a side path and solo 2 big akrid while your team goofs off. Grapple onto a giant boss's limb and pump entire magazines of bullets into its weakpoint while it's actively stomping your allies.
Want more awesome? Go into space skinned as a chick in skimpy armor and watch yourself do awesome things in character-accurate cutscenes. Battle in every 80s American movie classic setting - "battle in the jungle!", "battle in the slums!", "battle in the docks!", "battle on desert trains!". All this wrapped in a patriotic story about violent and ruthless war tribes united against a threat to their very planet (I won't lie, it took me like a year to understand this plot but there it is).
Whatever GFWL hassles people complain about, you can power through them. Hundreds of us have, and we're out here on helicopters shooting angry ice bugs. Grab some friends, or join some randoms who'll steamroll every stage for you. I promise, you'll only wish this whole ride lasted longer.

Let's get this party started! Devil May Cry 3 is the best. It just is. With a charming cast of supporting characters, Dante at his best, both gameplay and personality wise, as well as the best music, enviroments, enemy design, and bosses, weapon selection, and extra content of the series, I cannot tell you how much I love this game, but  I can say it is a lot. So much feels connected and satisfying, and the game just has so many satisfying moments it's enough to make me sweat more than anything else does.
Shamefully however, Ubisoft ported this and they did a pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ job too. No widescreen support is lame, really bad controller support is ♥♥♥♥ing awful and actually manages to make DS3 bluescreen somehow. And the cutscene quality is pretty dissapointing too,  but thankfully most of this can be fixed.
Now I can get on to the good stuff though. Dante's gameplay just feels great because he not only has the abilities to bring interesting stuff to the table, but enemies that flow around them. If there's something that feels awkward to fight, it's because you aren't thinking outside the box yet.  DT explosion is an okay mechanic too, I like it better than "DT improves style moves", but it's just filler most of the time I think.
The bosses in this are really cool too, Nevan in particular is a favourite of mine, not due to her sexuality, but due to the fact that she really compliments Dante in her scenes, if only one boss could become a Devil Arm, it should be her. The other bosses are pretty cool too, with Cerberus' great music and Dante's cheeky one liners at him, those twin swords guys making for an interesting fight that forces you to think of it as a double boss; as well as the Vergil and Jester fights that gradually get harder and more interesting as the game goes on, which make for a very cool REAL final boss fight, although fighting side by side with a certain character for that one boss was cool too. I also really like how while Dante tends to be an overzealous cocky badass, he does understand what it means to actually be human and actually shows emotion as well, which is good, since Lady is a great receptor for these feelings, as well as an attractive character style, sexually, and personality wise. I also do like Vergil's conviction and dedication to his personal creed as well. Arkham and Jester are also very cool as well!  Another thing I really like is how powerful styles get to be at level 3, it really makes you feel powerful with whatever you choose, but you also don't feel dependent on them, with the strong weapons and guns as well.
Playing as Vergil is also pretty cool, although I must admit he feels a bit too eh for me. I also like the ability to pick whatever level of Bloody Palace you want to go to, it's just neat, but I wish there was a boss rush mode sometimes.
Also have to say the credits sequence is a HUGE turn on, ♥♥♥♥ I love playable credits.
One hell of a party!/10

First of all lets get one thing cleared out quickly apart from the name dungeon siege 3 , this game does not have much to do with the other games apart from being set in the same world nor does it carry on the traditional style the first two games had.
I can only recommend this game as a separate rpg and not a dungeon siege rpg game. With that Obsidian got many things right with the game and many things horribly wrong. Overall its a decent rpg game with a single expansion that can easily last for about 30 hours. The story is good enough to carry on till the end.
Pros
- Good story decisions affect it a lot , every decision aftermath is narrated nicely in the end making you want to play the game again and correct a few decisions.
- Good graphics and a decent sized world to play in.
- Tons of side quests and lore to find and has a nice gps style helper to lead you to the quests if you have trouble finding the locations.
- Co-op is a hit and miss , surely no one plays it and the camera would mess it up worse but its always nice to play a 4 player co-op in story mode
Cons
- The controls are kinda good and horrible it fails to have a proper point and click nor a keyboard oriented control, which means you will be moving around awkwardly and missing tons of attacks. Aiming is horribly hard which made me stick to melee only.
- Mad camera view points, its the worst enemy , never use the mouse to control the camera.
- As with Obsidian games before the game crashes a lot and freezes up frequently in cut scenes.
- Terrible skills most of it is not needed and it makes the game more complex
- The game has a lots of unwanted complex stats instead of the standard attributes most rpgs limit themselves , just go for anything that increases attack and health leech(vampire) , They tried to copy the D&D attributes but gave up and its just confusing.
- Boring loot the rare items can become more better than unique items which should not happen in  a rpg.
- Companions are terrible and there isn't any romance or side quests related to them either.
It would certainly be sad that square enix killed off the dungeon siege series after how badly this game did , because this game sets up the story nicely for more sequels to be made in the series.

Top-down action adventure. It's okay, not great.
The good stuff: No glitches, decent storyline, interesting abilities, good combo-ing
The bad stuff: Not many abilities (only 9 per character), boring enemy abilities (melee or range. No specials).
The worst things:
1. DPS doesn't mean anything in this game. Every description is too vague. "Lightning has a moderate chance to do low damage over 2 seconds": This is meaningless without number. Most abilities work this way.
2. You can't play a mage. There's no way to just use 'will' to attack, and will powers spells. If you use just abilities, you run out of mana. Then you die because you didn't build attack power, just will. Be a mage and do something every 5 seconds or so maybe.
It's fun for a single 8 hour playthrough, but I can pretty much guarantee it's not worth a second playthrough.

Bottom Line Up Front: If you have a friend (or 2) who will play the game with you it's worth the $10 USD it currently costs.  If you don't fall into that category, save your money for something that will be a little more enjoyable in the long run.
Pros:
-Decent mechanics. The way you build your character as the game progresses definatley matters and can play a major role in winning or losing; as can character selection.
-In the same vein as the first one, characters are plenty and you can spend hours just playing through them to figure out what you like.  Then there's the matter of finding your "build" for that character.
-Smooth gameplay.  Disregarding actual latency issues from a player (very small occurence) the gameplay was smooth.  Something that deserves mention considering there aren't dedicated servers and instead each person acts as the "host" in a small P2P networked match.
-Very replayable.  Matches last for ~20 minutes.  And from when you click launch you can be in a match in less than 5 minutes.  After a match you can be in another in less than 3.  During peak times it's about 1.5 minutes.  It makes it a very nice game when you are low on time or don't want a huge time committment to have a quick enjoyable match.
Cons
-Because there are no dedicated servers, the game decides who's hitbox is "right" by going with whoever cast an ability.  If someone is lagging and throw's a nuke your way even if you dodge it on your screen, if they see it as hitting you then they hit you.  Some folks purposely lag their computer to get an advantage.  It's a very small subset of the already small population but it's there.  I hesitated adding this but since it isn't free to play you should know what you're paying for. (Funny side note: I once played a guy who in game name was "I only lag in nauts" or something like that.)
-You don't have access to all of your skills until you have leveled more in the game.  It puts you at a disadvantage against the players who have been playing for a bit.  It's a fairly quick leveling process. I'm almost done at almost 40 hours of gameplay.  How quickly you level will depend on how often you win ... which feeds into the next and biggest con.
-And finally, the reason I can't recommend this game. The player base for this game is miniscule compared to other games and the singleplayer is extremely lackluster.  As a result of the small playerbase, premade groups are in the same queue as solo players.  If you don't have a friend who is in this game and you decide to dedicate some time to it, you will move up to a league where it seems all you play is premade groups who are on voip.  They roll around stomping pubbers and have the nerve to talk trash while they do it.  All of my games for about the last 2.5 hours of gaming has been this.  The whole experience makes the game itself unenjoyable.  At this point I'm trying to decide whether I should find a real MOBA or wreck my stats to drop down into a bracket where I find less of them.  If you decide to look it up, you can find posts about it every year since it came out.

While I may have little time in the steam version, I have owned this game for many years.
Cobalt is an action side scrolling game with great combat mechanics.
The story, so far, is great and has a metroidvania feel to it. While not hard to find, the story contains some secret areas with powerful weapons or loot that are rewarding to find. The story also contains a few puzzles such as searching the area for a "plug" to put inside of a slot to advance or, as I’ve seen so far, three different kinds of lock picking. One where it is stylistic of a tradition lock with the pins and you have to listen for a click, one with the rotation locks that you'd see on a locker where you turn it until you hear a click then turn in the opposite direction, and one where it plays you a tune and you have to adjust some notes until you match it. There are also boss battles that are very fun to do. The story is great and while giving you a decent amount of lives it can still be challenging as you can die very quickly and in rapid succession if you’re not careful. As I have not gone too far into the story I can’t comment anymore about it but i have picked up blue prints and I know there is an upgrade/blueprint mechanic. There is also a hub area on your ship where you select which mission youd like to do.
The fighting mechanics are some of the best I’ve ever seen in a game, just take a look at the videos. There is so much to learn how different weapons react to many different variables. Such as how you can shoot a grenade back at your opponent or how you can roll the bullets away. There is lots of freedom in movement which is great.
Now for the couch co-op/multiplayer/single player with AI games such as "death match" "plug slam" and "team strike" they are a ton of fun to play with others. in all these game modes you can select a starting character to keep things new and switch weapons out on the map. Also i forgot to mention, there is a very nice array of weapons.
-death match: your standard death match game as you would assume.
-plug slam: a 1 flag CTF style game mode but usually in a small area. Changed from the standard ctf mode of the ALPHA on decent sized maps, this new tweak seems to try to make the game faster paced. You spawn with a plug in the middle and try to "slam" it into the other person’s goal. This can be done by shooting it, throwing it, creating an explosion by it to propel it, or anything else this game allows you to do. You can also shoot the plug away from your own goal just as you can shoot grenades.
-team strike: a usual 8 player game mode where you get one life and can get upgrades on your class before each round with money from kills. a lot of fun and it makes you change up your play style a bit since you have one life. Probably my favorite game mode but i have not gotten too far into the tweaked new CTF game mode.
Challenge modes are also in the game. For the competitive player. There is leader board to see who has the highest combat score in combat challenges and fastest completion speed in speed challenges where you try to complete a level as fast as you can.
There is much more I could type about but this is the main points. I skipped over a lot. Check out the tutorial videos on the basic of "offence" and "defence" to see some more.

Idea Factory is the best Otome maker/provider. Amnesia:Memories has it all, different paths/dialogue/storylines - no repeats, the art is simply amazing, and the voice acting makes you melt-despite not understanding a word. I'm still waiting for the other Amnesia games to be translated & released in Steam (Later,Crowd, and World).

This is an otome with a pretty interesting premise. Yes, amnesia is an overdone story gimmick in video games, but here the game is actually built around the amnesia, rather than having it as a convenient way of hiding story elements to the player and make some cheap plot twist. The character has to regain her memories in order to obviously live a normal life, but also to kick a spirit out of her mind (I swear it makes sense... kinda).
What is nice is that the five main routes all happen in parallel universes (ok, here's another cliche, but much more used in comics than in video games), but they all connect to each other. Your relationships with the other characters change in the different universes, but if two of them are friends in a universe, they tend to be friends in the others, and to have somewhat similar personalities. The fifth route, where everything is explained, is pretty satisfying.
The art is very pretty, there are some very cute moments (I took way too many screenshots while playing this game), there is a nice mystery in all of the routes, and the writing, without being outstanding, is good. Plus, there are fun minigames, and I haven't played with the voiceovers for a very long time (it distracts me too much), but it was well done from what I heard.
However, there are a few issues. Within a route, there isn't a lot of branching. If you take very different decisions, the few following dialogues will vary, and maybe the ending will be different, but that's it. There are no different scenes other than that. Sure, you can skip the rest of the dialogues, but it still makes replaying a route not that worth it.
Then, between each of the five main routes (especially the first four routes), there's a lot of redundance. You always work at the same place with the same people, one of them as a lot of success with the ladies and has a dangerous group of fans, one of them is a mathematics genius, two are childhood friends, and so on. It's like being served more or less the same VN four times. I would have prefered four shorter stories that are more varied than those long stories that almost don't change.
Finally, speaking of redundancy, Amnesia has a recurrent theme: the borderline abusive boyfriend. Except for one of them (Kent, not the most loving guy, but at least the only decent one), they all have some kind of inappropriate relationship with the protagonist. Switching between the very emotional or melting moments and the ones where they treat you wrongly is a very messed up pattern. In every good ending, I'm mixed in a very bad way. I think "Well, this is a very happy and lovely moment... if you ignore how badly he treats me the rest of the time, but shhhhh". I know it's fiction and it's not meant to represent what should be reality, but it's bad that in a dating-sim game, I don't feel invested in the relationships, and even a lot reluctant.

While I have yet to finish every route the game has to offer (3/5 routes have been finished), I can say with certainty that this game is worth the buy. Last year, I bought this during the summer sale after learning that it was finally localized. This is one of these Otome games where it's highly reccommended that you play the character routes in a certain order for plot reasons. I didn't know this initially myself but that's what I came to learn after I started on Shin's route. I was glad I started with his route for the very reason that is the route you're supposed to start out with. This is the specific order that I reccommend to go in:
Shin (Heart)
Toma (Diamond)
Kent (Clover)
Ikki (Spade)
Then lastly, Ukyo. That's the route to do last no matter what since in every version except for Android, you have to unlock him by getting the normal endings of each characters. I have seen sites where it's reccommended that you go through Ikki's route 2nd then Toma's route 4th and you can't exactly go wrong with either or. It's very much like Mystic Messenger in this sense when it comes to doing the routes in order.
The art (done by: Hanamura Mai) is fantastic. There is no doubt that this artist has an abundance of experience under her belt, and ontop of that her style fits in well with the style of story. The colors are very vibrant as well, which adds to the wonderfulness that is Hanamura Mai's art. The voice acting is really good, you have so many amazing seiyus involved in this game that you're pretty much bound to recognize at least one of them or more. Every one of them did an amazing job in bringing the cast of characters to life. I must mention the characterization too is well done, with even fleshing out secondary characters instead of just making them well... side characters!
There isn't much to say as far as gameplay goes considering this is a visual novel otome first and foremost. Your dialogue options tend to determine what your ending is going to be, and I would say that works well, and is typical of a game like this. I do wish however that there would be more instances where you could have dialogue options. But since the main character has amnesia (not really a spoiler) it's only natural that she would be so quiet.
The only bad thing I can say is this... While it's better than nothing, this is the only Amnesia game that has been localized so far as of this review. I am hoping that soon maybe, the other games get localized as it would be nice to have every game easily accessible. It wouldn't be such a problem really if I was able to fluently able to speak + understand as well as being able to read Japanese. I'm not sure if this game got very much traction though here which may explain why there hasn't been any confirmation regarding the other games being released outside of Japan.
Overall, an amazing VN and Otome game

First, I would like to say that this was my first otome game and I started to play from a friend's library just spend some time with some light game. I ended up getting caught by the otome game world's cruel claws *being dramatic*. It is true in some sense because I couldn't stop myself playing it. And I ended up buying it, I didn't even wait for sale. In my opinion, it's worth every penny!
I was so curious with what's going to happen with the next choice or character. It is a very well written visual novel. Characters have some depths and are not some shallow love interests. Developer did very good job on that. Every character has some reason behind why they decided to act that way, some more convincing than others but still ok. And what's the most amazing thing for me is that the story is consistent in every possible character. It doesn't matter who you choose as your love interest other love interest that haven't chosen have the traits. It really gives parallel universe feeling, like you're exploring what could have been in other universe. And it was this kept me in this game.
The game start with the introduction of Orion, a spirit. By some unknown reason that you are not going to learn until you unlock last character, Orion trapped inside you and it caused you to lost your memories. He is your guide during the game. And by his suggestion, you're entering different parallel universes that can be the universe you're coming from on equal chances.
In this game, you have five love interests. You're choosing one of them when choose your "world". As soon as you choose the character, every choice you make lead you one of the good, bad, and normal endings. Every character has one good ending and can be intriguing to get. Luckily, there are plenty of walkthroughs on the internet. I happened to always get normal or bad ending on my own. Apart from that, every love interest has several normal and bad endings. Some bad endings can be shocking. I sometimes said "no way!" and it can be creepy. But it is just a game, isn't it?!
Overall, I highly recommend this game even if you never played otome before. It is story rich and it is not some game that you make every obvious decisions to end the game and get the guy. It's worth giving a shot.

TL:DR: This game gets worse every year, do not bother buying if you are an experienced player.
I have been playing every version of this game since 2008, with a decreasing level of enjoyment every year. This game contains most of the bugs from 2016 and older versions, while adding new, even worse bugs.
I pre-ordered this game and got to try it in its beta-state. As one could expect from a game in beta it had a lot of issues, with most of the "bugs" being gone once the full game dropped. One of the most glaring issues I noticed during the beta was that my defenders simply would not mark the players I assigned them to mark. This was a frustrating issue in 2016 already but this time it was on a whole new level. My players would initially stand on the wrong side of the player they were supposed to mark, meaning the (un)marked player could simply run towards my goal, get a pass and score. Not only this, but once the (un)marked player actually got the ball and ran towards my goal, my defender would jog (F*CKING JOG) like 3 meters behind him without even trying to catch him.
"No problem", I thought. "This will get fixed once the finished version drops". I went on the Sports Interactive forums and voiced my concerns with this "bug", only to be told by Sports Interactive employees that this issue was due to my players having low attributes on "concentration" and "marking" and what have you. I was pretty shocked, as I have never in my entire life seen a defender defend so poorly in a real game of football. Are the developers actually this clueless or will this be fixed when the game drops?
Fast forward to today, a few weeks after release. The "bug", which isn't even a bug by their logic, is still present in the game.
I could go on and on about other issues with this game, but most of them have likely been covered by others, and the issue that I mentioned is the one that breaks the game for me. As I stated in the beginning, I have played every version of this game since 2008, and I have watched it continually get worse. It is such a shame that a game that is so good outside of the match engine, has such a poor match engine. I told myself before playing the 2017 version that if this version is not better than 2016 it will be the last Football Manager game I purchase, and it increasingly looks like that will indeed be the case.

Ryse Son of Rome, kill dem barbarians in style, for Rome needs blood to wash its corruption!!!
I bought Ryse on sale without expecting anything more than an eye candy. However I got much more than that. Yes, obviously being on CryEngine it is an eye-candy, but it also transfers the atmosphere of the ancient Rome, the struggle for power and the code of honour of simple soldiers. In addition to that it is a hack and slash game with no combos, but rather QTE executions and fighting system based on reaction. The game is not hard, neither it is easy (on the last two difficulty levels). The game is not long enough to become repetitive (although executions are limited) and not too short to leave you unsatisfied.
There is also a co-op multiplayer Coliseum which is fun.
From historical point of view the game uses real historical personalities but puts them into a fictional scenario. For example those of you who loved Gladiator (the movie) will like the chapter where you have to fight through at the Coliseum to face and kill Commodus :)
There is also a replayability value in the game if you want to collect all the "secret" which will give extra insight into the main story or if you would like to experience the beauty of various settings in the game (oh yes, the graphics are really good)
Overall I would give this game 7/10, if you have a powerful Rig than it is definitely worth to buy on a sale

This game sports absolutely stunning visuals, that make both your character, his enemies as well as the environment in which you slaughter them a joy to look at.
The story is told in a nice way and remains interesting enough, even though it seemed a little rushed at the ending. Then again it wasn't story that brought me to this game but rather the violence and gore, which is where "Ryse: Son of Rome" really delivers.
Integrated into the combat system, which reminded me a little of Arkham Asylum's Free Flow combat are frequent executions of your enemies in the for of QTEs. As boring as they are to play, as fascinating theya are to look at, even after having seen each of them. There's quite a wide range of possible execution-"moves", including the possibility to vanquish two of your foes at once in various rather brutal and gory ways. Again, on maximum graphical settings, these are a joy to look at.
Although this oversimplifies the already easy combat it makes playing the single player campaign feel like playing a few episodes of the "Spartacus" series, or a 300 movie, though the game does not contain any sex scenes.
In addition to this the voice acting and soundtrack in both cutscenes and actual gameplay are superb and make for a really immersive atmosphere.
Unfortunately the singleplayer content ist very linear and took me only about 7hs to finish on my first playthrough; I might do another one to search the levels a little more closely for the various collectibles, however to me this still make the game seem a bit lacking in terms of replayability.
I have not tested the multiplayer modes of this game yet and thus, can't really write about them, though I hope that they might add a little more gametime to me.
All in all my first playthorugh was a very fun experience for me, but due to its high price and rather short length I would not recommend "Ryse: Son of Rome" at its full price. It's well worth it, if you can get it cheaper though.

Based on my first impressions, I cannot recommend this game. I don't have any inherent problem with the mechanics, but the content they're used in up to this point has been completely uninteresting. The only piece of content I found interesting so far is the first boss fight which I thought was a lot of fun. The rest is too straightforward to hold my attention. A lot of the combat encounters up to this point have just been "shoot stuff that either shoots from cover or from the air," (with the only stand out non-boss fight being one I just got to where you jump between platforms while fighting) or some more puzzle based encounters, but the puzzles are so simple and don't do anything to distinguish themselves from previous content. The "puzzles" aren't more than either "shoot this thing with electric bullets while dodging" or "move this bullet here while avoiding enemy bullets." There have been about 5 puzzles so far to do with the latter, but they haven't done anything interesting outside of the first.
These faults on their own almost certainly have to do with this being the opening of the game, but the game does not give me enough "aesthetic motivation" to make me want to get past this crawl of an opening. The artstyle isn't bad, but designs of everything is pretty bad. The idea is that the game takes place is a Wreck-it Ralph style world, but this results in a lot of the characters not standing out due to the fact they are all things I've seen before. I don't have an inherent issue with referrential humour, but there is a distinct lack of noticable major characters. Hell, the main badguy is just the main character of Gears of War who doesn't really stand out in his own game, let alone when just used as a reference. This is compounded with the boring level design and uninteresting backgrounds. You don't really have any platforming abilities and the focus of the game is on the combat and puzzles, which again is fine, but when you never really move along something other than a flat plain it not only becomes very noticable, but also very boring.
I don't recommend this game because I do not have motivation to play any more of this game, but I should stress that the game may very well get better. Once you get more types of bullets and gun mods, the amount of puzzles and interesting combat encounters are most certainly going to grow. This is essentially a warning more than anything that there is a slog you must get through before reaching the actualy fun bits.

A fun little shooter/puzzle hybrid that pays homage to the games of yesteryear, Rise & Shine is worth checking out if you're a fan of sidescrolling shooters and have a lot of nostalgia for video games in general.
PROS:
1) Stellar production values. The game's art design, music, and sound are all top-notch.
2) Tight controls. Everything feels as responsive and as impactful as it should.
3) A plot that, while simple, is still quite compelling and keeps you invested in the game.
4) Lots of references to classic games that feel organic to the world and just the right amount of tongue-in-cheek.
5) Clever puzzles that actually make you stop and think.
6) Steady progression system that throws new elements at you once you've learned the last few.
CONS:
1) The art design can make it hard to notice all the projectiles and attacks coming at you at certain points
2) Puzzle elements often feel separate from the combat and like they could have been combined better.
3) No checkpoints during boss battles, which can be frustrating
4) Some sections very much feel like trial and error
Overall this is a very enjoyable, memorable game that I could easily see myself coming back to.

I bought this game on the steam christmas sale. I have a bit to say about it both good and bad
*I only have the vanilla game, I have yet to grab the DLC*
Grand Strategy Games:
This is a genre that focuses a lot on complex and/or large strategy games that mostly involve a political simulator. Victoria 2 is a grand strategy that puts you in the shoes of the leader of any country from 1836 to 1936, the cusp of the second world war. This was known as the industial era for many countries and was also the time the British Empire had reached the hight of it's power.
The Grand Campain:
This is the main game. You start in 1831 and you can select any country that was around during that period. From there, you will make many decisions. Each country plays differently usually because of location, what state the country is in and the different government and ruling party types. Of course, some countries are stronger than others, so there is a ranking system for the world. Great Powers are the top 8 countries. Theen the secondary powers. Followed by civilized nations and uncivilized nations. Parts of the world are also still uncolinized like parts of Canada and most of Africa. Some countries like Germany, Italy and Norway as well as many more countries have still not been formed or are yet to gain independece from larger empires like the British.
Pros-
-Large list of countries to play as.
-Real events such as the American Civil War.
-A good UI that conveys all the information needed about your country.
- Can colonize to expand your lands
(Only Great Powers and Secondary Powers may colonize)
-Choices define what makes your empire. They are important. Most choices have advantages and disadvantages to choose your choices wisely.
-Can have rebellions in your country if peopleget too militant.
-Play at your own pace. Fast forwarding and pausing the game at any time.
-Lots of techs to research and inventions to discover, giving you different kinds of advantages.
-A decent tutorial to get you going.
Cons-
-A very steep learning curve if you are new to these kind of games.
(Does have a decent tutorial though)
-AI has a few problems sometimes, could have been fixed with DLC though.
- Bad multiplayer, it's hard to join other people and you can't just quick join random people. To join someone, you must register on the Paradox fourms or use a virtual network like Hamachi.
-Hard to keep track of world events. You can set certain catagory events to pop up if you like but a lot of events wont pop up by deafault, they just happen.
Can't think of what else to say about the game other than it's fun to see where you can go by just choosing some interesting countries and trying to develope them into whatever you want. For example, I played as britain and released Ireland from the british empire and then decided to play as Ireland since I am Irish ha. I began to tax people severly to improve my econemy and so I began buying weapon parts. I began to build transport ships and recruit and army and then I invaded Malaysia. Tried to invade surrounding nations but the world quickly turned on me. America, Russia, Britain, France all declared war on me and they quicky arrived on Irish soil. The purpose of the war was to contain me and I agreed within a couple of months and so I lost a huge portion of my army. Oh well... I got Ireland pretty far in terms of inustry in the end with a booming economy as well. I got from rank 55 to 30 in the end but oh well. Now, I am ploting my revenge and my plan for world domination xD
Verdict, 8/10. Pretty damn good, but has a few problems.
*Again, note that I have none of the DLC for this game. The game might easily be a 9/10 with a couple of it's problems fixed*

Based on an interesting synthetic genre idea (Tetris+Match 3+Clicker) and nicely designed, this game demands grasping vision of the current board geometry, quick reflexes & precision (in which regard it also reminds me of Minesweeper's gameplay: choosing proper squares from a gigantic array).
The board rotates on demand, so that you can choose the direction blocks fall & you kinda ougth to watch the field from all sides simultaneously to achieve effectiveness. You have to predict the spots where the blocks could gather into 4-squares and chain-connect to bring you more points, clicking on stray blocks just allows you to empty space for the upper ones to fall. The tasks use timer and you have to be a really quick clicker too & if you miss a square you'll sometimes spoil yourself a combo.
The main problem is that the incoming colors are random & the success largely depends on luck, so that you might need to replay a task like 100+ times to pass through. Those little girl's cheerful voice samples that seem adorable at first become a torture to your nervous system in a while. So I can't recomment it to a normal player, only hardcore puzzle gamblers will find satisfaction here.

Данная игра, будучи основана на интересной комбинации идей (Тетрис+3 в ряд+Щелкалка) и приятно сделана, требует цепкого восприятия геометрии на игровом поле, быстрой реакции и точности (в последнем отношении она напомнила мне Сапера: выбор правильных клеток из большого массива).
Игровое поле вращается по требованию, так что можно выбирать направление падения блоков, и вам необходимо как бы наблюдать доску одновременно со всех сторон, чтобы играть эффективно. Следует предвидеть места, в которых квадратики могут собраться в большие квадраты по 4 и соединиться в цепи, принося больше очков, а щелкая по отдельным клеткам мы лишь освобождаем пространство для падения верхних блоков. Задания на время, так что необходимо также очень быстро щелкать, а вот если разок промахнетесь, можете испортить себе всю комбинацию.
Основная проблема в том, что вновь образующиеся цвета случайны, и успех в большой степени зависит от удачи, так иногда приходится переигрывать задание по 100 с лишним раз пока не свезет. А эти звуковые эффекты с радостным голосом девочки, поначалу милые, становятся со временем настоящей пыткой для нервов. В общем, я не могу рекомендовать игру нормальному игроку, лишь самые азартные головоломочные профи найдут здесь удовлетворение.

Play as commander keen! As he avoids terrible vegetable aliens and catholic priests out to molest him. This game was a revolutionary stepforward in computer graphics, as Id software found out a way to create parallax scrolling for the PC. PC gaming was never the same afterwards.

I'm not too keen about this compliation. While I could give credit to ID for creating one of the first PC side-scrollers, I will say that this has not aged well at all, and not only do you get killed in one hit by everything, but there is also absoultely no way you can give yourself a health powerup that can give a little leeway towards being damaged by enemies.  The backgrounds in episodes 1-3 are incredibly dull, and it feels like I'm playing a launch Atari 5200 game. To make matters even worse, you have a lives counter, and in a game like this, you will get so many game overs that you will want to destroy your computer, and play the Japanese Super Mario Bros. 2 on the NES instead. If you want an old PC sidecroller really bad that doesn't tear you into pieces and is vomit-inducing, I would go with just the original Duke Nukem, and avoid the second one, as that one is unforgiving compared to the first. If I were you, I'd buy Sonic the Hedgehog, or any other Sega Genesis classic here instead, you won't regret it.

Being one of the first games, I ever played, Commander Keen is the PC equivalent of Super Mario. You jump, run and shoot your way through 2D levels, avoiding traps, gaps and monsters.
Being an oldschool game, the difficulty is sometimes a little bit silly.
While 4, 5 and 6 had mid save options, in 1 - 3 you could only save in the main area, not inside levels. Combined with nearly unkillable powerjumping...we called them Zombie kangaroos...this game is quite a number of difficulty.
After the 4th part you also got a difficulty option, that enables traps and increase the amount of monsters.
Beside that, the game has a little ongoing story about the main character, explaining him and why he is doing all that (genius child, build a blaster and a rocket ship with parts of his familys home).
(PS: Every game has at least one hidden area and level)
The bad part about the bundle (yes its 5 games in one), that it is missing the last 2 games. 6 was a special limited edition (who limits a game???) and 7...we dont talk about 7.
The story doesnt end with 6 or 7 ether, so fans made Keen 7 (denying the existence of the real keen 7), Keen 8 and Keen 9, who look quite decent and end the Keen story for good. Check it out on Youtube.
Solid sprucing up of the originals.

I bought this game on Jan 2nd 2012
After a long dev process and failed promises of linux and MacOS ports,  admin abuse of stupid forum rules that almost eroded any remaining community surrounding the game beyond the devs themselves.. and the acquisition of Oxeyes parent company by Microsoft. We have Cobalt.
It is a wonder that this game ever made it through development and despite my gripes with the team involved, they obviously love the game and have put their heart and soul in to it. The game now features a story mode with lots of hidden secrets, great puzzles and some very geeky if not a little clunky, dialogue.
Multiplayer can be a really fun experience of total mayhem, and yet I have still always enjoyed my solo runs more. Take from that what you will, but Cobalt as an experience definitely has a lot to offer.
Worth noting that I have a controller and yet choose to play with the keyboard, so don't let the prospect of that deter you.
I believe this is a game that could have benefited from steams EA program  but I understand why they didn't or couldn't go for it.. Especially after how rigidly they policed development through their own medium, I can imagine had they been so totalitarian on the steam forums this game would have a bag of negative reviews already.
That being said as a new comer you don't need to have any dealing with Oxeye at all. This is a finished product and while arguably a tad overpriced at this point (I paid closer to £5, 4 years ago). I still feel it an easy recommendation to those intrigued by the prospect of a skill based side scroller.

An excellent 3PS game, with a lengthy campaign, and online play support. Lost Planet 2 is the second entry into the Lost Planet franchise.
PROS:
-lengthy campaign. For those of us casuals who like long single player campaigns, this game does not disappoint. The levels are intense and gripping, and actually fairly difficult.
-sound effects are on-point. I love the sound of the machine gun firing. I could listen to it all day. The weapon sound effects are spot-on. the grappling sound is perfect. Just in general, this game has audio nailed down.
-combat is intense. You will blaze through levels, shooting up anything that comes in your path. The boss fights take actual skill and strategy to work (most of the time), though there are the occasional few that you can just hammer with an RPG launcher until they die. Combat system works well, and doesn't need much improvement. AI isn't half bad. Could be better, but not embarrassing.
*I don't have much knowledge about multiplayer, seeing as how I only recently got this, and need to completely set up my Windows Live account to play online. Sorry*
CONS:
-Windows Live. Unless you want to spend a bit of time finnagling Windows Live stuff, you will be unable to save progress in this game. I know that other reviews tell you how to set up a functioning Windows Live account, and I am in the process of doing so myself. If you do take the time to set one up, it's certainly worth it :)
That's all I can think of for pros and cons. The game itself is surprisingly well-polished, and I enjoy the feel of combat a lot. Boss battles are engaging, but don't generally take more than 20-30 minutes at most (as far as I've played). Game doesn't look poor, or run badly, or anything like that. All in all, an excellent shooter game, that I would recommend to anyone. All you gotta do is take the time to set up a Windows Live account, and you're golden!

NOTE: This review is only evaluating the game concerning its single-player merits.
You know that scene from the movies, right? Where the new kid in school gets introduced in front of the class, and everyone looks at him/her with a mild mixture of disinterest and disdain? That’s how I felt when I started up Lost Planet for the first time. The game is all like „Oooh, look at our multiplayer content! Shiny! Now grab some friends and play this game how we want you to, DAMMIT!“ My reply: „But… I want to play a single-player campaign. Is this possible, too?“ The game averts its gaze, annoyed: „Yeah, I guess… freak.“
The game constantly hits you over your head with the fact that it’s really meant to be played in multi-player. For single-player fans, this makes things awkward. Where do I start? What about the AI stand-ins that accompany you, with silly “gamertag” names over their heads all the time? The “Battle Gauge” system, which is basically a multi-player “army strength” system? A system that respawns you right back into the running game without resetting to a checkpoint, complete with a respawn countdown? The team zones at the end of the levels, which are red boxes that all players – human and AI – have to be inside to complete the mission? Or that the game rewards you for using gestures in these team zones? I could go on and on, but you get the point. For single-player modes, immersion is key, and this game’s insistence on its multi-player infrastructure is a major immersion-killer.
But even if you are able to ignore this, there are still the absence of a noteworthy story and the jarring transitions. As you are a part of an actually-meant-for-multiplayer squad, there is no real protagonist, a detriment which is exasperated by the fact that you switch back and forth through multiple squads belonging to different parties during the course of the campaign. This wouldn’t be bad if each squad was somehow distinct, but this isn't the case. They are all faceless soldiers. No, literally, they are all wearing masks or helmets all the time! Then, there are the transitions, a problem which was already present in the first game. Episodes which should be one consistent sequence of levels connected by cutscenes are always broken up into artificial “missions”. And it gets worse: A tense shootout against enemy dropships ends in the middle of combat because an arbitrary “energy bar” hit zero – with ships still in the air!
All these things amount to the game’s greatest sin: Its clumsy and wasteful handling of its setpieces. Here’s where I have something positive to say about the game: Lost Planet 2 features a collection of stunning setpieces. Really, they are as epic as you can get. If they had been used by someone who knows how to craft a good single-player game, this could have been an action blockbuster for the ages. However, the dire reality is that without a meaningful story and an immersive presentation, these setpieces remain fragments without significance or emotional impact.
If you’re looking for an opinion about the multi-player component of Lost Planet 2, please consult a review addressing this aspect. However, if you look for a great single-player experience, stay away. It’s sadly not worth the effort.
