I'm really divided about this Rise & Shine. The game is so charming, yet frustrating.
The first chapter of the game is really good: nice puzzles, new abilities, new enemies. After having enjoyed it you will probably wonder what's next, how they are capable to evolve such a good formula.
Well, unfortunately, they aren't. The second part is just boring. Uninteresting story, no new abilities, no puzzles, boring "defense" sections, no easter eggs and frustrating boss fights.I really forced myself to play until the end twice (a playtrough 2-3 hours.)
The game do not deserve a thumbs down cause they put a lot of love (and art) in the first part, but hell, buy it on sale.

I also covered this game on YouTube:
The easiest way to describe Rise & Shine is if you took something like Limbo or Inside, added a whole bunch of colour, combat and gave it a simply told story set in a video game world.
I requested review code for this simply based on a trailer that showed off its incredible art style and that it was a platformer. I got a very different experience than I expected and while I was generally pleased, you should know what you're getting into first. Like Limbo or Inside, Rise & Shine is very short (I beat the story on normal mode and got about half the secrets in just over 2 hours) but each of its levels or "scenes" are exquisitely crafted to deliver a particular experience a certain way. Some are better than others and the story that ties it all together is a little basic and doesn't do nearly enough with some of the characters it introduces, but it holds things together well enough.
Most of what you'll experience in Rise & Shine is a puzzle of some sort, either an environmental one or a combat scenario where you have to figure out the best way through. You will die a
but it's also to be expected and checkpoints are frequent and usually pretty generous. While the art style is cartoony and cute, this is also a game that doesn't pull punches with gore, though it's usually presented in a hilarious way. I wouldn't call Rise & Shine hard in the sense that most players probably won't give up due to the difficulty but it certainly will challenge you in places.
The art in Rise & Shine is simply some of the best 2D artwork I've seen in a long time. This game is gorgeous and the sheer amount of art and in particular, unique art is amazing. Everything is colourful, exquisitely detailed and animates very smoothly. The original soundtrack also helps keep energy and pacing up and fits well. There's no voice acting, except for little one-word grunts, denoting who is talking in the also gorgeous comic book style still cutscenes. While the writing doesn't necessarily do as well as it could to bond you with the characters, they do a great job at conveying emotion and weight.
Rise & Shine is an expensive 2 hours for many at $15. There are many collectables, plus a Hardcore mode that unlocks once you've finished the game but unless you plan to 100% all that stuff, this is short. But so are Limbo and Inside and they're considered indie masterpieces. This doesn't do as good a job at storytelling as either of those (though I'm one of the few who think Inside is 2016's most overrated game by far) but it's presentation is second to none and it takes the formula of those games and manages to add engaging combat challenges to the mix and creates an incredible, gorgeous world to play in.
Even if I hadn't received review code for Rise & Shine, I would have been happy with it at $15. But if your gaming budget is limited and you need your dollars to provide as many hours of entertainment as possible, you'd probably be wise to wait for a sale, as you would also for Limbo or Inside. If you have the means and like this type of game though, this is a great one of those and shows how the platforming subset Playdead created can be expanded in cool new ways that I hope more developers try.

Let me start by saying that this is a fun game. That being said, Lost Planet 1 is a much superior game. The problem is they focused so much on the multiplayer aspect that it leaves the game lacking. Plus the game is good but not great. The story is all over the place and your AI suck. It was meant to be co op but the game is so old that the community is pretty much dead. If the map is big your AI wander around doing nothing. Plus the game has the lost planet 1 problem in that there is no running. You go everywhere at a leisurely pace. Also the game does not nearly have enough mech combat which is what made the first game such a major success. I don't think this game was worth the 5 bucks I spent but at least the game has some good length with a 10 hour campaign. The problem is because it’s a multiplayer co op game; you can't save the game until you finish the entire mission. Worse, you can't even pause it! This means you have to devote a half an hour to an hour to the game without stopping. Also you can't get the really good weapons unless you get lucky in their lame slot machine. Now don't get me wrong, I had a lot of fun playing it. I think it was a major letdown from the first game and they could have done better. In its prime this was probably a great game but now it’s just a relic. Honestly, I didn't want to pay five bucks but that was a cheap as it would go and I want to play the whole franchise. I'll probably end up paying 6 bucks for Lost Planet 3. A great game but it is sadly very aggravating.

Played this game on the xbox few years ago.  To this day, the game still holds up.  The graphics, gameplay, and fun-factor (whatever that means) is still holding up. The only reason I have this game is because it came together in a free package deal when buying my new video card.  I had happy memories of the original Dungeon Siege and Dungeon Siege II; so I was excited to play this to finish my collection as I always wanted it, but never got around to it.
15 minutes in I was feeling sick. I mean, Dungeon Siege was always a generic fantasy setting but had a charming 1980's D&D feel. This was just so bland, and I dare say the Dungeon Siege movie was more visually inspired than this game.
The graphics look good at first, but the animations of the first NPC you run into is just cartoonish puppet looking and  uncanny valley at the same time.
The lipsync was terrible, the eyes of NPC's dead and souless. Combine this with lack luster voice acting...I just couldn't get invested.
First impressions are important, and it did not impress, but I continued playing further. An hour in and I still found myself exiting the game to play something else because I was bored. I couldn't be hooked!
However, the major killer of this game is the camera, damn thing is clunky when being adjusted. It also turns so fast and wildly around making you sick and is never in a tactical advantageous position.
Also seeing how Dragon Age Origins came out a couple years before Dungeon Siege III, I couldn't help but compare the two. The graphics, animation, gameplay, camera and interface was just lackluster compared to a simliar sword and sorcery fantasy RPG. It feels like a cheap product trying to lure in some of the same audience by the way they were marketing this game and hyping it.
Some might say I have nostalgia glasses, but I have nothing against a game franchise trying out different styles so long as it's good or enjoyable. I got together some distant friends who were not familiar with the Dungeon Siege series, but were familiar with other RPG's or avid players and they too were unimpressed even as casual gamers.
I later learned from a review by Ross Scott of Accursed Farms; that one of the key and unique features of Dungeon Siege, it's large party system which could include up to eight party members active at one time, was not present. Having bombastic large melee's was one of the most memorable and fun things about Dungeon Siege and it's gone. Well, that killed any chance of me picking up the game again.
I uninstalled it and I wish I could delete it from my library.
I don't even want my money back; I just don't want to remember owning or playing this.
I have vivid memories of playing this on floppy discs when I was 5. Buy it!

There are few pleasures in gaming more potent than conquering a tough encounter through sheer endurance. If you can handle a game’s trial and error, succeeding after countless failed attempts can be exhilarating and propel you forward towards the next challenge, and you come out at the end as a master of that game’s various mechanics. This style of design flourished around the 16-bit era, with SNES and Genesis titles that were overly difficult due to a multitude of factors. Super Mega Team’s Rise & Shine harkens back to those days without being overly punishing, creating an authentic 16-bit experience surrounded by a lavish modern presentation. Simply put, there is a lot of beautiful art to take in and plenty of combat puzzles to solve if you can get past a multitude of references and a questionable run time.

I first played Rise & Shine back in December 2015 and I ended the demo with a sense that the game was going well and was due out early 2016. Well we are now in early 2017 and finally, the game seems to be seeing the light of day.
Back in 2015, we spoke about how fantastic the demo was and how gorgeous the game was and how the soundtrack rocked. Well, all of that is still true but unfortunately, the harsh reality is there is not really much more here than was in the demo over a year ago.
The game is short lasting about 3-4 hours for a playthrough and if it was not for the case the game is very difficult then it would be over even faster. And therein lies the larger problem in that while a game being really difficulty is not an issue Rise and Shine (particularly in the second half) is difficult for all the wrong reasons.
Firstly, the controls. I said back in my original preview that playing the game with a controller was an absolute must. Well, mouse and keyboard controls have been improved since then but still the controls in the game as fiddly and you never quite feel like you are in total control and for a game that relies so much on pinpoint accuracy that is a problem. The other issue is changing between gun modes. So, you have 2 different types of the bullet which are physical and electric and each of those can be fired in 3 different way (normal, guided or explosive) and the main issue is that you have 2 buttons to do this. One to switch between the type of bullet and one to switch between how it is fired and when completing some of the game’s later challenges this mechanism is incredibly fiddly. The other slight issue is that when firing you can only move very slowly and this also is a problem. Imagine playing a bullet Hell game such as Radiant Silvergun where you had to be still while shooting. It just makes the game ‘less fun’.
Visually, however, the game is gorgeous and there is a lot of fun references in here for gamers but I did expect so much more than there is and to be honest I feel like the game has not greatly progressed since the demo I played well over a year ago.
Rise and Shine has a lot of heart and I am sure there are some people out there that will truly love it but this is definitely far from the must by classic we had hoped for.

Well, whatever.  I recommend this game, with serious reservations.

I was enjoying this game up until a point.
That point is right after you visit NPC Island and the game decides its going to go all out on the difficulty level and just be a merciless, frustrating, headdesking, frustration-fest.
Up until this point, the game has been content with giving up numerous ways to upgrade your 2 types of ammo capacity, but never a way to increase Rise's health (or provide any other survivability buffs whatsoever). This is a problem in this game considering that it's essentially a bullet-hell platformer that requires precise movement, use of cover and and switching between ammo all while trying to avoid charging enemies and a hail of fire.
The dual-stick fire controls coupled with having to switch between different types of ammo means that Rise has to limit his movement every time he wants to switch ammo types or even aim, making things all the more difficult.
I was attracted to this game because of its art style, nods to retro games and bullet-hell, ammo switching mechanics (I love Ikaruga) but the game makes things way to hard on the player by limiting their mobility and giving them no way to quickly switch to different ammo combinations (you have to cycle your bullet-type and your firing type).

A very fun, action-packed game that, to this day, still has a true competitive scene, and consistent updates. All the characters feel unique, some of which are voice acted by youtube celebrities (Skolldir: Simon Lane (Yogscast), Raelynn (Dodger: Presshearttocontinue), Vinnie and Spike (Totalbiscuit), and Genji (Jesse Cox)). The entire game feels incredibly fluid, and is a fantastic stand out to the MOBA scene. The 2D aspect may seem like a negative, but it actually turns this game into a frenzy of combat in easy-to-navigate maps.
Pros
-Awesomenauts are plentiful and original
-Every "naut" has their own upgrades, some of which have significant effects.
-Amazing soundtrack. Very Jazzy, and every naut has a theme that plays during a killing spree.
-Many nauts are easy to play, but require lots of practice to master
-Maps are fairly plentiful, each with an interesting mechanic or two.
-Has a leveling, and a prestige, system to progress and complete
-Full of humorous, and perfectly placed, references.
Cons
-Numbers, while being significant, do not feel significant. You may be absolutely destroying your foes...but hitting a 40 feels a bit weak.
-Leveling system is a bit strange* (explained later)
*The leveling system involves collecting leftover "solar" at the end of a match, and using it to advance in levels (starting at one, going up to currently 155). Almost every level has the reward of a new upgrade to potentially buy for one of the nauts. At max level, you have the option to prestige, giving a new icon, and resetting your level back to 16 (preserving all nauts and maps unlocked).
You will almost always level at least twice, even against bots. The loss of all those upgrades, and some nauts, makes prestige feel like shooting yourself in the foot. Many upgrades feel incredibly fun on some nauts, but some of the best are locked further into the leveling. If you think a shiny icon is worth 10-20 hours of leveling, go for it (you can prestige up to 10 times.)

I love being able to play a game focused on world events 100 years prior to WW2, it lets you get great insight into how the World wars came about and how a lot of the foundations for other countries around the world came to be. Even though the game isn't 100% historically correct, it still tries to implement a lot of the big events that happened in the world between 1836 - 1936. You can take control of any country you want, be it an already Great Power, or perhaps a secondary power that wishes to achieve Great Power status or even a lesser developed country from the more remote parts of the world, which can perhaps even achieve Great Power status. The game is very varied, the great powers are always going to be more predominent in the worlds affairs but even great powers can fall to their knees sometimes.
The micro-management of everthing from factories, to the economy, to the politics, influencing other countries, as well as focusing on military production, is very in-depth and has a steep learning curve, but once mastered, can make the game so much more enjoyable.
I really recommened buying the 2 dlc expansions for Victoria II, they add so much to everything in the game, and they iron out heaps of bugs. The Heart of Darkness expansion is particulary good, it adds the "Crisis Mode" to the game, which just adds a whole new level of diplomatic and militaristic events to the game.
Overall, the game is great, and there is plenty of replayability to the game as you will always be wanting to go back and perhaps try a slightly different tactic to change the future of the world!
I give it a 9/10, the game can get quite memory/hard drive intensive as the game goes on and world powers suddenly have massive militaries to command.
I recommend 8gb of ram for this game and if you have an ssd, even better!

Do you like spreadsheets? What about the endless waiting and worrying over external threats that comes from the futility of contemplating one's existance as a less developed country?
In all seriousness, Victoria II is a great game, and stands as one of the most solid Paradox developed games. If you are just getting into the Grand Strategy genre after playing Crusader Kings II or Europa Universalis IV, then some features may be intimidating at first. There is micromanaging present in both of those games, but probably not to the extent that you are likely to experience when playing Vicky. Like all Paradox games there is a pretty steep learning curve, but this should not discourage you as there are loads of helpful tutorials online.
You will almost surely start the game try to learn the game as a fairly small nation and end up getting crushed by some event that will seem quite obvious down the line. Try Brazil if you are just starting out. They are a fairly easy nation for learning the base mechanics (using some gamey tactics to take easy uncivilized nations in Africa), but offer a nice challenge in the late game as one usually ends up competing for regional supremacy with the USA.
If you're still not convinced, here are some cool things that I have seen during some of my playthroughs:
Japan won a war against the Ottomon Empire, and ended up controlling the Hejaz including the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.
USA POPs revolted and left the USA controlling only the western portion of the country. The Confederates controlled the South, while the Free States of America controlled the north and had replaced the USA as the continental Great Power.
Poland was released in a Great War and promptly proceeded to take up boundaries almost exactly proportional to the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
PROS:
1. Maps are nice to look at.
2. The unstoppable historical events (think the Mongol invasions of CK2, to a lesser extent) add a structure to the madness that is a Grand Strategy game.
3. It is fun to take historically insignificant entities and create a narrative that establishes them as being a dominant power.
CONS:
1. State control of the means of production ends up feeling like a spreadsheet simulator.
2. Game slows down considerably in later years and is especially slow on a lot of laptops.
3. You will probably 100x more games than you actually finish

Cool short little MGS game (WARNING: don't expect a full game).  I'm s big MGS fan and I've been waiting for Konami to release another game to the series.  So if you're a MGS fan I'd highly recommend this to you.  But this could still be fun for you even if you're new to the franchise and you like stealth/action games.
Pros: You get to revisit the MGS franchise on PC, the game has great optimization (even some low end cards can max it out), great gameplay letting you choose different playstyles as in almost every stealth action game, gives you a bit of a challenge even on normal difficulty (if you're into that), the graphics are decent but not as good as some of the other games out there today (which I'm perfectly fine with if it runs well).
Cons: Story lasts one mission then basically tells you to go buy the Phantom Pain when it comes out (although there are some additional side missions you can play), game locks at 60 fps which I don't see as that bad of a problem since most people will be playing on 60hz monitors anyways.
But overall I'd rate this game 9/10 and I'd say it's well worth that $20.

The Metal Gear franchise has been around for a long time. If you grew up playing Metal Gear Solid on the PS1 like myself then you will feel right at home here. I have to admit my review may be bias because I consider the first MGS to be my favorite game of all time. I played it during my teenage years and it made me fall in-love with video game story telling.
With all that being said this is not a "FULL" game. This is a glorified tech-demo/prologue to the up-coming MGSV:Phantom Pain. This by all means isn't something that will keep you busy for 30+ hours. Not saying it won't keep you for awhile if you're into 100% completions like I am with this series.
There is plenty to do if you're a die-hard MGS fan. So I'm only going suggest this game to fans of the series. If however you have an extra 13-20 dollars laying around and like the idea of a free-roam (in a smaller space) stealth/action with a decent starting point for a story then by all means BUY IT. Also if you plan on buying Phantom Pain, you will need to play this game to get the full scope of whats going on.
Story: 9/10 (so far so good on Hideos part and looking good on the set-up to phantom pain, which will most likely being another amazing emotional ride)
Graphics/Visuals: 10/10 (some of the best looking lighting you will see in a game, aslong as you have a nice GPU/CPU combo you will be in for a visual treat un-matched by 99% of gaming has to offer.)
Gameplay: 9/10 (very rarely there are camera problems where it seems like the camera is too close and hindering your view, works great on a xbox 360 controller aswell as mouse/keyboard)
PC Optimization: 9/10 (lots of options and customization to get the most out of your hardware. Would like to see a better option for depth of field which I've found out turning it to "Low" stops the blur effects and makes the game look better. I don't know why turning an option down makes the game look better, but it does)
Overall: 9.5/10 Amazing game with very few to no flaws. Short maybe 10-20 hours of gameplay, longer only if you want to complete everything. Reports state that Phantom Pain will have over 200 hours of gameplay. So its fine with me if this one is short if PP is going to be insanly long and complex.
TL:DR: Buy this game if you are a MGS Fan boy or Want a short but sweet stealth/action thriller with a great story set-up to Phantom Pain.
PS: Game Devs... stop using Depth of Field and Motion Blur it's a cheap tactic to make plebs think something looks great but really doesn't. I know this feature was probably added for low-tier hardware (consoles) to make it look good even on low settings. People with High-Tier hardware should have an option to turn it completly off without losing out on other features like reflections.
Had this been a full game I would honestly like it. But sence it was advertised as a full game but is only a demo, I will not be buying any more metal gear games.

When crafting Terraria badges, I happened to get a 75% off coupon for this game. I had never even heard of this game before, so I went in open-minded. I expected it to be a puzzle game, and I was not dissapointed.
First of all, this game is extremely Japanese, so if that's not your thing, stay away. After installing this game and playing it for a small period of time, I can safely say I'm hooked. I was cautious about the game at first, but after playing it, I think the game is worthwhile anyone's time who enjoys a classic MMORPG. I'll break down the pro's and the con's of the game, and explain why they are in their respective places.
The Pro's:
1.) There are no classes. You create your own class through the talent system and various abilities you learn as you level.
2.) The game is very punishing in terms of not respecting mobs. Especially "elite", "champion", or "boss" mobs.
3.) The game feels very interactive with you and your character, very rarely are you not doing something while in combat from my experience.
4.) The game is complex, and not in a bad sense, but in terms of that the game doesn't hold your hand past the tutorial, and you have a lot of information to understand and process in order to play efficiently and effectively.
5.) There is plenty to do, between quests, events, professions, dungeons, etc.
6.) The game has a very small community. This can be a good or bad thing depending on preference, however, because of this, you make friendships with other players very easily, and for the most part, all of the players are very helpful, respectful, and welcoming of new players.
7.) The game doesn't feel like a stereotypical MMORPG Grindfest. This may be more relating to the fact that the combat is very interactive in the game.
8.) No pay to win garbage. Nearly everything from the cash shop can be purchased with in-game gold at some point or another. (Gold to Paid-Currency Ratio is about 1:3) All of the items from the cash shop are either purely cosmetic, or serve such a minimal purpose, it doesn't impact you.
9.) The graphics. I know plenty of people will disagree with me here, but I do enjoy the simplicity of the game's art-style. It's very original and appealing to look at. It's not an overly-glamorous professional graphics design, with high resolution textures and models. Whilst, I do like very high-end graphics, and I give full respect for those who can do such, it's become the norm. Therefore, it's nothing special. These graphics, however, are, in my opinion.
10.) The questing isn't linear. I can't go from level one to max level running in basically a straight line.
The Con's:
1.) (Intended or not) There [appears] to be an issue with auto-attacking where it must remain on your action bars, and you must use the action-slot that it's in, in order to auto-attack. This is not significant in any way, shape, or form, and is only a personal qualm of mine.
2.) Not being able to track multiple quests at once can be a tad tedious at times, but it's nothing significant.
3.) There appears to be quite a few issues with collision boxes on some in-world items. (I.E: Trees, boxes, etc.)
4.) Updates are few and far in between, which, can be a good or bad thing, depending on the way you look at it. It's good if you are a casual player trying to progress to max level, it will give you quite a length of time to get there and not feel the rush or obligation to do so as soon as humanly possible. It's bad if you are already at the end-game, and are sitting on your hands with nothing to do, assuming you've accomplished every thing possible up to that point.
Overall? I give this game a 10/10 in honesty. The cons are so insignificant it truly doesn't impact the gameplay enough for me to want to dilute my rating of the game.
TL;DR - If you get past the graphics, if you are a graphics junkie, the small community, and lack of updates, then this game is for you.

Let me start this Early Access review by reminding everyone it is early access. A lot of the things that might have put others to give no recommendation I might take as something that comes with early access. Do NOT expect a finished, documented and polished game. Expect some fun though.
Short list of pros and cons, again most might not be applicable because they're simply lack of documentation or effort by server owners:
PROS
* Fun concept (Basically Hunger Games: The Game, but more fun than it sounds)
* Replayability
* Looks gorgeous
CONS
* Bad performance
* Hardly any documentation
* Bad standard server settings given (which is what causes the Lobby issues)
* Still feels like a mod instead of standalone game
* Bugs, tweaks and the general stuff
It really is a lot of fun to get dropped in and play this game. You get beamed down (and that looks remarkably awesome) with all your other survivors (tributes) and 90% of the people runs to the supplies in the middle while a few people instantly turn around and waddle into the jungle. Within 2 minutes 10 people have died and then the game truly starts. A bunch of people take up the strategy of getting all their resources and levels in order, a bunch of other guys take up the strategy of running naked after people with spears and the last group of people are running away naked from people who carry spears. Fun right?
Apart from a timer bringing a Ring of Death closer and closer to the middle of the island where you spawned you are free to do what you want. There is just one certainty and that is that the Ring of Death will end up in the middle. What you do inbetween is basically Ark: Survival Evolved. Just trying to prepare for the fight at the end.
Now there are a whole bunch of reasons why this game might not be a-okay to you. If you don't like the concept that's a big no whatever happens. Most of the other reasons are because it's Early Access, that doesn't mean it's a bad game but just that you might prefer full games instead of being an alpha tester (as is your good right and probably a proper sane decision). The standard server settings given for all modes contain some typos and bad settings which leads to endless lobbies and games never starting. Some settings aren't really properly tweaked. To be honest I blame the server owners for that instead of the developers, if you feel like owning a server is just starting the software and never even checking how it runs or checking your log you might be better as a player instead.
The performance is bad. SLI isn't properly supported but if I force it in I get about 15-35 FPS with SLI 760's. Can only hope optimization is a big point later down the development process for the developers.
I haven't met any gamebreaking bug yet, just the occasional getting ported through a rock, a dinosaur stuck in a rock and a tree not sure which side to fall to. No terrible bugs on my side but something to remind you this game is not finished yet.
It really does look like a mod though, basically the mod baked into Ark: SE and shipped like that. One man tribes need to be created in Free For All mode due to how Ark handles dinosaurs and objects. A standalone game wouldn't have those dependancies, would it? Here I can only hope they will make it more stand alone. Just hoping that instead of just building onto the Ark base they will also modify the Ark base where it's relevant for this game instead of working around it.
So: are you not annoyed by some bugs, can stand a bit of waiting on a lobby (or finding out the server settings are bad), have a high-end pc or don't mind playing a tad lower fps than you are used to and like the concept? Then you should play this.
Only like the concept: probably better if you wait a bit.
Don't like all those things at all: what are you even doing on the store page of such a game!?

As a long time fan of the series and SI, having played their CM games and all of the FM titles, I have to be honest and share a summary review that truly represents a feeling of disapointment I have as well as most of the long time fans.
FM is obviously the best football simulationg game, it has incredible features overall. But speaking about FM17... You might as well keep playing FM16. I bought it and I honestly feel that if things next year don't improve A LOT this was the last one. A lot of things can be said about the game but I'll just focus some major aspects:
1) The match engine hasn't improved at all. AI is still glitchy, I cannot understand how 1 year after we still get the same poor experience in terms of realism. "Added motion control movements to players"... this ins't FIFA, the goal should be achieving greater match realism/experience. Movement of players is clunky and it's almost as if your tactical decisions mean nothing... Your opponent can have a lone striker and play defensively, you focus on that player, mark him, close him down, build a powerful scheme... And yet he scores a hat-trick! Say again?
You can play and dominate a game against your opponent with 70% ball possession, 30 shots on goal, etc... and yet you're opponent who only shoots 3 times, scores all those times and you lose the match 1-3?
You can have games between two top league teams that end with results such as 7-6.... 5-0... Absolutely ridiculous. And these are just a couple of examples.
2) The social feed... This new feature adds zero to the game. What was the purpose of spending time doing this? You always get a couple positive and a couple negative comments. It will not affect your decision making at all... Just useless.
3) SI should've improved the realism in contract/transfer negotiations by now... This has been addressed by fans for a long time. Agents demand unrealistic bonuses that can largely surpass the bonus for the player itself and be similar to the overall value of the transfer. Also they get impatient and unless you give them what they want the deal burns and you can't speak to them again. This isn't "Football Agent Manager 17"... It's absurd the amount of failed negotiations because of their unrealistic demands.
Another ongoing issue... You can try and sell your top players but you'll never get a huge offer, involving loads of millions for them, even if it's fair. On the other hand if you want to buy one such player you always have to burn trough all your fortune... It's realistic that a team demands a huge amount from you for a star player. It just isn't that you can't get those same teams to do the same for YOUR star player...
4) Player moral is still uncontrollable and glitchy... If you manage well and you do it right your team will have a superb moral, but nowadays it just seems that the moral depends solely on winning matches on a roll or giving a lot of playing time to some player. This is a simulator and it should be about providing optimal training conditions, decent contracts, superb team management, among all the other conditions you need to keep a smooth level of moral amongst the squad. How long before the improvement of the Team talks (should be able to do it at any time with pertinent dialogue)? Why is it that if you fine or warn a player because he's been ejected with a red card 3, 4, 5 times in 9 or 10 matches he thinks it's unfair, causes havoc in the dressing room and demands to leave? For the love of god... get it straight guys, that's not how it goes in real life...
I could go on forever. The essential is that not only didn't the game improve from last year's... But also it seems the most absurd and irritating issues persist year after year. SI has an incredible team and a great working force. I know they are more than capable of doing better. This is a game that relies heavily on loyalty players and I honestly thinks their major concerns are being ignored...
Still the best football managing game. But, for now, stick with the '16 version.

This is, I am quite certain, the oldest game in my steam library.  What is so very sad about this fact is that this is the best 2d platformer I've encountered in my quest to play every game in my library.  Yes, I put it above Braid.  How is this possible?  Well, let's look at what's required for a good 2d platformer:
Precise controls
Interesting levels
Precise controls
A good difficulty curve
Precise controls
That's not to say Commander Keen is perfect.  The controls are a little tight for my taste, and the scrolling is a little jerky.  The important thing, however, is that the controls are very precise.  Command Keen does exactly what I want him to do, when I want him to do it.  23 years later many platformers have still not mastered this basic concept.
As for the rest, this is a cool little game.  The levels are interesting, and there's an element of exploration built in as you explore the various towers and levels in any order you want.  The levels are short enough as well that you never get the level exhaustion you get in some platformers.
My only real gripe is the sound effects.  Man are those annoying.

Despite the charming and whimisical exterior the art conveys, Rise&Shine (R&S) is a brutally difficult game, that challenges your shooting and dodging skills, but never feels unfair for doing so.
It's rare to get a game nowadays that brings in the near-perfect level of challenge that frustrates you, but is still approachable enough that you say, "No, I can do it this time," after each brutally gorey death. The most recent game series to achieve that, that I can pull off the top of my head, is Dark Souls. Any game that manages to emulate anything from that series is worthy of some praise.
From start to finish, the art style of the game never fails to charm and impress. Adult Swim games are often known for their fresh and interesting art styles employeed by their studios, and it's nice to know this game is no different. Background art also stands out, and this is also where much of the meta game-humor comes from.
From the trailer, I assumed this game would be nothing but "us gamers, amirite? lol" jokes. However, those jokes never come up. Instead, what the game does is treat the planet you fight on like a sort of gaming hub (think Wreck-It Ralph, where all the game characters meet up after closing time). There are plenty of nods to classic games in the background, and each is amusing. Game culture (not gaming culture) gets adopted into the worldbuilding as well.
The sound design is top notch, making for visceral and satisfying gun fire, explosions, and gore splattering sounds. Music ranks right up there too. It never sticks out beyond the initial play of the track, afterwards it fades back into the background and acts more as a nod to your unconcious mind, reminding you of the tone and feeling of the level. Whether that's good or bad is up to you.
Here is where I think a lot of people are going to get hung up. Controls are very simple. Move left and right, jump up and then double jump, and a dash to avoid near-death-experiences. However, Rise, the  titular character, moves very slowly. The dash is going to get you out of trouble only a few times, and you shouldn't rely on it. This is doubley true for double jumping.
R&S offers two means of control: gamepad and KB+M. Initially I felt like a controller would be best, since I prefer them when doing a side scrolling platformer. When I realized this game had minimal platforming, as well as a reticle that follows your mouth so you can aim your shot perfectly, I switched over to KB+M. There's no beating a mouse when it comes to accuracy.
Speaking of accuracy - you're going to need it. There are big enemies you could randomly fire at and they'll get hit, but the bulk of what you fight are enemy drones that fly around, at speeds ranging from listing around in a small circle, to literally teleporting to another spot. You'll also need accuracy for the puzzles.
The puzzles in R&S are there to mix things up, so you're not always shooting. There are two kinds - guiding and dunking. Guiding puzzles has you use your remote control attatchment on your gun to take control of a bullet so you can manuever through a narrow, often guarded, space to reach a far away button. Dunking, so to speak, is you needing to use your grenade launcher and decide on the perfect angle to use so you can launch the grenade into a basket, of sorts. Same as the shooting, these puzzles can sometimes be challenging, depending on your skill set, but they never feel impossible.
Rise can move while shooting. However, he moves so much slower as compared to when he doesn't have his gun out, that it's usually better to stand still or duck behind cover. This is where some of R&S's problems start to really show.
Though it never feels impossible, the challenges the game throws at you can often frustrate you into making up your own swear words. My biggest was the first screen of the last level. I died on that thing so many times, I had to turn off the game, take a 24 hour cool down, and come back. It kept killing me again and again, but I did manage to beat it. Hell, I died only a few times on the final boss, but the screen before him I had to respawn dozens and dozens of times.
Things really get tricky when there are a lot of enemies on screen. Once enough show up, and start firing, the game becomes a bullet hell. Since Rise can't move very fast while aiming his gun, you have to choose between firing your gun now and hoping you can dodge in time, or dodge now and hope you have time to shoot the drone before it fires again.
You can shoot the bullets, however, which can give you more space to work with. However, this can actually work against you. When there's enough bullets on screen, you'll find yourself shooting a clear space through the barrage, only to have to reload, and the space fills back up. One particular enemy fires so many bullets in a straight line away from it, that by the time you shoot through all of them to hit it, it's teleported away. You can use the grenade launcher, but you run the risk of getting killed while lining up the shot.
The devs themselves have said that if you get the game, and find the challenge far more than what you can handle, to just go ahead and refund it. You won't be getting damage or speed upgrades. Your progress through the game is dependant entirely on your shooting and dodging skills. Which, to me, is a good thing. But it can be frustrating.
Overall, I do recommend this game. Its only glaring issue (aside from the fact the dev logo at the start of the game runs at full volume and blasts my eardrums out) is the challenge. Mind you, I said "issue," not fault. The challenge of the game does not make it worse. It does, however, make it more niche. If you wanted to get a mindless side scrolling shooter you can half focus on while watching Netflix, this will not fill that role. If you're a fan of difficult side-scrolling shooters, and don't mind dying a lot, this game is for you.
People have contested the fact that the game costs $15, and can be beaten in around 2 hours (less if you're super good). It took me 3 hours, but one hour was due to failed attempts. The game also lacks any replayability outside of you enjoying the game so much that you want to play again. It has an Iron Man mode, but god help whoever goes on that mission.
The value of a game, determined by hour to dollar ratio, is different for every person. This game works out to be around the same price as a movie ticket for a 2 hour movie, if you end up taking 3 hours to beat it like I did. That will sit well with some, but not with a (sadly) vast majority of players.
Personally, I think the value of a game is dependant on the care put into it and the quality that shows because of it. Rise & Shine defininitely has care and quality as two of its characteristics. In short, Rise & Shine is a short, challenging, game that is worth the price of admission.

* Giant creatures to shoot at
* Not quite as giant mechs to pilot, repair, and swap mech weapons found on the map  (some mechs even require multiple players to pilot efficiently)
* Tons of various guns, character skins you can mix and match (once you beat the game once), titles, and emotes to give all of the players thumbs ups and silly dances
* Huge focus on multiplayer modes (you can play by yourself with AI bots but it's not nearly as helpful or fun as online)
* Grappling hooks for climbing and closing in on giant enemies weakpoints

However, despite the story leaving more to be desired, the game itself is still a blast if you have at least one friend to play it with. There's plenty of unlockables to discover and show off between you and certain gameplay features do better with friends to amplify the experience. If you don't mind playing with strangers through the campaign matchmaking then more power to you!

I dived into this game without watching the anime or knowing anything about it beforehand. This review was written after completing every route and achievement in the game. This game gets a 10/10 from me.
If you are a fan of visual novels or otome games, this game is definitely one you should consider buying! Futhermore, it often goes on sale for ~$2 which is definitely a steal. Keep a lookout for this game during sales!
Firstly, this game has gorgeous art. I know art shouldn't be the main factor in a VN but it is a huge plus! There are five love interests you can romance, and each love interest has more than one ending. The personalities of the guys also varies so you should more than likely be able to find a favourite. Their routes branch out quite a bit as well, so you wouldn't feel like you are repeating the same storyline for a different character. The personalities of your friends and other extra characters changes depending on your route, which brought about a certain kind of freshness. Saving, loading and skipping functions were bug-free and worked well - which is essential if you are planning to complete all routes.
Although some parts were pretty cheesy and cringe (quite common in otome games though), I truly enjoyed playing through this game. There were many surprises and I even teared at some of the scenes... especially at the true ending. However, the MC doesn't really have a character of her own (except in one of the routes) and she is very passive, often letting Orion voice her thoughts for you. This is due to her amnesia. Honestly, this caused me to be quite irritated at her at some points in the game. Some of the routes (especially the bad endings) may be quite triggering too.
Overall, I would recommend this game, especially when it's on sale. My favourite routes are Kent and Ukyo, and I did enjoy all five main routes so I hope you would too.

Let me preface this review by saying that I've played visual novels like Hakuoki and Code: Realize (and XBlaze Code: Embryo, though it has some of the same faults as this) so I might be a little spoiled in my VN expectations.
I have the game on Steam but have been playing it on my Vita. I've played through two routes in the past couple of days in order to get a decent enough feel of it for a review. I played through Ikki's/Spade World first just as random selection, and then through Shin's/Heart. You aren't introduced to the characters at all before you pick, but I had seen some screen shots beforehand to know names/faces.
This really shouldn't be spoilery. I'm not going into any plot points.
PROS:
--You're not determining the love interest based on choices in the first 5 chapters or so, like I'm used to. After the brief intro/prologue, you pick a route based on a card suit, and that determines the love interest and story. This is a plus in the sense that you don't have to read several chapters that are 98% similar to the other routes each time.
--The stories themselves aren't nearly as long as what I'm used to. Generally, I would prefer longer, fleshed out stories, but dragging these stories out would probably just get tiring. The length suits them because so far they seem to just be "slice of life" and nothing super involved.
--The characters aren't the same personality dropped into a bunch of different skins. You have your playboy type, childhood friend(s), some mystery dude, math nerd, mean girl, etc. They're tropes, sure, but at least you can tell them all apart by personality, actions, etc. They're interesting and colorful.
CONS:
--The MC is like, nonexistent. I guess it was an attempt at making the player feel like they're her, but it just ended up making everyone talk in these extended monologues and wasn't AT ALL immersive. Someone is talking to her and her only responses are when you're prompted to make a choice, but that's usually while they've said a million things that you'd expect her to respond to so that it actually feels like a conversation. Toward the end of both routes, she had actual dialogue, but that's after going through the whole story with the spirit in her head saying things like, "You're really tired," or otherwise voicing her feelings aloud as if she's incapable. She lost her memories, she's not a vegetable.
--Tying into the last one...there's no real narration. Other than the spirit's comments about what's happening or on the day's events, there's no narrator describing the surroundings or otherwise doing any world-building. It made the stories a little flat for me. All dialogue and no "I went to work the next day, nervous about blah blah blah." The characters are obviously the main focus in the art, but they're not really deep enough for the game to simply be character-driven.
HALF PRO/HALF CON:
--The character art is pretty, as expected from otomate. They're expressive, beautifully-colored, and the outfits are interesting. The backgrounds are detailed enough drawings, but then they're just monochrome watercolor-splashed, so they're all pretty muted and not very immersive. Again, this could be because they wanted to focus on characters, but...see above.
--Not a whole lot happened in Ikki's route, but Shin's was kind of a mystery investigation. They're totally different stories, which I liked (going back to what I said about not having to play half of the story in order to choose the love interest). Just about all of the characters are present in each, but they play somewhat different roles.
All of that being said, I'm definitely going to read through the other routes, but the experience hasn't been nearly what I expected. I was used to the lively narration of both Code: Realize and Hakuoki, in which the narrator actually had dialogue and told a story in between interactions with other characters. It was hard to really feel anything for this MC because it was like she wasn't even there until a CG popped up.
If you go into it expecting a casual VN that will be entertaining enough but not super immersive, then go for it, especially while it's on sale. The focus seems to be on characters, not backgrounds or deep plots that take several hours to read through. I don't dislike the game, but I have certainly played better VNs.

If you like the Civilization games or the turn-based 4X genre in any way, Endless Legend is a sure buy. Same goes if you like Endless Space, but then, why are you reading this, you probably own Endless Legend already.
Endless Legend is a much-overlooked game in the 4X genre, and that's a damn shame. I suppose it's Amplitude's destiny to make great games that end up overshadowed by the established royalties in the genre (Galactic Civilizations for Endless Space, and Sid Meier's Civilization for this one), but don't let the smaller size of the franchise fool you. Endless Legend, like Endless Space, has the quality and the value to take on its bigger brother.
Since everyone will always compare every turn-based 4X game to Civilization and ask, "is it better than Civ?", well, my personal answer is that the games are different enough for the question to be moot. Endless Legend is different from Civilization mostly in how its factions handle, how its resource system works, and, well, everything else really, making it a game that is somehow very comparable, and somehow very different.
Factions aren't just cosmetically different with a few unique traits and a unique unit or two, they actually play completely differently, and every faction has its own way of playing out its strengths and compensating for its weaknesses, so much that they all require a completely unique playstyle, and this makes Endless Legend infinitely replayable. The region-system prevents you from being overrun by Settler-rushes, and the combat is highly tactical, making a good tactician able to achieve victory against a tactically less able foe, even if that enemy does possess higher-tier weaponry or units. Endless Space players will be relieved that the needlessly complex and unpredictable card system has been ditched in favour of a more intuitive map-based combat system.
Heroes make up the backbone of your army, and you can customize them through level-ups, investing points in different abilities and equipping them with different weapons, armour and accessories (if you have the appropriate resource and tech, that is!). Lastly, it is worth mentioning that the game, with its army system, gets rid of the annoying 'no-stacking' rule, while simultaneously making it impossible to form deathstacks, something a certain other game in the genre was never able to do.
The minor factions appear to be roughly the game's equivalent to Barbarians, but when looking closely, you'll see they are anything but. They offer quests, can be bribed, or even pounded into submission in order to be assimilated into your empire and give you certain bonuses, as well as letting you construct their unique units. Speaking of quests, this feature is very important in Endless Legend. Gone are the days of Goodie Huts just leaving all kinds of treasure for the taking. You may get lucky and get a freebie, but in most cases, the game will let you work for it, giving you a set of conditions to fulfill (military, diplomatic, expansion-oriented and so on) before you can claim that reward.
Victory conditions are both of the mundane and classic variety, and also some special ones, like the Faction Quest every player gets, which consists of multiple stages, taking you through multiple eras. This, again, gives the game a lot of diversity in playstyles and keeps you on your toes - after all, that faction you consider lesser because of its low score might just be on the verge of completing its Faction Quest and snatching victory right from under your nose.
Graphics-wise, the game is very good-looking, with the world being so detailed and diverse you'll sometimes wish it was a bit less cluttered so you can see the tactical value of the land, but that's a tiny gripe. Another tiny gripe is the somewhat repetitive music, but we're living in an age of multi-tasking computers, even if that bothers you, just play your own music in the background.
So, to sum it all up, if you've been playing mostly Civilization games, Endless Legend takes a bit of adapting, and you'll need to get used to the FISDI system and the rest of the differences, but is it worth it? You bet your buns it is.

Enemies lacking variation coupled with clunky spear-throwing sections are the only downsides to this experience. With that aside, the enviroment was crafted with so much effort and care that the attention to detail truly shines. The campaign features Rome as a struggling but bustling civilization, and the lush, eerie, and hostile forested outskirts of Britannia, the land of the Barbarians. In Multiplayer you won't see campaign settings being recycled, which is refreshing, instead you are given completely new settings, such as maps based in Egypt, those maps featuring sharpingly-detailed obelisks and heiroglyphics and even into the burning realm of Hades. The story wasn't as lacking as it was made out to be, and even hyped me up at one point near the end - fueling on the rampage that is Marius Titus.
Multiplayer Co-op is fun, too, which includes survival mode, campaigns, ranking up, a nice set of achievements, and unlocking armors and weapons while championing different Roman Gods such as Jupiter, Mars, Diana, and Apollo. The downsides to the multiplayer is how it's design could've been approached. There are only four gods available to fill the role of champion for, and you can change your deity every match. What's negative about that is you can only unlock one unique item per deity, and there isn't more of either, which Roman mythology is bustling with dozens of gods and goddesses and have no lack of mythical weapons and armor. There could've been much more there, but it's still fun to Co-op play it with a buddy. There also isn't a way to communicate with whoever you're playing with.
Additions they could've added to Multiplayer for more playability and overall better experience:
- Daily Tasks(Contracts, Missions, you choose) in the Colosseum, rewarding the Hero gold for 'x' executions done, parries made, focus gained, campaigns done, survival time achieved, etc.
- Additional Deities, with tiered weapon and armor unlocks for each.
- Legendary Items from Roman mythology, which can be acquired from high level Booster Packs.
- More stat bonuses, possibly granting abilites from special Items; A shield that automatically deflects arrows, a sword that never fails to parry a power attack, a chestpiece that keeps you alive once from a death blow, a helmet that highlights an enemy who is getting ready to make an attack towards you, a pair of greaves that extend your sprint time, a pair of handguards that extend your combo-to-combo downtime, etc. Come on CryTek, let's make the player value their character a bit more.

Imagine trying to play metal slug, but instead you can only shoot while standing still. And you have to hold the left trigger or right mouse button at the same time while you are hitting the button to fire, and you have to reload frequently and it’s slow, and you only have one type of shot, and occasionally in the middle of the fight you have to play a trickshot game of snakes with your bullets, only the fight isn’t paused. You have infinite lives, but every most enemy attacks are insta-kill and you have to start the whole fight over.
It doesn’t feel like they tried something new and interesting that failed, which I could understand. It feels really poorly done. Something that would have been caught and early in any sort of QA and was ignored.
You can tell a lot of work went into the game, but it almost like it was made by someone who doesn't play video games if that makes any sense ? Everything is great, except the actual game.
I wouldn’t be so critical except, except I’d expect a lot better for 11$. Which should tell you just how bad the controls are. Especially given the long history of sidescrollers to draw inspiration and learn from the mistakes of.

I am no stranger to big game hunting. I enjoy reading extensive books on african hunting. My absolute favorite being "African rifles and Cartridges" by John Taylor. Knowing what I know knocks much of the realism of this game out of the window. When one fires just a .450 into the skull of an elephant, whether or not it hits the brain, it will knock it out for a few seconds. Even longer if it is a larger cartridge like the .577 Nitro-express or .600 Nitro-Express, that is why they are called stopping rifles. Not just head shots will stun animals like this but quite often shoulder shots with "modern" cartridges. That is why there are so many stories of hunters instantly dropping animals, only to have them pop back up and run off, or run after them. Now I know what the reader will say "But Jack, these are big boy dinosaurs.". Well let me lay down the numbers. A male african elephant can get up to 6 metric tons while modern estamates of tyrannosaurus are about 8 metric tons (both according to wikipedia). So yes Tyrannosaurs were big boys, but we aren't firing .410 jeffery at these guys. We are firing a .700 cartridge, which I presume is a nitro express. The jump in caliber from 600 to 700 is about X1.36. I'm not about to dig through my books for a simple reveiw but I beleive the time that a 600 would knock out an elephant when shot in the head was a minute or so. So if you were to use a 700 on the head of a tyrannosaurus it would, if not knock out, stumble or be stunned greatly by the shot. When you read about african big game hunting
. Now you never, you
see this method recomended by anyone or used effectively by anyone in this game. So, this game, ontop of it's other problems, feels unrealistic.
Now that will bring me to my biggest point about this game. You will never feel satisfied. The best thing in a game is when you pull the trigger and the guy drops. That is satisfaction. It is satisfing to hear the gun boom, the muzzle to jump up deliciously, the guy to drop, and for you to work the action.
But in this game. you will eventually get a .700. You will fire it, it will hop just a bit in your hands, and the creature shot will not even flinch as a puff of red comes off of its side. You might as well be using a pellet gun that fires slow acting neurotoxin, because that is as satisfing as it feels.
Now I know that it would be op to have a gun like this, but it takes ages to find this gun and a few rounds to go with it. All within a world where many giant unstoppable carnosaurs are always right around the corner.

After being one of the the many that was fooled by 'The Stomping land's', back in the day, this seems like a WONDERFUL game expeirance, at first glance, however I let it slip past me until 2016.  A Hunting game where you hunt dinosaurs instead of Deer, whilst done before by The 'Carnivores' franchise to realtive sucess, it is still a form of game that could do very well, in the right hands, however, this game *did* have protentional, but instead was abandoned for Just Cause 3 and Thehunter: Call of the Wild development. (To my knowledge, not saying this *is* the 100% truth, but most likely something along those lines.)
TL:DR; AVOID THIS GAME, If it suddenly is being patched daily, new content added, be wary, but maybe buy it, but until that day comes, which it most likely won't, don't buy it. Unless it is on sale for 1$ or your regional equal.

Now, to the main part of this reveiw.
Pros:
+Semi-Realistic dinosaurs: I imagine this will confuse most people reading, what I mean by it is, this has dinosaurs with feathers, even the mighty T rex. As well as a Semi attempted at 'Recreating' what they might have actually did, though no one knows for certain.
+/- Fairly large map, Easy to get lost, cornered, or fall of a cliff, but vastly different, some places being near fully Coniferious trees, then to find a Inactive large bed trailing down from a volcano, to a Grassy plain with hills.
+ Fairly good graphics on a Lower end computer like myself.
And now, what most of you are waiting for, the cons:
- Barely any weapon variety, at all. Most weapons are either slight variations, or just not very useful. Biggest offender of this is the crossbow. The crossbow, obtained from BEATING THE FINAL BOSS, is not all that helpful. Doesn't hit as hard as some would want it to, Terrible sights that can glitch out, and the gimmicks with the weapon are: It has tracer bolts that stay lit up as they fly, as well as when they hit a target, and that you can fire it laying down.
- Fairly Dumb A.i. I know what some of you are think 'But didn't he say they have semi realistic A.i?' I did say 'A Semi attempt at how we thought they would act.' I.e, Utah's roam in packs, Trikes roam in herds, t rex hunt in 1's or 2's, etc. But that doesn't mean they have good path finding.
- Somewhat of Permadeath. Ok, this is more of a Personal complaint more than a Universal problem, feel free to ignore this con. When you buy, you drop ALL of what you were carrying, every item. You can track down your body, you can get your stuff back, but players can come along and steal your stuff while you are returning to get it. Meaning, if you die, you most likely will lose your stuff. Some servers kick people whom loot, which helps with this problem, but there is no option to turn this loot off.
- Fairly confusing audio. Say you hear a roar of what you think is a dinosaur in the distance, so you pull your Settler mate, and there is no call on it: That would be a Audio call, that has no importance to the game. At. All. This will confuse most newer players, and some more Experiance players as well.
---- BIGGEST PROBLEM----
BUGS. Bugs bugs bugs! Very, VERY BUGGY GAME. When you leave a game server, your level will reset and so will your inventory,  this can be fixed with a bit of Document fixing, but very hard to do so. Dinosaurs will teleport around, use telekinetic powers to grab you from a mile away, this happened a few times to me, though it seems to be rarer, Bullets and Arrows will just go through the dinosaur and land in a tree 3 miles away, You'll be teleported to the sky very rarely..
Final verdict: 2.3/10.

I do beleive this game has ALOT of potentional, and in the right hands, it would've been a amazing game, one that could've even been a game of the year. Instead, After a long time, it was just abandoned, not that disimiliar from the stomping land in some respects.

There's lots wrong with the game, but it's still really good; once you start laughing at all the crazy stuff that can happen if you mess up one choice. I don't reccommend doing Toma first, as it will completely turn you off from the game. Do them in the order the worlds appear. Heart, Spade, Clover, Diamond, and then Joker once you unlock it.
The art quality is fantastic, despite everyones very....um...odd choices of fashion. The artist really REALLY loves belt buckles. The only thing I didn't like about the art is the ridiculous stunned bunny look the MC always has on her face. Compared to the guys, she's always an expresionless doll. She doesn't really have any personality, for obvious reasons, but I was fine with that, as at least she's not dumb as a doorknob with no common sense like the MC in OZMAFIA!! so I was able to skim past her flaws. Orion more than makes up for her.
I knew going into it, that there was going to be a lot of messed up stuff, and that one of the characters is a hardcore yandere. I ended up taking a screenshot every time someone he said raised a red flag, and I made a game of it to make it a bit more lighthearted. By the 15th day, I had over 70 screenshots. I ended up just giving up, since I didn't want a thousand more screenshots.
From best to worst, my characters would be-
Ukyo + Orion cuz he's B E S T B O Y E
Ikki
Kent
Shin
Toma
Toma is well...Toma...It's funny, if I didn't know information about the game before hand, Toma would have been my first route. The sweet, scincere, protective childhood friend. *snorts*.  Toma's good ending is "um...." Toma's normal ending is "um...." Toma's two bad endings are "um...."
Shin's romance was meh. I was more interested in the actual murder mystery who-dunint than anything else. Not much else to say, really. I don't like tsunderes, they remind me of a child still stuck in the 'pulling the hair of the girl you like' stage. Shin's good ending is "That's it?". Shin's normal ending is "Meh" but Shin's two bad endings? They give you the true taste of what is to come in the game, and they are great. Which is why I reccomend doing him first.
Kent is the cyborg learning emotions for the first time. It's endearing most of the time, but can get kind of cringy at times. His good ending was very sweet. Normal end is kind of bittersweet, while I haven't bothered to do his bad ends yet.
Ikki was a surprise. I knew he was the playboy type character which I always loathe, but once you get into his route more, he's one of those "surounded and 'loved' by everyone but still lonely" characters, which I always end up being a sucker for. I enjoyed his route a lot. I figured he'd be my top guy at the end, but Ukyo came out of left field and shoved everyone else off the pedestal. Good end is just great. His three bad ends are great as well.
Finally is Ukyo. Ukyo, Ukyo, Ukyo. He is locked at the beginning of the game. You need to obtain the good ending with the four other characters to unlock him, but honestly it's so worth suffering through Toma route for him. During all the other guys, you'll get bits and peices that will make you very curious as to who this guy is. This♥♥♥♥♥♥is the true ending. I haven't done his normal or his SEVEN BAD ENDS (SEVEN!!!) but his good ending...*muwah* it's a masterpeice. Ties everything together, and it's just fantastic.

I first played Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes the day it launched on PS3. Leading into it's release I replayed the franchise, PeaceWalker included. I was shocked to fire up the PS3 and try Ground Zeroes out, it looked like trash.....
I found Ground Zeroes on the PS3 suffered from the same problem GTAV did, low framerate! After playing the silky smooth MGS4 I expected FoxEngine to be a step forward. Instead what I got was a chuggy, blurry, and jaggy mess. Once I beat the main mission I took the disk out and never wanted to try it again.
Fast forward to the PC re-release and I was getting nervous. My computer is a few years old now, a Phenom II x4 965be and a GTX570. I was worried I would be getting a similar experience with low framerates, jaggy  models, blurry textures. Even if it didn't run I was still going to be buying it to show support for Godjima, and all Japanese developers for that matter, to encourage future PC releases.
Well hot damn, does it run amazing. I'm running on High settings at 1920x1080 and the game went from being the uglyest MGS I've played to the most georgus. It runs silky smooth, the animations are great, the textures are detailed.... It's just damn beautiful.
As for the content I've put in 13 hours so far and am only at 18% unlocked, and that was from the main mission and two side missions on normal difficulty and B rank. If you were to JUST play the main mission the game can be short, like an hour the first time short, but you would be missing out. The side missions have enough variety in weather, spawns, items, costumes, and objecteves to keep things fresh and exciting well after the main course. I have many more hours to go as I finish each unique mission, S ranking them all, then doing it all over again on Hard.
Considering it's reputation as "a demo with little content" this would be one of the best PC games I've ever bought. It's so well programmed, it makes me happy I can run it at such high settings without it heating up or maxing out my PC. If you're like me and grew up with a PS1 and a PS2, support one of the best franchises in video game history. I am so excited now knowing I'll also be able to run silky smooth versions of Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain AND Metal Gear Online 3.

This game has great artstyle but its extreamly short (got to the last boss in 1.5 hours) and resorts to artifical difficulty in some parts.
This is a slow paced shmup that clearly doesnt want you to shoot and move simultaneously; your mobility while shooting is very limited and theres an animation that has to play when you bring out your gun, so it clearly wants you to stay still behind cover, wich is fine for the most part, excep that if you play on a big screen, as its difficult to aim at the enemies and keep visual track of your character at the same time.
The game uses player mechanics of games like flashback where you mainly fight a couple of guys in front of you from cover, but then throws a ton of flying enemies that shoot you from above wich gets very weird when a fast moving flying enemy flies on top of you and you cant shoot it becasue your cahracter can't shoot straight up.
There are some enemies that seem a bit like artificial barriers, one is a giant gear that spins towards you and you're supposed to stay still between two of its teeth, excep its movement doesnt match the animation so can get squashed even if you calculate the rotation right; theres also that fast flying enemy that teleports every time you hit it and shoots a lot of bullets which would be good if could aim straight up.
I feel like the game puts out those barriers at the end of long difficult sequences to kill you and make you repeat them.
Did I mention you can't aim stright up?
Jokes aside, I wish this was a bigger projec released on early acces to extend the story over the dev cycle, as well polish some of the mechanics.

Alright, not usually one to write reviews on Steam, but I felt it was necessary here in order to help combat some of the negative main stream games press this title has received.
I buy and play a great number of games every month across all platforms.  Typically, I play those games for anywhere from 10 minutes to an hour – and never go back to them.  I am always looking for that next ‘gem’ which has the right mix of gameplay, aesthetic, and challenge in order to hold my attention from start to finish.
After reading some reviews on the main game sites (reviewers I typically agree with), I almost didn’t buy Rise & Shine.  I kept watching the gameplay video on the Steam page, and I felt I needed to give it a try anyway (I’ve liked most Adult Swim published games so far).
I’ll address the main criticisms – length, difficulty, and story/humor.
Length will be any easy one – it took me about 4 hours to beat a $12 game.  Not sure what the issue is there – that was with minimal searching for secrets and collectibles, as well as trying all the mini-games a few times each.  I haven’t even touched Iron Man mode or gone back to find the rest of the secrets and get perfect scores on said mini-games.  You’ve got some replay value right there.
Difficulty – I’m a player with what I’d consider average skills.  Let me define average – I usually fall in the bottom third of the points board in online matches, can’t usually get past the first ‘dungeon’ in most rogue-likes (but I’ll be damned if I don’t try), and can’t even tell you what happens after the first boss in any of the ‘Souls’ games. I can finish most games of high difficulty that offer a reasonable checkpoint system and some sort of pattern that you can learn from with each attempt.  Rise & Shine falls into this category.  Is it difficult? Yes.  Can a player of average skill complete the game?  Certainly.  With a little trial & error (there’s your sequel Super Mega Team) and a bevy of patience, I think most gamers could finish this game – and feel rather proud of that accomplishment – it’s not walk in the park.  There’s one area in particular toward the very end of the game which I had to retry about 500 times – but each time I noticed something new in the pattern, something the developers had included for a purpose – that helped me make a bit more progress.  There are at least 10 variables to keep track of in that fight at any given time.  I think that battle could use an extra checkpoint somewhere along the way.
Story/Humor – what’s not to like?  Great comic-book style cut-scenes with equally great artwork.  An interesting overall setting – lots of references to classic game franchises both modern and games past.  The humor could probably be hit-or-miss for some folks, but it doesn’t detract from enjoyment of the game.  It’s an action-platformer, and you’re getting a story deeper than any early Mega Man or Mario game – nothing to complain about here.
So back to my initial comment about the ‘mix’ that keeps me interested.  Rise & Shine has it.  I was compelled to keep coming back to this game (despite raging out during a few of the more challenging areas) until I finished it.  The gameplay is a great blend of a bullet-hell shoot ‘em up, puzzle solving, and strategy.  The graphics and sound are top notch, and the challenge is just right.  Overall, it reminds me of an old-school game like Mega Man combined with something like Ikaruga – both short but difficult games in which the true reward is being able to say you finished them.
Buy this, support the devs – it stands tall among the crowd of Indies we’ve already seen this year.

Going into this Otome you need to understand that it exhibits some borderline and not so borderline abusive relationships. While they do have reasons as to why they are the way they are, whether or not it is justified is completely up to you.
This Otome has everything I look for. It has beautiful artwork, unique characters, voice acting, lots of choices, numerous endings, and a deep well-written story. Each route can feel like they drag on for a bit but as this isn't free, I appreciated the amount of content. The characters are all extremely well-written and are easily recognizable from one another both physically and personality-wise. Getting a glimpse into the mentality or rather mental health of the protagonist and male leads was not only incredibly interesting, it is something I have not witnessed in many other Otomes. There's even some post-game goodies that you get to enjoy such as the mini-games, memories, and voice-overs on the CGs.
Overall, great story and great characters. I definitely reccommend playing through the whole thing.

After playing about 15 hours of Bus simulator 2012 I've had trouble coming to a conclusion about the quality of this game. Bus simulator 2012 is a very unique and indie bus game that is let's you simulate being a bus driver. This game is very in depth and so in depth it's very intimidating to start off. When I first bought Bus simulator 2012 I put about 20 minutes and couldn't figure out how to start my bus, so after that I threw it to the side and didn't come back to it for a few months. I really wanted to love this game, I like buses and I couldn't find a good bus sim but after a lot of troubleshooting I got my bus started and was able to play the game.
Here is the good parts of the game. It's very fun, I love the feeling of driving and trying to stay on time and try not to screw up. I also like the price, it's very cheap and if you really like buses then you could put many hours into this game. The Bus is fairly nice you can play it as an amature or play it as a bus efficantio. I like the amount of bus routes that are available to drive it gives a lot of replayability to the game. Overall it's very fun and it feels nice to drive.
Although the game is fun there are many problems with bus simulator 2012. One of the major issues is how extremely buggy it is. It's far from finished and it doesn't look like the developer is still updating the game which is a shame. Another of the games major problems is the city's design, the city isn't very well planed out. There are stop lights that don't make sense and there are stos with major congestion. I also dislike the mirror quality in the buses. The Mirrors on the bus are almost useless and the resolution of the mirror is also low. At high settings the mirrors work but they barely show anything, most of the time you just have to blindly change lanes and that can often be a problem. Another problem is the passengers animation. The passengers move extremely slow and you can not tell which pedestrians are trying to get on your bus and who isn't. It's also very hard to drive and make some turns, it took alot of pratice to get use to the buses size and how best to best maneuver the vehicle. I do wish their was an option to respawn your bus close to where you were, it became very frustrating to have to respawn the bus and start the route over because I got stuck in the fenses. Although the most frustrating part is the lack of a saving function. The saves don't work so you basicly have to start over your game once you quite. It doesn't affect the gameplay much but you have to write down your new driver id and password which is frustrating at most. Overall it's a good game but it has many major flaws.
Bus simulator 2012 is a very fun realist bus game with it's peaks and with it's flaws. It's really fun to play and the bus seems fairly heavy. I would like to see the developer put more effort into updating fixing bugs and polishing up their game. I feel It's not perfect but it can be really fun depending on how much time you are willing to put in. It's has major flaws but I would recommend this game to any person who likes buses and would like to drive one. 3/5
