I'm going to pull a fast one here and say that I don't recommend this game. But only for people coming from monster hunter or expecting that type of experience throughout. I'll tell you why.
Firstly, It's too hard to swallow. Skipping videos after two to 10 minutes of gameplay is not really enough to make it feel like any other co-op shooting experience in the sense that there is enough to do or even enough to see. You'll be turning pages more than you'll be reading. It's too much to be repeated without noticing and being fatigued by it.
Next, Anyone who has faith in the game itself can see the amount of love and care that went into the mechanics of the game, this grenade can be shot to explode, this one has a delay, this gun does stun damage, this one freeezes them, you can reload and throw grenades while on a zipline, THERE'S A FREAKING ZIPLINE, and it's useful. Everything You can see, You can get for yourself. You level up enough, You can wear it all.
Then, there's the customization system, Which is actually pretty cool, But after you find out that it's easier to beat missions and dash fr credits than it is to actually level characters, and that there's no real point outside of getting full customization, You'll have an empty victory pulling the slot machine.
Finally, It's too short. In games with massive levels like halo, you'll notice a lot of goofing off mid mission and places where you go, hey screw it, I'm going to throw a sticky at my bro. Yes, you can do it here, but honestly, there's not too much content to get you outside of a heavy grind for parts, and then a heavier grind for the full customization perk. I don't even know If I am going to go after that. This is the type of game that needed DLC Badly. There's a lot of effort and ideas swirling around a toilet sized game, and the way it's designed, everyone is trained to flush past the cutscenes and then it's kind of over. Great for couch co-op I guess.

You play as an amnesiac college girl; after waking up in a hospital, you can pursue
love interest per route while meeting the other love interests as friends and colleagues. Each route has different trials and tribulations as you develop your relationship.
Overall, it’s really enjoyable getting to know all the different characters. By the time I got 100% on the game, I liked (or at least understood) everyone, which is rare. See the Game-Specific Comments for more detail.
It’s a visual novel with typical choices. It’s a 10 for lack of things to criticize.
While the characters are crisply drawn, unique, and expressive, you have to wonder why they’re walking around wearing punk-rock outfits all the time. You’re a university student; some of the love interests are also students — there’s no way they’re wearing that day-to-day in Japan! Also, in contrast to the abysmal anime of Amnesia,
, so the design choice to have
, especially, wrapped in a trenchcoat and belts is a strange one. Though the backgrounds are decent enough, they have little detail and become repetitive as you play though the game. This game really wants you to focus on the foreground; the characters and their expressions. The characters are intricate, so mission accomplished.
The soundtrack is mostly there just to fill silences. None of the pieces are very memorable during the game, though the title sequence by Zoetrope as well as the theme played at the successful end of the route get honorable mentions. You might get some of the tracks stuck in your head if you play the game for a while, but they aren’t melodies you’ll carry with you after (in contrast to games like Skyrim with songs you’ll probably listen to once you’re done playing).
I read a guide to get all possible endings, including the bad ones. It was fun (and occasionally disturbing) to see all of the outcomes for the heroine. If you fall in love with fictional characters, you’ll enjoy playing through the routes again for
waifu simulation.
It’s well-made and one of the better visual novels you can get on Steam. I enjoyed playing it all the way to 100% completion and will probably replay my favourite routes a few times.
As many other reviewers note, this game tends to portray
. Two of the routes involve the heroine
Though I personally find two of the love interests to make very unhealthy/distasteful/abusive choices as partners, it may be examined differently in Japanese than Western culture. The remainder of the love interests are fairly human and make normal relationship mistakes.

Time to review my favourite (and most played) game in my library.
Awesomenauts is a 2D, side-scrolling MOBA centered on 3 vs 3 fast paced matches with a more casual feel than other games in the genre. It is made by Ronimo Games, a small team based in the Netherlands.
The graphics are great, as is the smooth gameplay (any latency aside that is). The soundtrack is very good too. The only thing I have against the game is it's use of peer to peer rather than servers. But for the most part, as long as you stay in your own region or close to, that isn't much of a problem.
The game also has a great sense of humour, with many of the characters, or their respective scripts, making reference to other games and parts of pop culture.
Your first few matches may be a trial by fire as you start in the lower leagues where toxity reigns and ignorance is bliss. But after some perserverance you'll see the community for what it actually is; Friendly, helpfull and funny. You do need to get to at least league 5 (of 9. League 1 being the top, as you may expect) to see this though. This is much easier with friends than it is going solo, but the latter is still capable of leveling up, league-wise. It's just pot luck as to who you'll be matched with if you decide to do things that way.
In summary, Awesomenauts is one of the best value for money games on Steam IMO. It is frequently on sale for peanuts as well, so even more value. It is constanly updated with rebalancing and extra content (it started with 5 playable characters and now has 21, soon to be 22 (5 of which are DLC)) and even has a complete rework in the pipe-line as far as matchmaking goes, so less being matched with people outside your region and league.
I think you should buy it immediately.

The game forces both players into the same screen (which for pc is a slap in the face), only the host of the game gets to progress any character, money spend is the hosts money, any items obtained are only obtained for teh host, If you have a mic plugged in its always on (no toggle to talk) and etc. Overall its pretty much pointless to play multiplayer unless you own it on console and only play with a friend at your house.
If you are reading this you most likely dont care about multiplayer or realize that the game has been out for so long that the multiplayer base (what little there was) is now dead. Honestly i have to say that the single player aspects in this game are fantastic. While in single player you are limited to only 1 additional teammate. Depending on play style will depend on who you like to partner with the most. The story line is the thing that suprised me the most. Unlike mass effect your decisions often effect you long term. For example early in the game you get the choice of killing an archon, putting her in jail, or letting her go free. While the first choice will give you an extremely powerfull staff for that level, it will in turn make all future instances with archons hate you forever.
The combat is what i really enjoy most about this game. Each character you have has 3 abilities and 2 stances that they can switch between totaling 6 abilities overall. Each stance is either single target is aoe focused. Each stance though often has buffs or pets you can summon that remain active even if you switch. So reguardless of the situation i often found myself switching between them fairly often just to get the extra buff out even if that stance wasn't optimal. Using its combat system took a little to get use to. It's a small delay but deals quite a bit of dmg if you are able to get combo hits off or finish a long casting spell.

First off, this is a pretty quick play - I just beat it and Steam's tellin' me it took only 91 minutes.  So how did I like it?  Well, it didn't feel like a COMPLETE waste of time, but there were definitely better things I could have been doing.
Fans of Myst will understand and appreciate the gameplay best.  It's an FPS view, look with mouse, move with WASD, interact with E.  My first complaint was about these mechanics: not that I didn't like the button layout - that's standard.  But (and this may have been the game glitching out on me while I was playing) I found on certain levels, different buttons didn't work.  Right-click is the default zoom, for example, but for an entire level this zoom functionality was taken away.  It led to a very buggy feel to the game and increased my frustation as I tried to solve puzzles because I never really felt sure my buttons were doing anything as I tried to interact with the world.
The point of the game is puzzles, to include being given no instructions (beyond a menu pre-startup to define button layout) on how to actually play the game.  In that vein, I'd say disregard the reviews that said it was impossible to play, or there wasn't any guidance / direction.  That's kinda the point.  But when the number of interactable items on a given map are ONLY the ones required to solve the puzzle, and they're only available in the order they are needed to solve the puzzle, the game becomes less of a "puzzle" and more of a "click random♥♥♥♥♥♥until stuff happens."
Third area for review: graphics.  The world graphics are very nice, very clean, and very pretty.  I was playing on max graphics settings, and the world was very nice to look at.  Until you reach a certain point in the game
The ambient music is very nice and soothing; enough so to warrant a mention in a review.
The voice acting and dialogue, however, is not very good.  There is a lot of anger and cursing right off the bat that doesn't really seem to be warranted by the story you are dropped in.  This makes the dialogue sound forced and over-dramatic, with your character saying strange things like, "You always do this" to a disembodied voice he literally met a half hour ago.  I was actually embarassed by the hammy dialogue, and it was bad enough that I had to fight the urge to stop playing during practically every conversation / level change.  (Oh yeah, you get to sit through these drawn-out, over-dramatic convos between nearly every scene change.  While looking at black.  And not moving.  And no skipping.)
The dialogue isn't the only thing that's poorly written, btw.  The story is pretty crappy, too.  I'll just leave it at that - no spoilers.  Just, if you're looking for a good story, it's not here.  The quality of the writing seems to be on par with Twilight or 50 Shades - awful.
To recap: this game is nice to look at, plays pretty music, has horrible dialogue, tells a story that's not worth telling, and may, or may not, have buggy controls.  So how enjoyable was it?  I hated the first half of the game.  But I read a bunch of reviews before playing it that said all these neg reviews just weren't giving it a chance.  So I grit my teeth, suffered through it, and about half way through, actually started enjoying it despite the irritating convos that kept trying to pop my "blissful fun" balloon.  Unfortunately, that only amounted to about 30 - 45 minutes of fun playtime, and I really don't think all the♥♥♥♥♥♥you have to wade through to get there is worth it.
I rate this game 3 / 10: little return for putting up with the bad parts.
TL:DR - Move along, nothing to see here.
Pros:
-Pretty Graphics
-Pretty Ambient Music
-Some of the puzzles are fun
-The entire game is a puzzle (Pro, if you're into that)
Cons:
-Crummy story
-Embarassingly bad dialogue that you can't skip
-Some of the puzzles are just irritating and provide ZERO enjoyment
-The entire game is a puzzle (Con, if you're not into that)
-The game is super short, with little to no return on enjoyment

Imagine shooting up heroin whilst riding a roller-coaster made of crystalline excitement which is going through gargantuan hoops of fire over a swamp infested with three-headed sharks which have lasers for eyes and chainsaws for fins. That is exactly what Bus Simulator 2012 is not like.
You are initially offered a choice between two settings, "Beginner" or "Expert". Beginner mode is essentially expert mode with more prompts and sunny weather. Even on the beginner setting there is a steep learning curve, I ended up watching tutorials online and consulting the manual due to the inadequacy of the limited in-game prompts and lack of help features.
On the plus side the simulation is incredibly in-depth. Every single button on the bus is functional, including for example, all the switches for the blinds, windows, roof hatches, door locks and suite of climate controls. You also have the capability to fine-tune many aspects of the bus including brake and steering behavior, such as the brake speed and delay.
The environment and its dynamic effects also add to the sense of realism. For example, if you have the heating on when it's raining outside the windows can fog up; this can be remedied by turning the air circulator to the defrost position. What's even more realistic is everyone whinges about the rain as they get on.
On the downside, there are only 2 bus models (articulated and standard) to choose from which I found to be a bit of a let down. Perhaps a better game title would be "Very-specialised-urban-area-of-Germany-Two-Buses-Simulator 2012".
The game-world is expansive and has a great level of detail. I really felt like a bus driver in Germany which was mildly depressing. The only thing which detracts from this sense of immersion is the handful of minor AI bugs, but they are rare. Occasionally when turning a tight corner a car will ram into you from behind which is annoying. On the other hand, it's quite amusing to see an overturned AI bus  - it makes you feel a bit better about your driving abilities.
Overall graphics are average to decent but require abnormally high specs. It seems far too taxing but it's still playable on lower settings. The current price of $9.99 seems about right considering the simulation is very in-depth but the game feels unfinished in some areas.
If you think you will find no enjoyment in driving a simulated bus for an hour then obviously don't buy it, otherwise give it a shot.
Overall:
This game is horrible, it lags, it has horrible graphics, don't even think about purchasing it.

The Hunter, stylized as theHunter, is an online-activated hunting first-person computer game released in March 2009. The Hunter: Primal, a standalone expansion featuring dinosaurs, was fully launched in March 2015.
Step into a huge Jurassic world, where the very environment will challenge your survival skills, in TheHunter: Primal, part of the popular TheHunter franchise created by Expansive Worlds and Avalanche Studios. In theHunter: Primal players begin with very limited equipment. You need to explore the island in search of more powerful weapons, clothing and equipment. Sounds easy? Well not only is the island littered with poisonous plants, but deadly dinosaurs roam the island looking to feast on the weak. Only the foolish will challenge the mighty Tyrannosaur Rex alone. Careful planning, cooperation and backpacks filled with ammo and weapons is needed to bring this beast down. But watch out! The island is also populated with highly intelligent Utahraptors traveling in packs. Like wolves they communicate and work together to bring down a lonely hunter. Make sure to check you six! Want a more peaceful hunt? In that case the Triceratops might be an easier prey.
TheHunter: Primal offers both single-player and multiplayer modes (up to 16 players), and you can make each game session private. For a real challenge join or create a PvP session, but for players that want to focus on cooperation you can turn PvP off. The game features a persistent inventory system, which means that what you collect in one game session is available in another. But alas, this comes with a price. If you die, all your equipment is lost, but if you are fast enough you can claim back your lost backpack before another hunter loots your stuff.

Hunting in this game is more of a brief side challenge to the main game, which is slowly walking around a giant map trying not to die while you find tools just to get started.
The game actually has a giant and varied map, which is pretty, even if it gets a bit blocky in some areas. The downside of having a huge map however is that there is NO FAST TRAVEL. Expect to slowly walk (and briefly run) through a mostly empty map for your entire playthrough. Join a friends server? You may end up having to walk across the entire map to reach them upon joining, alone with no items. Unfortunately, even though you are given a good mapping tool, you will rarely ever be able to make the most of it.
The game is basically 100% ironman mode. On death you lose ALL map data, ALL weapons, and ALL equipment.
Then you will be transported quite a distance away from your body, with a blank map and a machete. If you're lucky, you MIGHT be able to make it to your body and recover your items (but not map) without dying again to whatever killed you in the first place, be it Trex, or incredibly steep cliffs that you always seem to spawn at the bottom of.
This game also doesn't have a single player mode, the closest thing being a private passworded server.
I HIGHLY recommend that if you choose to play this, you only play it with a group of friends who are also REALLY into walking/hunting games. You can try looking for public online games, but you may have issues finding someone who speaks your language to hunt with.
While you sort of level up from killing dinos, the only thing it really affects is what items you can buy after each death, assuming you have any credits to do so.
If you are looking for a fun, easy to get into hunting game, DO NOT PLAY THIS.

First, let's just say that I was hoping to see some improvement in this game series since the last time I bought one in 2011. I was surprised - not really at the improvement part, but instead at how extremely well the artificial idiotism works. Yes, that's right. I said idiotism, not intelligence.
Here are few of the problems I have spotted so far:
- Goalkeepers. They have two main actions; either skate crazily and catch the ball firmly, or try a miracle save when an easy low ball comes straight at him. Very clever to try that miracle jump into the top right corner, when the ball is actually going low into the middle of the goal. Absolutely stupid actions there.
- Defensive playing. There is no proper pressing or tackling, no matter what the tactical setup is. Defensive players approach the attacking player like they were absolutely terrified of the ball, cowering in fear two meters away and letting the opposing player pass the ball away freely and safely. If a random tackle ever happens, it's usually two-footed and results in a direct red card.
- Headers in midfield. If your goalkeeper or defenders open up with a high ball into anywhere within the mid-half of the pitch, your players never even try to win those balls. They apparently have absolutely no jumping strength at all, while the opposition players look like kangaroos out there. To be absolutely honest though, most of the time your midfielders run 5 meters off the ball's actual landing spot and as such never even need to show that lack of jumping strenght. They just like to watch the opponent picking up a free ball, from a safe distance of course.
- Strikers and headers. Even a target man who should be regularly winning headers and trying to either hold the ball or flick it to the other striker or attacking midfielder never seems to even try. In the team I played with, I had a very strong target type striker, who should be stronger with head than foot. And what does he do with high passes? Stand still, usually in the right place though, but firmly rooted to ground, while the opposing team's tiniest-midfielder-ever jumps way over him and heads the ball into safety every time.
- Receiving passes. Why on earth does the receiving player have to stand absolutely still until the pass comes all the way to him? Let's say that Player A passes the ball to Player B. Player C is the opposition defender. When Player A sends the pass, Player C immediately sees the chance to intercept and starts moving. However, Player B does not react at all; he stands still, waiting for the ball, until Player C has successfully intercepted the pass and is already starting the counter attack with his whole team, while your team doesn't even understand that there's any danger at all. If Player C can see the possibility to intercept, why doesn't Player B see that and try to get to the ball as well instead of just "giving it away"?
- Picking up loose balls, such as rebounds. Midfielder runs to the ball, takes control of it, and... well, simply stands with it long enough for an opposition player to freely take it away. Generally, there's a huge amount of just standing and letting the other team take a freebie, and within highlights, it's always the AI controlled team who gets these freebies.
...such as a midfielder getting a pass just outside of the penalty box, standing like there he's grown roots, back towards the goal, with two opposing players curiously staring at him and wondering why he has suddenly started to meditate instead of trying to pass the ball anywhere. Finally, opposing players just take the ball and pass it safely away from the area. If this happens for example near the sidelines, your midfielder will stand still for a long time even after the ball has been taken away, and then sprint into chase. Into a hopeless chase, as the opposing player is already 30 meters ahead.
- Another version with loose balls: Your player is 10 meters from the ball, running towards it. Opposing player is 15 meter from the ball, also running towards it. Which one wins? Yes, it's always the opposing player who wins and takes a freebie, as your player is afraid of any close proximity of others and slows down well in advance to avoid it.
Seriously? This is the level of AI that has been considered good enough for release?

Commander Keen is awesome - the series was one of the first video games I remembered playing back in the day.
Easily one of the most classic games; I can remember playing this in the basement as a kid for hours..

Commander Keen is a classic platformer series for the DOS. Created by FPS pioneers ID Software. This game has a special place as a showcase of the future software innovations that ID would bring. Commander Keen was unique in that it was one of the first games to have real time scrolling for the DOS, Something viewed as impossible back in the early days of Shareware. The only thing that holds me back from fully reccomending this classic is the lack of inclusion of two of the Commander Keen games, not really a "Complete Pack".
But still great games that are more then worth the asking price.

Play as Commander Keen and save the Earth from the alien invasion with nothing more than a neural stunner and a pogo stick.
A game for all the lovers of old-school platformers (Sonic, Mario, Jazz Jackrabbit) out there.
The only bad thing about this game is that keen is as fragile as a piece of tissue paper (dies in one hit), but otherwise this game is top notch.
Episodes 1-3 are okay, but if you want the best of the best in the series then play Episodes 4 and 5, which are have better graphics, levels and gameplay.

An echo of iD and 3D Realms' past, Commander Keen is a simple platformer. What makes it special is the humor and art styles it uses. I would recommend this game to anyone who loved Super Mario Bros. and really wants to play something like it.

I hope not, because I really like Endless Legend. If you ever played the Fall From Grace mod for Civ IV, then you have a pretty good idea of what Endless Legend has going on - albiet with a much more distinctive graphical style and some of the unique rules that made Endless Space a really interesting 4E. It's actually kinda fun - it looks so much like Civ you can't help but play it as such, at first, until you lose horribly several times. Then you break down and learn how the games various interlocking systems work, and it's quite intriguing.
Or maybe not you. Maybe that was just me.
This is so closely based on Civ 5 that my wife thought I was playing the same game, just by overhearing the soundeffects from the next room. MP works great, have yet to have an incident with booting or lagging. Playing versus the computer is amusing, at least while learning. The unit designs and animations are great. In fact, the visuals are great throughout, not so much in rendering as in design. THe factions all feel distinct, and encourage different styles of play.
It's not a home run. Some factions are stronger than others, and games have a strong tendency to end militarily in the early going, regardless of factions/options/tech. The tech wed and the technologies themselves are not intuitive, nor is there an identifiable progression through them. Combat can be played out, but it is quite dull, so quick-combat still rules the day.
That aside, it's quite a bit of fun, particularly if you want that whole Fantasy Civ vibe. I'd give it a very solid 8.5/10, and call it the best "Civ-like" game I've ever played, except Civ itself.

*I loved the art and the voice acting. (Akira Ishida is one of my favorite seiyuu.)
*I liked the design of the CG gallery and how it allows you to replay the scene and allows you to click on the images for extra voice clips.
*I thought that the backgrounds of the relationships that the heroine had with the capture targets were well thought out; some where rather cliche though.
*I liked the presence of other characters in a particular capture target's route.
*I enjoyed the mini-games, especially winning at them; I would've liked for them to have been incorporated into the story itself though.
*I loved doing Kent's math puzzles.
*
What I Disliked
*I'm not too big a fan of having a character route locked down so quickly. I'd prefer several choices to be made in order to choose a route. (I was expecting that the heroine would have to raise affection with a particular character first to lock into their route.)
*I would have liked for the heroine to be have been voiced even though she has few lines.
*Additionally, I would have liked for every character to have a sprite even though some some minor.

*I wish there was a music room, so the BGM could be replayed on its own.
*I would have liked a harem option.
*I wish there was an Orion route.
*I wished there were more math puzzles.
*I felt like some Ukyo could have been fleshed out some more.
Other Comments
*I read one review complaining about the heroine lacking a personality, but I think it's purposely that way because it's an otome game. The heroine is supposed to be
after all. It's something of an immersion factor I suppose, so you can pretend that you're truly dating these guys.

I have gotten into Otome Games after playing Amnesia Memories. I have played backstage pass and Blood Code. One thing that makes this game stand apart from the others is the fact YOU DO NOT PLAY THE SAME STORY OVER AND OVER AGAIN WHEN PURSUING THE OTHER CHARACTERS! THIS IS AWESOME! I think this is a huge feature. I know I haven't played a whole lot of Otome games, but I am thinking, based on my experience, that a lot of otome games force you to replay the same story and based on your choices, changes your end story a bit.
Visually, this story is good (just wish they wore better clothing...yikes!), but overall it is stunning. Amnesia memories is a novel game sort of like a choose your own adventure books you might have read and been familiar with when you were younger.
The story line is decent too. If you like otome games you will most likely like this game. The basic premise of the story is a girl who had a spirit collide her mind and now has amnesia. She needs to go through the various worlds (where there is a new guy she is supposed to pursue) without letting them know she HAS amnesia. The mystery of the story involves a guy who pops up occasionally. He seems to know more about the heroine than he should and warns the heroine of danger. He either appears that he has genuine concern or is downright creepy - seeming to take pleasure in the idea that the heroine might die.
There is one path that really depicts an unhealthy relationship with boy Yandere (in the simplistic term...a psychopath) if it was to happen in the real world there is no way I would entertain someone like that...BUT it isn't the real world. Personally, I liked his path, if nothing else than to scare the hell out of me. It made me tread very carefully in all the paths and raised my level of distrust.
In each path you can have a bad ending, normal ending, and good ending. It was fun to see what happened if I responded to the characters naturally.
The final path wraps the story nicely. It explains the reason Orion (the spirit) collides with her mind and why this guy keeps showing up.
I guess that is all I can say about it without giving away the story. Its good! I like it. I hope Idea Factory brings out more games including Amnesia Later, Crowd, and World. The fact is that these kind of games are new to North Americans. Sorry to say, but has to be said. They are taking a risk introducing these games to which most North Americans are not aware of this genre yet. So, I repeat DO NOT DOWNLOAD ILLEGALLY!.

The "cancer" version of the Counter-Strike series. Somewhat buggy and sluggish feeling. Does offer competitive ranking system in a Counter-Strike 1.6 setting, has more content custimization and casual gamemodes, microtransaction options.
"Cancer" version might sound nasty and biased, of which it's probably true because of the amount of time I've spent playing Counter-Strike. But in the detailed review, I'll try to provide an unbiased view.
Counter-Strike Nexon: Zombies is a free-to-play game based off of Counter-Strike 1.6 that has a huge emphasis on the "zombies" gameplay (hence, the title). The game offers many other gamemodes, such as the original bomb defusal and hostage rescue, along with new co-op and eecentric ones, like scenario missions and "Bazooka Battle". The gamemodes are somewhat fun with a group of friends, but could be confusing if you play solo.
The game also offers weapons and character skins not present in the original Counter-Strike, adding more variety to the game itself. These can be purchased with acutal money or be bought with in-game money.
For me, the gameplay itself is somewhat laggy or choppy, which could be due to how the game connects to the server. It does not make it unplayable, but it becomes a bit annoying as it is just tiny stutters. The game could get obnoxious where all you hear is just bullet shots, especially in the zombie gamemodes because of how there is a "boss battle" and the only way to kill it is to shoot your gun. With that logic, you end up with a full server with heavy machine guns spraying at this high-health monstrosity (the boss is a monstrosity, not the gamemode/game mechanic), which becomes a headphone nightmare (of which you can just mute your volume).
I can say that it is a moderately fun casual game to play, due to its creative gamemodes. On a competitive level, I would advice against it. The game just does not feel like it provides a good competitive environment (other than the lag stutter, it's just not the style of the game). Plus, most of the servers are predominate with the casual gamemodes.
The main menu is similar to many free-to-play game menus made by companies similar to Nexon, where there is a server browser for different countries, an inventory page, a challenge page, a microtranaction page, etc. The menu is also somewhat clunky, which takes away from the experience (it's not even gameplay, but it just brings a feeling of "cheapness").
I do like the challenges, as it brings more goals and things for the player to complete to gain rewards. It adds challenge to the casual game experience.
It's really hard for me to recommend this game because there are other free-to-play games that are much better than this, like Team Fortress 2 or (if you want to stick close to the arcade shooter) Combat Arms. If anything, I would recommend it for people as a (not that great) "demo" for the actual Counter-Strike or for people who enjoy mindless shooting of monsters. It's not much of a "horror" genre when it comes to their Zombies gamemode, but rather "meh" survival gameplay.
I would definitely not recommend this game for Counter-Strike fans, hands down. I would also not recommend this game overall due to how there are better free-to-play games that are similar to this one.
Even though I've only played this game for only 1 hour, it was more than enough to know the game experience.

The campaign only lasts about 6 hours or so which is kind of short for an AAA game.
The campaign duration may not be so bad if only the co-op matchmaking works. Since this game only supports 2 player for multiplayer, it is very and i mean VERY hard to find partners with the matchmaking system. You have to scour the steam community for players and add them individually and hope they are free to play with you. The last time I've checked, theres only about 300 players in game
which may be why the matchmaking does not work. Well thats not so bad, of course you can play the multiplayer maps by yourself or bots am I right. Well, no you are wrong. There are only a limited amount of maps that you can play by yourself which will get rather boring after awhile. There are also no bots capability so you have to find co-op partners to play those maps available in multiplayer only.
If it is so bad, why do you give this game a thumbs up?. Well its because I got this game on sale (about 50% off). At that price, I feel that this game is really worth my money due to its stunning graphics, and the enjoyment that I get when I first started this game. However, if I were to have bought this game with the full price of about $50, it will be definitely a different story.
In conclusion:
Pros:
- Stunning graphics
- Good game physics
- Amazing soundtrack
- Simple combat
Cons:
- Multiplayer matchmaking does not work
- Repetitive combat
- Unclear upgrade system
- Short campaign

One of the best isometric action games there is. Definitely a really good game. Four playable classes, my fav being the mage because he has cool looking spells like clockwork bombs. I have beaten the game with him and the entire game was awesome. Now I am playing the dlc Treasures of the Sun with my gunner. The gunner can switch between a rifle and dual wielded weapons that include a one handed shotgun and pistol and she has some really powerful skills. The fighter chick can summon a fire dog to help and the warrior is pretty self explanatory with some good skills also. The voice acting is very good and the game has memorable sound effects. The mouth movement actually matches the words in most cases in cut scenes. That's some pretty good detail for a top-down action game. The music is superb and always fitting of the place and mood. The graphics are really very good and hold up very well even by today's standards. The best thing about the game is its unique combat system. You get two sets of weapons with three skills each, and you can hold right trigger to activate more powerful versions of your spells or hold left trigger to activate healing and defensive skills. Obviously I play with a xbox 360 controller and it actually works very well because otherwise I would never even consider using a controller for a isometric game. A good example of a game that you can easily find somewhere on sale for a steal or could actually pay its regular price of $15 and that is still a great price, especially since the game will give you around 14-16 hours of playtime as it did me.

I played this game outside of steam, I had a max leveled character with almost best gear and I am terribly sorry I played this game. Don't get me wrong, when I started playing, the game was doing fine, all it lacked was some balance and end game. But they never added end game content and just kept adding pay to win updates like buying gear upgrades.
I'll make this short, these are the bad points of the game, play if you can not mind:
-Pay to win, you can buy everything with real cash, and if you can't, you can buy it from other players by trading, this includes: Gold, Gear upgrading (which can't be done via in-game means), Bag space and others.
-No actual end game, you repeat 1 same dungeon over and over, after the 100th time it gets kinda boring, after 300th time you just kinda chit chat and make jokes with your teammates while wondering why aren't you using a bot because you're just clicking 1 or 2 spells
-Crafting is BORING, you know how you gather? Click on an iron ore, now wait 15 seconds, okay, now click on another iron ore. Oh wait, your inventory is full! How about you run 20 minutes back to the bank or pay for some inventory upgrades with real cash?
-Half of the updates are seasonal events, last one was gathering easter eggs, you walk around map and click on eggs, yes,  you have to do that 2000 times to get a key, which you can buy for 1 euro. That's how much these developers value your time, 1 euro is 10 hours of your time.
-The game lacks things like action house and guilds, and for some reason it's taking developers YEARS to make it. They also keep postponing the release by giving excuses.
-The game's population is very small, about 50 people per server online usually.
-Looking for dungeon group? Spam world chat or ask your friends. By friends I mean half the server, because if you add 30 people as friends, you have half the server there.
-PVP is dominated by 1 class alone, a mage healer hybrid can deal tons of damage and heal themselves, stomping over everyone else.
-Leveling is like any other game, the quests are a bit more interesting but not fun at all, you just kill 10 rats and then sometimes you get stuck with no quests, so you kill 500 rats to level just by that.
I have tried giving advice to the developers on the game forums for a few months now, I told them to stop with the pay to win updates, I told them how to make end game better, how to make leveling better, how to fix their game and they end up listening to none of what I said, or anyone else for that matter. I consider this game dead now, it will only get worse and I've lost all hope.
Conclusion: stay away unless you like playing an inferior, grindy, unfun, p2w game.

I picked up Endless Legend during a Steam Sale around the same time as Sid Meier's Beyond Earth, without expecting very much. Unfortunately, Beyond Earth was a bit of a letdown and I grew bored of it within a few days, deciding to give Endless Legend a try, and discovered a truly great 4X game.
Endless Legend takes a lot of familiar 4X concepts, adds a few new and interesting features, and polishes the whole package beautifully. Some of the more unique features are;
*Heroes & Quests - Your leaders are powerful combat units themselves (or alternately can become strong governers for your cities), and you can level them up with unique skill trees, and equip them with items to specialise them in certain ways.
*Upgradable/Customised Units - In much the same way that your Heroes can acquire gear, so too do all your standard units. Each faction only gets a handful of different units throughout the game, but because of the way you can customise them, it never feels like there is a lack of choice.
*Factions - In Endless Legend, the different factions play extremely differently. From a tribe who can move their cities around at-will, to one who are limited to only one city, to one whe are utterly incapable of any sort of diplomacy with other factions and is instead in a constant state of war with everyone. Every faction is unique and different, giving the game a lot of replay value compared with others of the genre. If this wasnt enough, you can create your own custom faction, loading it out with unique perks and weaknesses.
Endless Legend is a gem of a game in a pretty fiercely contested genre. It combines the core elements of successful franchises such as Civ, and integrates its own features and additions. Well worth getting for any fan of the genre.

Only If is unique, but it is definitely not for everyone.
The story is not told particularly well and develops incredibly slowly for such a short game. The cutscenes are also incredibly long for what little amount of gameplay follows and cannot be skipped (though due to the unusual save mechanics of the game, you can skip ahead large portions of the game by looking up various save codes online.) It also means if you're having trouble with one particular chapter and can't get through it in one sitting, you may have to watch the same long cutscene over and over.
The "puzzles" of the game are not particularly puzzling, it's just a matter of knowing what to do, and a lot of it is the ability to think quickly. Some of the time trials are a bit short, and the dialogue becomes incredibly tedious if you're unable to get through things the first time.
As for the gamplay itself, I personally was not a fan. The controls are fairly basic as far as movement, but as opposed to having one standard "interact" key listed with the controls, signs will come up on the screen and tell you what button to press for certain scenarios (much like Call of Duty: World at War for the PC). This can be helpful with the short amount of time that you're sometimes given to figure things out, but is also one of my least favorite game mechanics as I feel it takes away some of the connection that I have with my character (though I barely felt connected to my character at all in this game.)
I also am not sure that I would classify this as a horror game (despite having found it in the horror tag), as it lacks many aspects usually associated with the horror genre. Though the character often finds himself in life threatening situations, none of them are particularly frightening or disturbing for the player. The most that I can say for it is that the atmosphere can be somewhat unsettling throughout certain points of the game.
There are some parts of the game as well that are a bit glitchy which I did my best to overlook as it didn't strongly interfere with my progress, but it was annoying nonetheless, and something that you should be prepared for if you decide to play.
There were some good aspects of the game, the story was interesting (despite being hard to grasp) and there were a couple levels that were pretty fun to play through.
While I would say the game has both merits and flaws, it's probably not a game that I would strongly recommend, though it is one of the better free horror titles available.

Now to review this great MOBA!
Awesomenauts is a very interesting form of moba that has been overlooked by many gamers. The community is awesome yet small. The game introduces a 2D platformer moba that is extremly skill based due to everything being a skill shot. I find Awesomenauts one of my favorite games and the developers at ronimo games are always updating it. The developers have recently gotten a larger team so updates will be more often. This means more characters and skins in the future.
Awesomenauts begins with you choosing your character and waiting for the game to start. Once the game begins you drop down in a pod trying to collect "Solar". (Solar is the currency in this game). There are different maps that will be randomly chosen for each game. each map consists of 3-4 towers, creatures you can kill for HP, and a Solar Drill AKA: the nexus/Titan/What ever other mobas have for the battle arena. Maps can also have jump pads that when touched launch you in the direction of the pad.
Each game is a 3v3. You upgrade your skils by teleporting back to spawn and purchasing upgrades. With all of the solar you have collected, killing enemies or destroying towers; you will then proceed to purchase items according to your build or the situation you are in. If you are new to the game you will notice that some items are locked due to the fact that you need to level up in the game to unlock new characters and items for said characters.
Now for my favorite part! The ranking system. There are a total of 9 leagues and 10 prestiges. Once you reach a certain level you have the option to prestige which will reset you to level 1. Do not worry! You will still have all of the unlocked characters in the game. You will just have to unlock the items. by playing more and more games you will advance in a league. they are in the following order:
9-Copper
8-Iron
7-Bronze
6-silver
5-Gold
4-Thorium
3-Plutonium
2-Crimsonite
1-Awesomantium
These ranks are not shown in a game. They are, however, shown on the leaderboard in the main menu. The rank that you will see ingame is their prestige. *Note: there is no casual or ranked seperate play in Awesomenauts. Basicly, every game is a ranked game.
Final Review: Awesomenauts is amazing and needs more recognition. I love the game and I think a lot of other people would too! Each game is different and each game is as fun as the last. I believe the reason why people do not want to play this game is because it is not free to play like the other major titles like Smite, League of legends, and Dota2. Take a look at this game and try it out.
P.S: It is like a buck during sales!

Allright, After playing it for a bit I want to add that I am enjoying it although it has many problems.

I don't know how you guys came up with the controls but they were unplayable for me. I created an auto hotkey script that swaps the X and D keys. But I understand if you don't want to spend development time on that. There are many alternatives available that let the player rebind keys.
That said I do enjoy the game. The gameplay is solid. It is also a fresh take on rythm games.
Instead of the usual press this button on the correct timing, you opted for "you have limited time to input these buttons". I also like the variable speed the button prompts fall and the breathing room once in a while.
I think it's great how you guys made this possible with RPG Maker! Good luck on your future projects.

Honestly the game is extremely broken right now. I don't know why the devs thought it was a good idea to have a save file  that anybody could edit with notepad and give themselves unlimited XP and Tokens to buy weapons. Also the save file doesn't even work correctly because it will not save your level or inventory after you leave the game.
The game has decent enough graphics and the gameplay is very similiar to the original theHunter, but the numerous bugs, problems, and game breaking issues ruin it right now. The only way to even get the save file to work is to edit it with notepad, but what is stopping people from giving themselves unlimited XP? You guessed it! Nothing.
Another thing is that online multiplayer games lag so bad that a lot of the time players lose connection to the host. This issue seems to get even worse when more players join the server. I have noticed that when the server has 8 or more players, de-sync gets so severe with the animals that they will freeze for a few seconds and then reappear several meters away from their previous position. Imagine the difficulty of shooting at a moving target when this happens. Also, if the host leaves the game, you will lose any progress you made during that match because of the broken save file. If they would simply implement host migration when the host quits the game it would make the game at least half as frustrating as it is. Dedicated servers would be a better alternative, but at this point that is wishful thinking. There are guides on how to fix the save issue but honestly to me it is borderline hacking because you can be a new player and give yourself 1000000 tokens just by editing a save file.
I can only recommend this game if you are a die hard theHunter fan and this game is on Steam sale. Casual players, it isn't worth the $10. If you really wanna try it out, be ready to deal with the numerous bugs, random level reseting crashes, and laggy online gameplay.
I have also submitted a support request to theHunters support page on their website and one of the developers emailed me that they are aware of the issues and are looking into a fix. When that fix is and what they will do is beyond me. If you are interested in buying this game I would wait a month or two and see if they release any patches first. Fingers crossed.

This was an amazing game , and a great experience. Everyone should play this game.
Now for the spoilers
The only reason I can see why people dislike the game, is either they missed the message , or they got stuck . or they are trying to criticize parts of the game that were intentialy strange , because thats the point of them. case in point for 2 of the three reasons previously mentioned is a section in that you have to shoot green vases and jump pillar to pillar, and about 1/4th the way through you have to start jumping on the sides and on other strange parts that most other games wouldnt have you jump on, this makes it very hard because these areas are round , or just in wierd places. But that was the point, during this part of the game , the character is litterally on drugs , if it was inteded to make sense im sure they could have made it make sense , but it was supposed to be a drug induced halucination, in which things are strange an dont make sense, and to relay that onto the player , they make you do strange things and follow paths that dont make much sense in a conventional style of gameplay.
The only thing I can complain about, is that since the game designers didnt have any actual human models in the game, some parts of the game can be a bit annoying, a great example would be in the house mission , when you have to hide in a closet to survive, the only indication of how far away your pursuers are , is the light shinging through the doorway, so you never see them, and even if your out of eyeshot of a real person, if your not hiding in the closet you will die. Later in the mission you again have to run away from them , but this time instead of hiding you actually run, and it took me a few times to figure this part out because there is an escape lever you can hit that allows you to fall through the floor and I thought that was the way to go, it isnt and it serves no other purpose really other than to prank the player the first time they throw the lever, but I digress. In this part again because they have no actual models for people or damage models for getting shot, even tho the sound effects lead you to believe your getting shot at, there is no one shooting at you, or anyone there at all. just sound effects, now in away this can be justified by the fact that again , your character is on drugs , and he is being pursued by someone he has never seen and the human brain cant make faces of people you havnt actually seen in real life , but im just looking to far into this at that point. But its annoying if you go the wrong way in that part , and yet still hear people shooting at you and the soud effects making it sound like they are RIGHT BEHIND YOU when no, they arnt anywhere near you.
Other than those minor complaints , this game is amazing fun to play on a day you dont have much better to play, or if your internet goes out as mine did. Great fun, and would recommend it to everyone to try.

Like many of the recent years' entries, one again another one arrives with some improvements, but core aspects of the game remain poor, if not outright broken at launch.
As the same as in previous years, the goalkeeper AI is hideously unpredictable with a healthy dose of fumbling the ball either into his own net or in front of someone who instantly puts it in the net.  In addition, distribution from the goalkeeper is DIRE.  Far too many kicks go directly to opposition players who are standing in acres of free space.
Defenders, AI is also poor, either that or tactics are not being recognised correctly.  No matter how much you tell them to close down, tackle hard, man mark... nope, you can guarantee that if the ball is crossed in from the wing or from any distance, it will land at the feet of the opposition striker who has NO ONE within 5-10 years, and he then skins them to score.
Passing, also DIRE.  Either an issue with the engine or again poor AI/recognition of tactics.  Short passing and retaining possession for instance is irrelevant... the team will still try long balls and miss their supposed target by a country mile. Same thing as Goalkeepers basically.
About the only one that works is strikers... they seem to get a realistic number of goals/assists, a goals to shots ratio.
And also, there seems to be a heavy imbalance towards "smaller" teams to boost them against larger player teams.  Yes there's some "cupsets" that take place in the real world, but dominating performances seem non-existent.  Same effect seems to apply in the league games where a team that's got 3 wins out of 30 will suddenly destroy you 5-0 when you're at home.
So yeah... as always, the game has launched with a sense of imbalance/bugs/brokenness that will probably not get fixed for 3 months.
In short... after just over a week since early-access, I'm close to uninstalling it and this will definitely be the last version of Football Manager I buy.  The whole series has been a frustrating, broken mess since they brought in the 3D match engine.
It's just not worth the effort now.  So, I'll be retiring at the end of the season.  Let someone else deal with this.

I would have to reccomend this game higly so. It is a breath of fresh air into the 4X gaming community. Big changes from any Civ game you would have ever played when it comes to technology or how cities work. The fighting in this game is long but it's more enjoyable than watching simple animations playing out between strong unit and stronger unit. Manual controll if you are compitent will always be better than auto however it does take a good chunk of time. The races in the game are very unique even with a race that plays well (much better than Venice) and can keep up with the other races. Like Civ games you can buy out buildings but you do not get them the turn you buy them, in that way so you can't rush build if you weren't paying attention to your borders and didn't notice a army. You must wait at least one turn before bought items take effect taking up likely 1-0 production so that the building after wil use what's left to finish on it. Your race has only 5 units and only 4 are buildable or customizable. Militia is the only one you cannot customize the rest being Settlers your archer, support, flying, calvery, and/or ifantry and as you are thinking you can't have them all. You can however get the others by taking over small villages of minor factions in your territory than taking them into your civilization allowing you to build their one unit which is usually more powerful than faction units. You will also gain a bonus depending on the minor faction. Earlier I mentioned customization, you will be giving your units armor, weapons, and accesories which improve their skills but cause them to cost more production and depending on the type it will cost a certain material. You will also have hero units to customize, eahc of them will act as an ambassidor or a general in your army which will be all in one stack in this game. You cna level them to buff your army or buff your city so you really cna specify what they can or should be. Heroes can also equip hero only items unlocked by the quest system in the game or what can be found in ruins which can lead to the quest system. Of course you can win my domination science, expansion, diplomacy, or the faction quest. I'll let you figure out the rest on victories. Note you do have a good amount of customization of the world you will be playing on. You also may create your own custom faction with basic customization on talents and what you want to be your base faction. Unfortunatly you cannot customize the quest or units on the Custom faction you just get the base units. There is a Winter system in the game, during the season practically everything will decrease by at least 1 and food production will be cut in half. Each time you discover 9 different technologies you will advance to the next era like Civ but you will not be directed through branches, instead you can select any tech you want but believe me it's hard to get them all so just get what you need if possible and go to the next.
In the end this game was extremely enjoyable for as you might be thinking from this review and I hope if you do choose to buy Endless Legend that you will find equal enjoyment in the product.

One of my favorite games of all time.
An action RPG (more RPG than ARPG, you mind), with an in-deapth storyline and good loot tables. They did a fantastic job with the atmosphere of each area, capturing the feeling of darkness and turmoil in each zone while keeping the individuality of each location.
The combat is challenging, and each playable character brings a feeling of uniqueness to the combat. The followers add support that (at times) is much needed. The loot system is decent, and upgrades feel exciting. Watching your gear change as you gain levels is as satisfying as it is in any other well-done ARPG.
As long as you're not looking to play this game with friends, you'll find DS3 to be a well-rounded, immersive game with a storyline that will suck you right in.

This is a great take on 2-D, turn-based strategy games, very similar in design to the Combat Mission series of games, but with a Fantasy-RPG perspective.  The game's core game-play (so far) focuses on the Planning and Execute phase.
During the Planning Phase, you move your characters around the map within the limitations of your characters movement ability in 5 second segments and issue orders to attack based on (typically) 3 different parameters: Auto, Adjusted, and Manual.  Auto involves a zone-of-control where any visible enemy that falls within that radius gets attacked, but enemies take less damage; Adjusted allows you to place a smaller attack radius within a certain distance of your character and attacks any enemy that falls within that radius, for normal damage; Manual has no attack radius and relies on direct contact and inflicts the most damage of the three, but requires being able to predict the enemies location precisely.
Once you've planned all your character's actions, you can then hit the Execute button to watch it all play out in 5 seconds of real-time.  Rinse-wash-repeat.  It takes a little bit of time to get the hang of it, but the game-play emphasizes predicting your enemies movements and attacks (there is an indicator to tell you which character a specific enemy is targeting) which I do like, but can be a bit easy fighting an enemy one-on-one.  Fortunately, many of the fights involve multiple characters and enemies to juggle and to me, that's where the complexity lies.
On paper, you would think it would turn into a "they're attacking so I defend, ad nauseam" kind of game-play, but there are things you can do to affect the outcome of battle, like intercepting other enemies and applying an attack or defensive option as they attack a weaker or near-dead character (thereby protecting them), so long as you can get in the way of the enemy.  Because of this, the combat doesn't turn into a simple slug-fest and is very refreshing, forcing you to consider many options, and not just in terms of pure statistics.
Graphic-wise, the game has a really nice pixel-art, 8-bit aesthetic, reminiscent of "Sword & Sorcery" (but then again, it could just be the limitations of pixel art games) with beautifully rendered environments and character designs (within the limitations of pixel art, again), with the characters a nice mix of eastern and western influences (it seems).  Throughout the game there are numerous little touches here and there (such as on the world map, how the clouds seem to move and part, revealing some areas of the map) that add to the feel and look of the world and give it a level of ambiance that some games are sorely lacking.
Music-wise, they have done an incredible job as well, with the style of music bringing me back to the days of Chrono-trigger, Tactics Ogre, and Final Fantasy Tactics, not in the sense of a carbon copy, but one that has the trappings and nostalgia of the era, with a personality all its own.  The tracks are varied, beautiful, appropriate to the mood, and are a key component in providing a sense of wonder (along with the graphics).  They go hand in hand very well.
Story-wise, the game is good, although key elements of the story are not really revealed in the current build of the game (purposely done) and it's understandable since the game isn't complete as of yet.  What exists is definitely intriguing, although it's too early to say whether it's something of a standard fare or something different, or maybe a bit of both.  I'm hoping it strays more from its JRPG roots to give something less standard, but I also appreciate an uncompromising story told by the author,  as long as it is told well.
I personally love the game so far, although it should be said that this game is far from complete and is being made by an extremely small team (of 2, I believe), so you should consider that if you plan to purchase the game.  I would expect to see infrequent updates due to the time commitments of the two developers, with patience and understanding being a prerequisite when purchasing this game.
The reason I bought the game was because I tried the demo and loved it, and the $10 price tag was a small sum to pay for an interesting game like this, with the expectation that, as more content is developed and expanded upon, it will be well worth my time and money in the long run (plus a developer needs to eat), but it isn't without it's caveats.  Balance and design seems to still be in process, so expect things to change for better or worse, depending on your mindset.
I definitely recommend this game, but only if you are prepared to deal with it's long gestation time and the constraints of the developers.  Going into the game like that, it made it much easier for me to accept the 3 hours of game-play that it offers, but if this is a tip of the iceberg, then the rest, once developed, should be a very unique and enjoyable experience.

Some bits feel like Myst, some bits feel like Amnesia, all in one queer head-trip that will leave you puzzled and uncomfortable.
For the price of free, I give it my full recommendations, but with the caveat that it's there for people that enjoy simmering in the surreal and have the patience to push or sometimes bungle through a puzzle that gives little to no explanation. Give it one evening and treat it like an abstract novella more than a whole game- if you're not likely to read strange fiction, give this one a pass.

$9.99 I can almost recommend this game, but not all the way.  Let me explain.  The environment has been done supurbly.  The foilage could be adapted for any vietnam shooter, the rain, the weather in general is awesome.  The sound effects are top notch.  Very few games can claim to have audio like theHunter: Primal.  I bought this in early access, and at that time, i gave it 5/5 stars, it seemed brilliant before its release, and I couldn't wait for the rest to be added into the code.  But with a very few additions of dino quantity, and no real improvement in dino graphics, this game still falls short of its potential.
When you think of a dino world, you do think about the Jurassic Park type of world.  You think about valleys teaming with duck bill dinos, brontos, stegosaurs, all sorts of herbavors (sorry about the spelling) - everywhere you look....with the meateaters hiding in the foilage ready to ambush you at any turn.  This game has about 6 dinos now, all of them, with the exception of the triceritops wants to eat you....and they are all in their predictable locations.  When you do find one, there is no wind or scent type of system, so, they can't smell you.  They just rummage around until they get close to you.  Or you sneak up on them.
Getting back to the graphics, the dinos seem to be in about 10 angles of the 3D spectrum.  Meaning you will see them at 90 degrees, and they turn toward you and the graphics will jump to 45 degrees and then 0 degrees heading toward you, so they really never refined the smooth transitions of the dinos.  It's still in the pre-release stages.  I found this frustrating, but if you read the review from other of the developers game, not surprising.  Updates are few, and now only to stop a bug or few.  So, I've given up hope of anymore dino additions or improvements.
For this reason, I am resubmitting my review to a mediocre 5/10 stars.  Yes, there is fun to be had, multiplayer can be fun if you have a team that works together, so, it's not all that bad and a $9.99 price right now, is about where it should be.

As mentioned before faction mechanics are unique and vary how you play the game out. Multiplayer games with friends are a lot of fun and produce good banter and by good banter I mean top kek banter.

Cons: There aren't many things I dislike about this game but they influence the game experience a LOT. The game bugs when playing multiplayer are great in number and nearly always game breaking. I can't tell you how much of actual game time I've spent trying to work out these bugs. I seem to see most bugs come from trying to reload saved games as host, from players disconnecting or god forbid players who have disconnected wanting to reconnect. Resyncing can turn into an absolute nightmare and EVEN WITH SAVING you can still lose that awesome game you invested 4 hours into. The other con is pretty minor and it's really only a preference thing but this game is time consuming.
Conclusion: This game is the bomb without the bugs but bugs can destroy your entire multiplayer experience with this game. The main reason I published this review is to provide visibility to the bugging problem and hopefully this will get the developers to act fast.

I bought this game during the Steam Winter Sale and felt deceived by all the overwhelmingly positive reviews. Firstly, I have to say I enjoyed the art and voice-acting. The story was intriguing enough that I played through all five worlds so that I could figure out the entire mystery.
But Amnesia left me with a really bad taste in my mouth. It doesn't portray any healthy relationships, and makes light of verbal and sexual abuse, kidnapping, and murder in the name of love. It feels like the company is going for  dark, edgy stories, but they're creating some really horrible and abusive male characters in the process. "Anything is okay, as long as I love you" is the message that gets sent. It's not romantic or beautiful, it's creepy and disturbing. I didn't get the warm, fluffy feelings I was looking for, but unsettling ones instead.
I needed brain bleach after Toma's route, in which you're held hostage "for your own protection." Shin, the token bad boy that dishes out tough love and verbally abuses you throughout his entire story, was intolerable. Yes, there is Kent, the only normal one, but he was too little, too late. Playing through all the routes, I didn't feel as if I was being offered different stories about love, but more of the same crap treatment. While I wanted to run in the opposite direction, getting the good endings required me to love him unconditionally no matter what he did to me. I know Amnesia is a work of fiction, but toxic relationships should not be romanticized. I really wish the men were better people. Then I would have actually enjoyed this game.
It also made me uncomfortable and gross to play as a helpless female character that goes along with everything the men feel like doing and saying to her. She is sexually harassed in most of the routes. She is drugged and caged in a second, and murdered multiple times in a third. Yet, she says nothing, never fights back, and forgives instantly. For the entirety of the game, she comes off as a passive and docile robot doll whose life revolves around not offending her love interest. I wonder if the developers think this is an attractive way to act in relationships--meek, obedient, and willing to forgive all the horrible things done to her. The MC could have easily been written as someone proactive and smart, and unwilling to take BS. I would play the hell out of a game like that. But instead, we got someone whose dialogue choices are literally "..." or "...Um."
Lastly, all the other women in the game, with the exception of her best friend, Sawa, are created to be jealous of the attention MC is receiving from men to the point of bullying and attempting murder on her. It really aggravates me when female characters are created to be so one dimensional, as if women's lives revolve solely around hating and plotting against each other.
Honestly, I feel bad that I supported a game like this instead of one with healthy portrayals of relationships, respectful treatment and representation of women, and a strong heroine. I'm in the process of playing Nameless ~The one thing you must recall~ by Cheritz, the amazing company that developed Mystic Messenger. So far, I would highly recommend it over Amnesia. The MC has a personality and the men are likable and not creepy. Cheritz also made Dandelion - Wishes brought to you -. Please consider giving these games some love.

Victoria 2 is a fantastic game that is probably not for everybody. I personally have over 350 hours into it, and it's one of my favorite games. That said, I have never played a game with a more complex learning curb than Vic2. I spent several hours on the tutorial before starting it, and it probably took me another 15 hours to 20 hours to really start to understand it. It took me over 100 to master it. Be prepared for a challenge if you delve into this game.
That said, it is extremely rewarding. You have free reign to play any country in the world that existed in 1836, and you can do whatever you want with it. Want to become an industrial powerhouse? Go for it. Want to counquer all of your neighbors, good luck. You can play an easy game as one of the starting great powers, or you can take small, insignificant nations and build them to greatness. For example, my greatest personal accomplishment was taking Punjab and retaking all of India from the European powers to ahistorically form India. One of the beautiful parts of this game is the historical accuracy, but with the freedom to create ahistorical realities.
If you are ready to take on the challenge, I strongly encourage you try out this game. I also strongly encourage buying both expansion packs right off the bat, as the game is nowhere near its full potential without them. Enjoy!

Dungeon Siege III is the third game byu the Dungeon Siege franchise developed by Square Enix. Let me just start by saying that i probable have player more than 80 % of Square Enix tittles and i love their games so much!
Graphics/Art: The graphics are smooth and the game is optimized well so it can play on older devices aswell. The enviroment is very good (not the best) but very enjoyable and the cutscenes are awesome aswell. There ae not much to be said about the raphics of the games, but certainly it is a big improvment from its predecessors. Soundtracks help you get in the mood of action as they feature a medieval/action/epic rythm.
Plot: The storyline was very good and interesting. As a classic RPG you have to complete quests to move on through the game. Those quests can be main storyline or substory quests. In general there is nothing hard about getting the flow of the game as it is very specific on what you have to do and where you have to go. You dont really have to search around for what you have to do, you just follow the indicator. In general for a fan oof the series its a very satisfying game as you even explore and area directly related from the first game of the series which is awesome if youve been there before!
Gameplay: As a classic RPG you have the overwatch camera where you see a fixed amount of map and you character which is a little bit annoying because you would get a whole new experiense if you had a different camera. The movement is simple and so are the attack patterns. Each player has 2 combat modes that that one focuses on single target attacks and the other focuses on AOE attacks. Each mode has different skills and abilities. In general the gameplay is interesting and intense some times as the game on the hard difficulty is very hard, almost impossible to complete and the only way of doing so is by playing online with other 3 players. Each boss you fight offers you a different experiense as you have to play by a specific way to defeat each. In general each character offers you a very different experiense, defensive / offensive or close range / ranged attacks.
If you get this game at a daily offer its a pretty sweet deal in my opinion.

The game describes itself as a "surreal first person adventure-puzzle game" and "The game's mechanics are designed to be experimental and unpredictable, to defy the logic of "What you see is what you get"."
Had there been any logic to the game, then maybe it would be the above.
"as an unseen, menacing, radio-bound antagonist will stop at nothing to block Anthony's path at every turn."  Well, for the first 5 minutes, yeah.
Let's start with the main menu of the game: Continue, Start and Quit.  Booting up the game gives me a launcher to rebind keys, choose how the game looks "Beautiful", "Fantastic" and "Good" being options.  Nothing else.  No AA.  No Volume sliders.  I can't choose whether or not I want  V-Sync.  Captions WHICH ARE GREATLY NEEDED  Nothing.
What I saw: A good-looking game.  A little too much memage for the achievements but they don't really matter
What I got: More of what I lost.  I wasted time on this game but I'll try to explain what I "experienced" (there are things that are called good and bad experiences) through my playthrough.
A game with some bugs such as collision and direction.  During the "Windmill" level, I managed to clip out of the mapby crawling through fire.  Had I known that the direction I took was incorrect, I wouldn't have crawled around for a good 7 minutes before getting stuck in a pit of the bottom of the lake.  I verified, re-installed and verified again.  I encountered the same "bug" all 4 times
The voice acting wasn't so good.  I've done some VAing but I'm not a professional or anything so forgive me if I'm just bad at critiquing them.  The quality of the recording equipment sounding good; there wan't any echo or the "through a can" sound that comes with bad equipment.  The acting, not so much.  The main character sounds really bored and disinterested in what's happening around him or what he's doing.  Oh, you got found and are going to be shot in the head?  "No... please..."  No, not "No! PLEASE!" just a flat "No" and "please" will suffice for this character.  The antagonist?  I can't tell if he's supposed to be hispanic, from Boston or what.
Usually, I couldn't hear what they were saying and had to crank up my volume way up.  Problem is, some segments are at a good volume so I'll blow my ears out at times.
Textures were good looking. but oddly placed.  Again, in WIndmill, the ground textures (leaves, dirt and sticks) were found at the bottom of the lake.  I also fell through the water and the lake.
Gameplay is minimal.  Press E, Walk, smash space or "E"  It plays more like an Amnesia custom level more than anything (you even hide in a dresser at one point, hiding from 2 enemies.).  Don't know what to do?  You're out of luck.  You either run around trying to find things to interact with, wait for the MC to talk and hopefully give you a hint or just get lucky.
Can you start from where you left off?  Depends.  Do you remember the name of the level?  No?  Understandable; you have to go the the "Esc"/pause menu.  Doesn't pause when you go there either so if you're, again, in the Windmill level and have to smash you interact button, guess what, you just died.
Inventory?  No.  Health?  No.  Map?  No.  Compelling?  Not really.  Forgettable?  Yes, most definitely.  Fun?  Uh...  I didn't find it fun.  Didn't find a puzzle either, unless gathering items are the puzzles, then these are flipping cake compared to Professor Layton or Puzzle Agent.  But if finding out what to do is the puzzle, then this blows Ace Attorney, Professor Layton, Puzzle Agent and, hell, even Kryptos out of the water.  I'm not asking for hand-holding (I love challenges, not artificial difficulties or just bad game design making it hard) but I want to know that I've going in the right direction at least.  Now, the first three usually don't matter for a game and usually not a "puzzle" game like this one but the last 3?  Yeah, those are important for every game.
I was really dissapointed in the game if you couldn't tell.  Wanted to like it because the first two or three reviews seemed to really, and suspiciously, praise the game for everything I found fault with it.

The game is smooth. I have an average build PC and I have never yet experienced lag or crashing, which I had to deal with on a regular basis with Civ. I play multiplayer a lot with friends, and yes the turns slow down as the game gets longer, but not by a huge amount.
