Everyone throws massive showers of praise on this game, they love the factions, they love the rpg elements, they especiallly love all it's new twists on the 4X stategy genre. And I enjoy these things, the RPG elements with regiments and heroes is really cool, the battles are an interesting twist from the norm, the quests are cool and the factions are all very disinct in look, play and lore.
However, I must stress caution with this game, don't expect a masterpice, becasue it isn't, the increadible amount of praise on this doesn't take into account all of this games problems, which is what i'm going to stress here.
I first played this game when my friend brought it over on his laptop, I would play a few quick, short games and they where so much fun, and indeed the start of the game is a lot of fun. But once I had the game and started longer playthroughs, I began to get bored really quickly. The game is great when you start it up, but as you get further in, it becomes a drag. This is largely the fault of a terrible AI, which isn't a good thing to have in a game for a genre that is heavily reliant on single player.
The Ai just doesn't know how to play this game, it will always build the same armies over and over again, in one playthrough it will build full stacks of Dragonlings, and only that, then next playthrough it will build 6 wyverns and two ancients per army, and thats it, it will take a stack and only build that stack, and this makes battles in one playthrough increadibly repetitie and boring. It's play style will never suit the scenario, andf it will almost never declare war on you. It's increadibly easy to beat as well, and this means that games become a drag to play through till the end.
The quest system, while initially pretty cool, has multiple problems, for one it won't often make sense what it demands of you, for instance it may tell you to conquer a city from someone you've signed an alliance with when there is someone else much closer who isn't your ally. Biggest problem however is that they can become uncompletable very easily. You can get a quest asking you to do something that you've alrady done, and as a result the quest becomes incompletable. I remember with horror when in one of my campaigns I got a quest to increase the population of one of my cities to a certain level, and found that the population was already at that level, and then the quest became incompletable! And this was a faction quest, the kind nessisairy to continue the storyline!
The winter system too, while initially cool (no pun intended), helps this drag as it bcomes more and more frequent the further you go into the game, and this helps add to the drag that you start to feel the further in you go.
There are some other problems, but most of them are really negligable, the biggest dissapointment is that these issues could all be fixed with a better AI, and so it is with a heavy heart that must say i can't recomend this game, despite all the effort in the art style, the lore and all the unique mechanics, the poor AI just makes this game soo boring. So I say don't buy this game, at least not yet, if they fix the AI then it'll have my full recomendation, but until that stage, I just have to say no.

Badass Hero is a roguelite platformer where the action hero under your control goes through the comic book universe. The game is well styled: each level is shaped like comics which you traverse, „picture by picture”. There’s a lot of action going on and the game rewards you being fast: as you kill enemies, your combo meter goes up. The death is inevitable, but as you die, you get a chance to improve your character, making further walkthroughs much easier. During each playthrough, you have a chance to find armor / weapons. You lose them when you die, but they greatly affect how far can you go.
-	Action packed gameplay
-	Plenty of items like armor / potions
-	Very-well polished/juiced: even basic weapons feel awesome to shoot, lots of effects on hits, gore, explosions
-	Responsive character controls, which is very important for the genre
-	World is generated randomly, but there are good room variety so the room layouts do not feel boring
-	Not much weapon variety so far (yes, stats are generated randomly (I think), but shooting patterns do not differ much: gun, smg, shotgun, bazooka, grenades)
-	Only 3 worlds planned, with 2 first ones available (they have plenty of enemies, but backgrounds get repetitive pretty quickly)
One of the biggest achievements of the game, in my opinion, is the way that authors dealt with random element. In roguelites, you often feel cheated when the random is against you. Since initial weapon is not bad and killing enemies is pretty much skill based, there’s no feeling that you are getting dealt a bad hand, which is really commendable.
I think that’s a great game for anyone who’s into Roguelite Platformers. Definitely grab it if you liked Rogue Legacy.

TL;DR: Has a lot of potential, but work to do. Only get this if you want to help forming the game!
*Video contains gameplay, below is the review
Since it just released in its early access state, there is still a lot of content missing. This isn't that big of a deal, if you don't mind following the state of the game and help shaping it up. Also meaning that the current version keeps you amused for a couple of hours at most, till the next content patch comes up.
I personally play with a controller and I do think this game is made for it. Although, if wanted, it can be played with a keyboard and mouse. As for the controller, it feels smooth, has a valid standard layout (which can be changed if wanted) and suits well with the learning curve of the game itself.
Unlike a few other rogue-likes I played, the missiles projected by enemies can't be dodged in any way (like dashing, down stomp) and must be avoided at all costs. This took me some time getting used to, and in some occasions due to RNG being a ♥♥♥♥♥, gave me unfair situations. Rooms filled with enemies, with projectiles coming from everywhere, nearly impossible to avoid. Be that as it may, it seems to be a core element of the game and in general works well apart from those few instances where you get blown to pieces (or atleast lose half of your HP when you where just doing so well!).
Regarding RNG, there is a lot of it in this game, even the bosses are randomized by changing the layout of the environment. Which feels refreshing but as mentioned above, in some occasions can be a bit unfair.
There currently are just a few different weapons (amongst others: smg, shotgun, bazooka, minigun) which are randomized by things like different reload speed, more magazine ammo, freeze/burn effect etc. You do have unlimited ammo, and only shoot with guns (atleast so far, no melee of any kind). While playing you find these weapons along with other items that you can either use for that playthrough or redeem for experience instead.
The enemies feel very different from each other and the animations are well executed. Giving you that learning curve improving with each run you make. Meanwhile leveling up unlocking new abilities like more health, more drops, longer combo time, faster reload speed, etc. (mostly passive). Keeping your combo count up is also pretty important, advancing quickly from one stage to the other getting bonuses from the abilities you unlocked by leveling up in your previous runs.
The music in its current stage is very boring, linear, its basicly one soundtrack that gets more intense when your combo count goes up. However, they mentioned in their early access FAQ this will be completly reworked and is just a placeholder for now.
So all in all, this game has a lot of potential. It might be a bit steep for its current state, but may definitly be worth it in the end. I would only recommend getting this game if you want to try it out for now and help building the game to a solid final release.

Seems simple at first, then you realize that your brain is going to get fried.  This game is hard as hell, and wrapping your head around these puzzles is going to provide you with nightmares for weeks to come.  Level 1 sets you up for level 2 to take you down.  In The Great Permutator you have a soft limit to each stage for the number of conveyor belts and pieces that you use.  In order to get the objects from the top to the bottom, you're going to need to start thinking of how to manipulate the system.
Your soft limit is typically 20 conveyors, but you can place as many conveyors as you want (you just get less score if you go above 20, I guess).  Not readily apparent at first, there is an order to which boxes have to leave the factory first, which is where the true challenge comes in.  You need to figure out ways to make sure the right boxes leave the factory first.  Unlike the "as many as you want" rule, this rule is hard and immutable.  You can't just take a penalty and drop the boxes off in any order.
It's fun if you like puzzlers, but if you don't, then you might as well save your $7 and use it to buy something more your style.

Gameplay wise - this game is great as far as puzzleing goes. Personally I think they could have done more with the presentation, but it's not so important. If you are looking for an intellectual challenge and are interested in finding the most efficient solution to something then this will satisfy that itch.

Pros:
Challenging but rewarding puzzles
Cons:

This review (and probably many others) is going to make nuermous references to SpaceChem.  This is because the mechanics of both games are very similar.  Instead of atoms, each level has boxes to rearrange into the targetted combination.  This is done using conveyor belts and various machinery that sort, rearrange, duplicate and combine them, depending on what you need.  The theme is more 'real world' than SpaceChem and while  I quite liked it, the 2D nature of the conveyor belts restricts the complexity of possible solutions.
As much as it pains me to say, the presentation is somewhat lacking (the whole game is 33 mb).  However, I consider that puzzle games should be ranked on their puzzles alone.  In this case, the levels are straight foward but challenging so that it's a rewarding feeling when you finally solve them.  While I haven't yet attempted the hardest puzzles, based on the difficulty of the earlier ones I expect that each will take a long time to solve.
While SpaceChem is the gold standard for this genre, there's no shame to be in such a great game's shadow.  If you want more, then Great Permutator is worth your time.

Amnesia Memories is a visual novel otome game that you'll surely remember forever! There was never a dull moment for me when playing this game, theres countless things to explore and many ways to play the game. Also, with each route, there will be a good ending, a normal ending and a bad ending (Sometimes theres more than just one bad ending, so be prepared) Not going to lie, sometimes I feel like the normal endings are just as terrible as the bad endings; You should definately strive for the good endings in all routes though. There's four guy's routes in the beginning, but if you stay until the end you'll be able to enter a special world and get a true ending!
When I first started playing this game I was hopelessly obsessed, there's something like a magnetic attraction that charms and pulls you into all the little odds and ends of this game.. With each guy, there's different personality; you're bound to find the one you like. Within the four main routes, the heroine will experience different instances; some lovely, sympathetic, scary or even questionable.. Its all in how you want to interpret the many feelings of this game. Amnesia Memories is also a very humorous game, It's fun to see how things turn out in the end since choices really do matter.
Overall, Amnesia Memories is a gem of a game, don't miss out.. Solid 10/10. If you're still contemplating on buying this game, be sure to have one to multiple boxes of tissues close by, you might just cry a river. (It's better safe than sorry)

What is Awesomnauts? A 2D Platformer Shooter MOBA, where 2 teams of 3 compete to take down the other's drill, while pushing down towers and the drill with friendly drones.
What can be said about it? It's gameplay is extremely solid, leaving a lot to good aim and skilled platforming to determine the better player, in addition to strategy.
It also feels as though they looked at other MOBA's (that shall remain nameless to avoid wars) and thought "What flaws do these games have that can make the game boring, and how can we changes that?" What results is a bunch of simple changes that make the game more engaging, such as respawn times getting partly replaced with a minigame to earn "solar" (in game currency), replacing loading screens with fan-art and themes of the character you chose, a variety of maps (each with gimmicks, such as a giant worm that can pop out when a button is hit), and removing the concept of "items" (now you don't have 20 characters who all build the EXACT. SAME. THING.) and instead special upgrades for your different abilities/attacks (such as increase damage, or give it a stun, or allow multiple uses but less damage per use) but also restricts these upgrades (You can only choose 3 out of 6 possible upgrades per ability, meaning you need to plan ahead due to no selling mechanic).
The music is also amazing, and does not seem to grow old no matter how much I hear it (helped by the fact there is a new song that plays each respawn, as well as if you go on a killing spree). I often find myself listening to it outside of the game itself.
The characters all have a lot of charm to them as well. You have a Worm and Pufferfish partner's in crime going "We are going on a heist here, see?", a space viking out on a war path because he was called fat, and the greatest action hero that ever existed (though we will touch on him later). Simple phrases such as how they taunt and use voice commands to what they say while shopping really show off these characters.
One more great thing about this game: Local Multiplayer. You can play locally with somebody split-screen, but you can team up with them online. Few games do this, and it's welcome to be able to invite a friend over to have them join me for a round or two without them needing to own the game itself.
Finally, unlike most other MOBA type games, you aren't dedicated to a round. People can leave their game (though it DOES count as a loss) at will, and that space gets filled with a Bot player instead of unbalancing the teams (and to be fair, bots are pretty competant in this game, a rare occurance in a lot of games), and a player can eventually replace that bot as well. Most other MOBA type games force you to sit through a whole game, or cripple your team, but this system prevents both of those issues.
So what is wrong with it? Well, it's not nice to new players. A LOT of upgrades have to be unlocked, and while this is nice at first as to prevent a player from being overwhelmed, some important upgrades (such as damage for assassin type Nauts) don't get unlocked until hours upon hours of gameplay. Also, new players have a good chance to be paired up with players who have a LOT of experience (a flaw in a lot of multiplayer games) simply due to the system, where it pairs you against people of a similar ranking.
Also, there is no dedicated servers. While it's nice as this means the game is never full, since players host the games themselves, this can lead to lag and hits are based on the client of the attacker. This can lead to some cheap deaths just because somebody is lagging or the host does not have a computer suited to hosting.
Then there is DLC. Now, I wouldn't mind paying the $5 more to get the whole game, but it feels like I have been ripped off when I buy the game just to find out I can't use 5 characters because I haven't dropped money into it (Such as the afformentioned Ted McPain, greatest action hero alive).
Finally, and this is a nitpick, but there are a LOT of references. Now, I am a person who likes a small reference now and then, but this game feels like a lot of humor comes from simply getting those references (A lot of characters items are references... There's even an upgrade called "Skrogachu" with a picture of what is clearly supposed to be a Pikachu.
Overall, great game, though network issues could be improved. It's worth the money, worth playing through it, but expect to get kicked in the teeth by seasoned players for a bit. Get past that, you'll appreciate the game.

Just finished my Germany campaign. Through brute aggression I forced the creation of Poland which was to serve as my buffer to the Russian Empire who was quite keen on aligning herself with Austria, France, and Britain. Poland was under my protection (my sphere, my ally) and they were invaded. They sent me a request for help but it just disappeared within about 15 seconds while I was trying to figure out the situation and prepare. Apparently their Casus Belli prevented me from getting involved.
Suddenly it's Poland vs. Spain, Britain, Austria-Hungary and a few other powers. All I could do was prevent them from entering my territory.
I decided I wasn't going to be limited by such petty rules. I was like a father to the Poles. So I decided to justify a war against Austria-Hungary (just asking for some random territory of theirs). It was great for Poland. I swept through their conquered lands and reestablished their military. I conquered France, Austria-Hungary, and Spain. Poland comes out victorious with more territory (I joined the war because the great powers were demanding Poland secede their own territories. The war started because Poland wanted more land).
Well, of course I get punished with infamy. Poland doesn't want to be my ally anymore because I was too infamous.
I got mad. Poland no longer wanted to be my friend? Queue the Fascist takeover of Germany by my hand. I declare war on Austria-Hungary. Invade France, invade Austria, land ships in Britain and let Irish nationals rebel and take land while Britain burns. March eastward into India fabricating wars with any nation that opposed my armies.
I have maximized my technology.
I became Hitler.

USA still got 1st place.

Some War among the powers begins. Not WWI but something fairly large. Britain is at odds with other powers. Now is my chance! I invade the final seaport province I had lost. Victory! >:)
Then Britain signs peace treaties and takes care of their final order of business: Me.
I dig in. Machine guns are loaded. Education other useless commodities of the posh are cut to 0. We mobilize and prepare.
As Britain takes my land they finally reach my defensive positions. Welcome my friends....
They suffer staggering losses but these people don't quit. They're so committed to the sovereignty of some pitiful state. I fight hard but there are too many.

WORLD WAR FRIGGIN 1. I started it! Me! I'm basically Princip! Germany, Italy, Belgium, Denmark, Turkey, etc. join me in my struggle for freedom from the Austrian oppressors!

Many indie platformers display a distinctive failure mode in which partway through, the designers clearly decided that the first part of the game has allowed you to master the controls and thus there is nothing wrong with now demanding prolonged spells of absolute perfect control mastery.

For me, the last straw was "This long corridor has a lethal floor and ceiling, so you must use your jetpack - which only has two settings, 'off' and 'full throttle' - to keep yourself in mid air. There are barriers spanning half the height of the corridor at regular intervals, alternately protruding from the floor or ceiling. You must traverse this corridor fast enough to keep up with the NPC you are pursuing, but not so fast that you go off-camera (the camera is locked to the NPC rather than you)."
I cannot recommend it, but if you don't mind that sort of thing, I dare say it's a good example of the style.

Okay let me write my first serious review, ayy?
Okay, the game  has a solid idea, i won't go into story, since that is pretty well marked in the game, and story shoudln't be the main point onto playing a platformer.
The graphics, look pretty decent, sometimes things get cluttered, but overall the characters look nice in the 16bit aesthetic, music is pretty nice, a bit repetitive (I'll get to it) And overall, very nice.
The problem comes to the gameplay.
The controls are very responsive, however, they are built in such a way, to dash, you just double click to go to a direction, that doesn't work very well, due to the game being full of death traps and pits, you'll often die because you dashed at the wrong time, or because  you simply didn't dash, your character moves pretty quickly for a robot, and that is not a really good thing.
Think of megaman, on heatman stage, but istead, blocks have much bigger gaps at times, and you move at speed of sonic, you can upgrade and go light speed for a short time, but that may be too much, going just small gaps is difficult on this game due to this.
The missile, is already fast, by default, if you play on the hardest setting, you better learn how to control that or you won't pass the game. On megaman x5, you get a laser firefly, that moves slowy, and is only required in one part of the game to get a BONUS thing, it also is expensive, like in this game, but at least it pays it by being slow, controlable. The missile spends too much, and goes too quick for a REQUIRED part of the game, if you don't like using it you better learn liking it.
Bosses, from what i saw, don't get me wrong i couldn't get far into the game, and bought this mostly for the cards, but man, the bosses are meatboy-like, at least from the part i played, i don't know if it goes into a real fight later, but well, i can tell you this meat boy sonic the megaman is going to annoy you, specifically early, and a little less late. Due to the whole " the world is falling behind you " side scrolling, you may get anxious and accidentally dash/not dash when you needed to. It's a huge trial and error, there are check points, but not really enough to make up the speed-paced character.
I know this may be just me being bad at the game, but man, sometimes countering an attack on a moba, where your main tower is on 1 hp, seems to be more enjoyable and less frustating than this.
I wouldn't recommend this game to who doesn't have enough reflexes to deal with this, i can recommend it, to who enjoys fast paced games of different kinds (I think even a touhou fan would like to try this)
If there is any grammar/spelling error, sorry, i'm not the best when it comes to english.
That is all, i have respect for this game, i like it overall, but those gameplay issues just seem too big for me.
TL;DR : I recommend in case you like fast paced, almost pixel perfect games, but i wouldn't recommend if you are more onto the slow paced, later fast paced games.

If you enjoy Civ and the fantasy genre appeals to even a little bit, this is a great game. Each of the factions has an interesting and asymmetrical schtick. You can customize and/or upgrade your units. As you acquire more territory, you have access to minor factions which grant a passive bonus to your entire empire as well as access to a unit blueprint representing that faction.
The basics are simple— FIDSI are exactly what you'd expect. They compose with myriad other mechanics to produce an incredible level of nuance and complexity.
Don't let the word "complexity" scare you off. If you play a game or two on Newbie/Easy, you have a chance to fiddle around with everything, and learn more about it. Personally, I do not enjoy complexity for its own sake. I assumed that (e.g.) customizing units was going to be tedious but necessary. It's not tedious, it's relatively simple, and I don't believe it's necessary to min/max.
If you enjoy turn-based 4X strategy, you owe it to yourself to check out this game.

For all the jokes my friends kept taunting me with for saying I am playing Amnesia and dating hot guys instead of running away from barrels, illuminated by a solitary oil lamp, I finally have to write a review to give this game justice.
And well, get back to reviewing stuff now that university is over, lolololol.
This otome is one of the best I've played so far, if not THE best amongst the paid ones. I've been checking out some free games from NaNoReno challenges and let me tell you - storylines in some of the free stuff FAR surpass the scripts of paid content. But, Amnesia is a great story, great gameplay and great experience, and a benchmark I use against any new otome games I want to play. I got it last autumn when it initially went on the big -90% sale, and I believe you really should be on a look-out for it as it has been done again for the Summer Sale, and you could have snatched the title for mere 2 quid instead of paying over 22 pounds.
The sprites are beautiful! And I really mean it when I say beautiful. Each guy is very distinctive, with their flair of style, set of clothes and colours. Supporting characters are unique as well, easily recognizable in each route. Even though some people complain about the backgrounds, I actually like the Photoshop, minimalist style of them - considering the careful design of characters, you'd get a headache if everything was just as detailed. Apart from that - expressions! The changing poses (although, I have to say this, most times Shin and Ikki look AWEFUL facing back, and some of Ikki's CGs look as if he was a different person altogether, with very wonky features. It's been a let-down for me, as I've seen art from later Amnesia games and he looked good in them, not only when facing front. Oh well, can't have Medusa eyes beautiful from all angles, right?). The change in lighting and colours is a very good touch as well, "sunset setting" is done really well, as well as when night comes around and the whole colour scheme of backgrounds changes. BEAUTIFUL.
So far I've found two of my favourites, and have been constantly replaying their routes, with Shin first and now Ikki settled as my fav, fav, FAV character for a long while. Each guy has their own problems, quirks and things you are going to learn about them only if pursuing them directly, I really like the setting of having separate worlds and interacting with recurring characters in different circumstances. For once, Ikki made a "whatever" impression on me outside of his own route but baby, in his own - GOLD, GOLD, GOLD SWEET BABY.
And it's really satisfying

Visual novels rely mostly on your own control over the story, and I find the choices here pretty varied, and actually compelling. Endings are really good overall, although true ones could be potentially more romantic. BAD ENDS however, oh MAN. I LOVE THEM. THEY'RE SO SICK. Like, really, really bad. It's no "oh man I'm lonely blah, blah", it's actual♥♥♥♥♥♥going down,
, and other drama, Bad ends are actually one of the reasons I use Amnesia as a benchmark while judging other games - it's an art to make bad choices entertaining, and have people investigate all options. Some of them are hidden so well, I had to resort to Let's plays to even notice what pattern you should have taken to even start on their route of destruction The menu is really helpful to keep track of all those already opened, or still left to witness.
There are two mini-games within the main menu you can play, some of the CGs are interactive where you can hear more from the characters "in that exact moment" after poking them a lot, and there are so called "Memories" that I find most entertaining of this bunch. It's the defining moment in each route that you can replay to learn more about the guy in that highlighting moment, and it's really, really sweet! Only after completing the route do they open, I believe, and only after checking them out will you realize the normal playthrough kind of omits the stuff said without losing an ounce of the romance. Clever screenwriting, I have to say, because it is essentially cut content you only notice missing after having played a Memory.
Even though the trope of an amnesiac MC is an overused trope, this was the first game for me with it (lucky me!) and so it did not feel straining to go through the motions and the journey of reclaiming them. Guys are awesome, choices do matter, your heroine is actually pretty well rounded for not having memories for much of the playthrough - what I mean, is that you learn from interactions with the guys how mostly independent and level-headed she's been up to her amnesia, which is really nice for a change. I am currently playing OZMAFIA!!, and let me tell you - the MC in Amnesia is a Terminator compared to the MC there, who is simply an idiot that goes rogue against your own choices, fair and square.
Amnesia is much less frustrating in this regard, but I have not even fully unlocked a romance of OZMAFIA!! so yup, not gonna give up hope yet.
As said already, be on the lookout for promotions and discounts, as the premiere last year was a big success, and more high budget otomes have started appearing on Steam (OZMAFIA!! as one of the other key productions) ever since Amnesia got released. Rejoice, rejoice, dear otome brethren! Get on it if you want a really interesting story set in different worlds, AMAZING boyfriends (Ikki is the best, just put up with all the drama, and you'll see), CRAZY bad ends and really pretty artwork.
Now I actually want to
but I miss the edginess of Amnesia. It's a hilariously dark and frightening world the more you think about it, and the more you learn about their problems. So yup, recommend, recommend!

I previously wrote that this game would not load. I found the solution.
If you have the two major DLCs (or just one, at that), you need to download them one by one. I hadn't even downloaded the extra content for the game itself.
Step 1 - Start up the game without the two major DLCs. There should be a download.
Step 2 - Add one of the DLCs. Let it download.
Step 3 - Remove that DLC, add the other, let it download.
Step 4 - Add back both DLCs. Now you can play the game!

This game was amazing back when I played it in 2007. Since then, the detailed graphics and brilliant AI have aged quite a bit (to put it mildly). Thankfully, mods to the rescue!
Oblivion has one of the most prolific modding communities out there. They've been churning it out since 2006 (Oblivion comes with its own mod creator) and you can still find fresh mods on Nexus and other sites.
Because I like to play as Vanilla as possible, I personally favor visually enhancing mods (textures, new NPC faces -- this is especially important, because I can't stand the glowing potato faces of the original), additional soundtracks, and AI-improving mods (especially regarding the Guards and inter-NPC conversations).
The best aspects of this game:
- There's a LOT to explore, and much of it won't be saved on your map. The world is chock-full of secrets, ruins and hidden locations.
- You can create your own spells! So few games give you this much freedom.
- Quests are VERY unique, and every quest adds a bit of backstory into the world. The faction quests stand out as being particularly interesting. It's not like in Skyrim, where you keep doing quests for that one faction quest-giver until you've rescued the faction and become its new leader -- here, factions have multiple branches across the land, and their members have their own feuds, intrigues, alliances.
- The Shivering Isles DLC brings back some of the outlandish fantasy that endeared players in Morrowind. It's a great diversion from the thoroughly Albion-esque landscape of the main game.
The only downside I can think of is the main quest, specifically the Oblivion Gates. They're repetitive, difficult to navigate, blindingly crimson and ruthless. It's like being in a DOOM level but without any of the space marine's weapons :/
This game and Morrowind are very /free/ RPGs. So far, replaying it on Steam, I've spent about 26 hours just doing side-quests and faction quests -- I haven't even progressed in the main quest yet, beyond escaping through the sewers at the very beginning!
Is it better than Morrowind or Skyrim? They're all different. I like the aesthetics, crafting system and melee combat in Skyrim; I like the outlandishness and challenge of Morrowind; and I like the spell-casting, alchemy and quests of Oblivion. Out of all of them, Skyrim is the easiest to slip into and play; Morrowind is the hardest. Oblivion is in a nice medium ground.

Old-school style platformers seem to be all the rage with indie devs. They don't require massive teams of people to create and their low CPU usage results in a wider audience getting to experience the game. Sometimes, though, you just have to wonder if going retro was the best choice.
With Terrian Saga: KR-17, there doesn't seem to be any real defining feature. This is a game based on the likes of MegaMan or old Apogee MS-DOS titles. It's an action platformer with a greater emphasis on platforming. These levels will require you to search for keys to progress; just like the good-old-days.
Still, there really isn't much to it. You find keys, shoot enemies and progress. The game routinely stops to give you frustratingly difficult boss battles, but even those end up being too short. The game breezes by without much of a care.
I suppose that could be noted as a plus, but I never felt invested in this game. The sprite work is fantastic, but the art style puts me off. It looks like a 5 year old's drawings of a "cool" robot he saw. This is almost like if Wall-E got fed up with cleaning the Earth.
The choice of weapons is almost entirely moot, too. While you have access to a bomb, a remote bomb, a claymore and flamethrower, you really only ever need the bomb. It has the most use, deals the most damage and can be lobbed a great distance. Nothing else really matters, apart from a failed attempt at diversity.
Your core blaster even works quite well against every enemy. One foe requires you to dodge when shooting it, but you could take advantage of the invincibility frames and mutilate him. Nearly all the adversaries are the same, too. Just shoot, shoot and shoot some more.
Do I really find the game that unenjoyable? No, honestly. The music is excellent and the level design, itself, is solid. I love old-school style games that require you to remember routes and plan out a perfect path. KR-17 has that in spades. I just wish they lasted longer.
I would also like it if the game would play by it's own rules. In most levels, you have access to a dash ability. Sometimes, within the same section of levels, you lose that ability. You also get a jetpack that carries over into some levels, but not all of them. It becomes confusing and infuriating when you go to dash and then fall into an acid pit.
I also have to take points off for the lame final boss and horrendous cliff-hanger ending. I'm not certain that a sequel will be inevitable, but to end your first title on what basically is a "To Be Continued" screen is just mean.
Still, for $5, you could do worse. Honestly, I'd just check out some of the other retro style platformers on Steam. This one doesn't do much that would differentiate it from the pack.

Let me start by saying I like this game but can not recommend it because of the following reasons:
First of all: There are flying enemies AND YOU CANT SHOOT UP. Only way to kill flying enemies is to use the rocket ,which consumes like a third of your ammo.
The visuals are nice enough ,but the color and inconsistency of the sprites makes it hard to know which sprite is a platform and which is part of the background , and trying to jump on a piece of background is a pretty dumb way to die.
There have also been some poor choices in using said sprites , like for instance in the second area there was a level where you had to navigate a cave while riding a crate floating in water (water instakills you btw) and for some reason the dev decided it would be a good idea to put non transparent sprites in the foreground so they hide the crate you are supposed to ride. That wouldh nave been much of a problem if it weren't for the fact that when you ride crates , you dont really ride them like in most platformers , you have to move with them. if you stop pressing left every 0.5 seconds the crate just continues on its way leaving you to your watery death. Ok thats fine , but they had barrels (or are they wooden logs) that act the same way, which makes sense, as the water is flowing the barrel is turning so you'd have to balance on it. But why crates. In fact , why not putting barrels instead of crates .
This appears to be fixed by turning vsync off
Some sections where you need to control your rocket buddy can be frustrating as hell ,the gaps are way too small , the corners way too sharp and the rocket dude moves way too fast to be controlled adequately , especially with an analogue stick. Most of the longer rocket flying sections will probably take you a few tries to get right , which really breaks the game pacing for me.
There is a game section where you need to hack computer terminals. Hacking is ok except , the game does not pause while you hack. So if there are any enemies around they will attack you. And you cant stop the hacking too , the only way to get out of hacking mode is to mess up. Which costs you one health bar , so you might as well let the baddies hit you.
Other things I just find odd:
The boss sprites look kinda out of place , like the art was made by a different person or even for a different game.
The "cinematics" (Im using that word for the lack of a better one) look weird too , for the same reason , in game sprites look nice and you can tell some work went into them , but the characters in the cinematics look iffy. Like they were drawn in a hurry and then pixelated a little to look more like they fit the whole 16 bit theme.
Other than that its a nice game , with some challenge to it.

is the only game ported to PC from the highly successful otome game series called Amnesia by Otomate and Idea Factory. Originally made for Playstation Portable and later Playstation Vita; Amnesia game series were started in 2011 and it was well received primarily in Japan. Within a year or so, the franchise earned a notable fan base and a reputation all over the world as a high quality otome series with countless merchandise and many sequels. Here we have
, which is actually the 4th game in the series, yet it is consistent and well elaborated enough within its own self, so you don't necessarily have to play any other games to enjoy it.
Our heroine is a college student whose life will take an unexpected and unexplainable turn with the appearance of a spirit called Orion. Apparently, Orion was pulled into our consciousness and merged with our heroine accidentally while he was travelling between worlds. As it may be significant to mention, Orion's merge into our mind pushed our former memories out and our heroine ended up with Amnesia! We have no idea about who we were supposed to be, what was our personality like, whom might be our friends etc. and we are stuck with a spirit only we can hear or see. Luckily, Orion is a good natured one and takes full responsibility of this accident, even agreeing to stay by our side until we can recover our memories and adapt into our life. By the way, it seems that we are surrounded by charming yet problematic gentlemen with interesting backstories whom are desperately in love with us and there is no reason that we shouldn't pursue the romance of our hearts... Will our heroine be able to find her memories and win the heart of her preferred gentleman while doing so?
Cheesy? Yeah, a bit. The storyline isn't terribly imaginative for our chosen romance options, but all their singular stories are relevantly intertwined on a bigger picture. Once you complete four different romance paths with good endings, you'll be allowed to explore a fifth path to take a glance on this bigger picture and discover the reasoning behind seemingly irrelevant plot holes in all other stories. By its ability to collect all different paths in a unified story consistency, the core story is amazing and surely refreshing in this genre. According to my own experience, a solid core story for the starting plot and the setting consistency always wins over pretty romanceable boys with not so interesting personality defects. Thus, the final story was my favorite. Our 4 primary romance, on the other hand, felt a bit rushed and hollow. Sure, the narrative is good, event correlation is amazing etc. but only one of our pretty boys felt like an actually likable sort for me. Then again, this is a matter of taste.
As the game starts, we are asked to choose between four different worlds, where our heroine and any other character connected to her will take a different incarnation and a difference in interrelation. Core liaisons between characters rarely change. In all worlds, we are a college student with psychology major who lives alone, works in a maid cafe named Meido no Hitsuji during the summer and has more or less similar kind of relationships with people around her. In each incarnation, our primary romance target changes though and we gain new opportunities to discover more about our pretty boys.
Artworks are glamorous with a good amount of CGs used. Character designs are a bit flamboyant and exaggerated for my taste - like a Final Fantasy villain fashion show - but they are quite unique. All the boys are designed to be a symbolic representative of four French suits of a pack of cards: hearts (Shin), spades (Ikki), clubs (Kent) and diamonds (Toma) - Ukyo being the joker. That presents an Alice-like taste for the whole game: elegant yet uncanny. All characters are properly voice acted with suitable choices. Environment design might be called stylized, - pastel colored renderings of some basic drawings - but it wasn't really appealing or remarkable.
5 romance paths with each their good and normal endings + a truck load of bad endings thanks to the world being a constant danger to you for some reason + extra memories and short story routes present you a nearly 50-60 hour experience, and this is by skipping already seen text. There is also a great amount of choice options within each path with a good cause - consequence relation presented. If you are not using a guide, I highly recommend for you to take frequent saves. When you are bored of all the drama, you can take a break by playing some mini-games too.
For any otome gamer, Amnesia is a good deal and goes into a decent sale like %90 twice in a year or so. Okay, I'm hushing myself now. It was already hard for me not to spoil the actual story in this review. I'm going away before I blabber about something. Good gaming to you!

An update to my previous review...
I initially recommended this game in the now seemingly childlike state of optimism that the devs would come back and actually take a look at the feedback it had been receiving from a fanbase that was just as youthfully hopeful for change as I was.
I can now say without a doubt in my mind that "Primal" has become another victim of dev neglect.  When I bought this, I was SO excited at the prospect of finally having a survivalist-hunting game involving dinosaurs.  Who doesn't like the sound of the concept?  Beginning with the state of terrified excitement, you blaze a trail through the thick jungle and swamps, up mountains and through valleys, looking for anything with which to give you the upper hand against your quarry.  Keeping in mind that the you were at any point in time both potential hunter and hunted.  Hearing the sound of a pack of Utahraptors sent chills down your spine, or you'd spend minutes divising how to take down a triceratops without the situation turning into a prehistoric Running of the Bulls.
And the always-ominous footfalls of the Tyranosaurus... come on, what's not to like here?
Apparently, the concept seems to be the only thing keeping anyone from freeing up some space in their hard drive as I did.  It blows my mind that the devs have literally left what could have been a spectacular and unique experience to drive itself to extinction.  Aside from the gamebreaking and otherwise irritating bugs, there has been ZERO content added since I last played.  I personally bought the game to see the variety of ancient creatures that would be implemented over time.  When I bought the game, there were 3 species; the Rex, the Utahraptors, and the Trikes.  Over the passing of nearly 1-2 years since buying the game, there have been 2 additions... The core of the game was hunting alone (or with friends, or being hunted by said friends sometimes), facing off against some of the greatest animals to have roamed the earth, which once numbered in dozens if not hundreds of species... and the devs believe that just 5 dinos (and quite frankly sub-par state of the game in general) is enough to warrant a full release, never to be touched again?
Please please please please please save your money for a more worthy venue.  As much as it pains me to write essentially an antithesis to my previous review, I believe it has become clear that the devs are content to leave this project to the very same fate as the dinosaurs themselves.

Before you read too much into this, theHunter: Primal is a good game.
However, the lack of updates and support from developers leaves this game feeling too empty and unrewarding for the player.
The game currently features only 5 dinosaurs to hunt which isn't bad to start, but it get's old fast. This isn't helped by the fact that two of them behave very similarly, so you basically only have 4 unique dinos to hunt.
Again, if the game were recieving constant updates this would be fine, but it's become pretty clear that this game is dead to them so they can work on more lucrative projects.
The only bonus I guess would be that nothing is locked behind a pay wall like in theHunter. You get everything just for buying the game.
That being said, the game itself is fun. It is an actual hunting simulator that you hunt dinosaurs in. Many people complain that it takes too long to get from A to B and that there isn't enough going on for most of the game. While things are spread VERY far appart and it can take a long time to walk to where you want to go... it's a hunting simulator.
You're supposed to track things for a long time and have to walk long distances. It makes it feel more real for me. Just don't be expecting to run into the dino you're looking for after a few minutes or have giant, fast paced battles constantly.
The game is very much: walk, track, walk, track, walk, track, shoot, track, walk, etc.
Again, fine for some people, but not most.
The main point of complaint would be lack of updates. The game does feel unfinished with only 5 dinos and no real reward system other than just buying better equipment. (Which is actually just annoying due to ammo and weight restrictions.)
TL;DR: Amazing concept and execution hampered by the fact that the devs care more about money than this game. It's fun for a few hours but get's old fast. If you really want a realistic dino hunting game, buy this when it's on sale.

As of 30/05/15 I have played much more Victoria 1 than 2 however that will soon change. Personally I love both games in short I loved Victoria 1 as it allowed me to function militarily or economically in huge detail, whereas most games only allowed me to do one of these in the detail I wanted. As in my review for Victoria 1 I would like to point out once again how this game is not for the casual gamer due to the deep and complex systems that you must learn to manage through error to be victorious in militarily, economic or political means.
The biggest advantage over Victoria 1 is the diplomacy this is more in depth and allows you to gain power by been wise and commanding of the world, instead of a rudimentary system where only alliances and basic trades are implemented. Most features of this game are easy to grasp at basic levels but to use them to their capacity a few games will have to be played to learn from the mistakes that you will undoubtedly do and suffer from. For most players the combat system in Victoria 2 is less complex than 1 I personally have not noticed much difference, however considering this game is about retaining power and control when it is slipping away from you been simpler is arguably the military commanders doing this. However for those who are to aggressive and don't exploit the other excellent features in the economic and diplomatic fields be warned of infamy.
In my Victoria 1 review I talked about the outdated graphics, whilst I still stand about how they are unique and you will get used to them the graphics on Victoria 2 are much better and I do prefer them by no means is this an ugly game. Whilst impressive graphics are not included they do their job and are not key for a strategy game. Another improvement over Victoria 1 is the population control instead of just assigning roles you can also influence what gets built and who wins the elections in a far more complex system which fits the game.
The fact you can play as any nation at the starting points allows replayability, but can you maintain your nations status or will you destroy the old powers? Build a new economic or military superpower which will have the old orders living in fear and the nations previously aligned to them at your will instead?
Militarist, economist or diplomat? New or old order? The world can be your oyster but can you make it?

Let me start off by saying I have not played the first two Dungeon Siege games, so I cannot say this game did or did not kill the series or something like that. And although this was my first Dungeon Siege, I can honestly say I immensely enjoy this game. I loved how I could actually control my character's movements instead of just clicking on some part of the map and wait for them to get there. It makes me feel more involved. Also, the combat was absolutely great and at times a great challenge. The abilities the four hero's have were all fun to use, and they each felt different from the other's. Something that really impressed me was that when you change any part of your armor, so too did your character. I do not tend to see my character's look change with other RPG games like this one, so it was just nice to see something as simple as this being implemented.
Now, despite what I said, I still have faults with the game. I have to agree with many others when saying that camera was a pain at times. It was too close to the player, and at times it made me feel constricted. However, is the camera beyond awful and ruin the whole game? No, not even close. I also would find myself getting stuck in objects towards the later levels for some reason. I would be walking then uh oh, I am now stuck in a log, or what have you. I also see many complain about the confusing skill tree, clunky AI, bad controls, and for some reason picking up objects. I really do not understand their complaints because one: the skill is so simple to use. You literally choose what ability you want(only certain levels let you pick an ability), where you want your proficiency, and what talent you want. It is so straight forward. As for the AI, I have never had a problem. My companion was always helpful ( I have not played co-op) and never felt useless, and the enemies were not mindless oafs. I also thought the controls were just fine. There was nothing confusing about them (I played keyboard and mouse). And picking up objects? Really? If there are a lot of items near you, press ctrl. You now just picked up everything. No reason for that to be a struggle.
If this is your first Dungeon Siege game (because apparently this is not worthy of being called a Dungeon Siege), or if you like action RPGs, I recommend this game. It is beautiful, addictive, and the story is actually pretty awesome. I got hooked with it and felt really involved in it. It really is a solid gaming experience, and I wish more people could see that. I also recommend getting the DLC as well. Raises level cap, grants enchanting weapons and armor, and adds a good lengthy and engaging mission. The game is great and I highly recommend picking this one up.

The next in my long line of pretty appalling reviews. I played this (on normal) for around 8hrs, and was level 11, completing as far as I know all of the side quests and getting to the end of Act I.
Graphics
@@@@@
The game is about three years old, but Titan Quest is older, but looks much better. Nice enough, but nothing special. There is a gamma setup, but I think its more to annoy you - making get stuck on the scenery to add to its difficulty.
Maps
@@@@
The area's seem varied enough, but oh my god is it bad in how its presented. All ARPGs are huge open maps that are basically mazes, with natural terrain to force you to backtrack as required, but using these dead ends as boss encounters or hidden chest areas. In DS3, you are in a series of corridors. I am nearly having a panic attack as I play this game, its so claustrophobic.
The map is beyond woeful. Imagine trying to navigate from Lands End to John o Groats with your map that looks like a small circle with a line going from South to North. That's what your map looks like. Sometimes its a little wiggly, but its basically a line. You can change the zoom once, or you can remove the map. There is no overall map and no map overlay of the area and no adjustable zoom to be of any use at all. Quest markers lead you to think that you are heading in the right place, but are miles away from where you think they are.
Mobs
@@@@
You get swarmed a lot, and need very early on to perfect the hit, roll, hit, roll, hit, roll technique if you don't want to be dead. I am not sure why you can roll faster than you can run, nor why just about EVERYTHING can run faster than you to swarm you as they run down the corridor, sorry I mean through the dense forest that is so overgrown apart from the perfectly manicured path.
Mobs are a little samey, bandits and spiders so far, but the Boss mobs and encounters have had some interesting attacks.
Skill Tree, UI & Classes
@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
Lets start with the UI. Basic is the word, and nothing is contextual, meaning you have to wonder what on earth the empty orb things are that appear to be un-learnt skills are as no little pop up box helpfully appears.
The Skill section is something else. I am still not entirely sure what the Proficiencies do, as I think they only work when you expend your focus with your Ability 1 button (normally 1) You then change Stance to do something else and while in this stance, the 1 button does something different, but 4 always heals and 5 always does the other buff spell....its simply too confusing, when other games would allow you to use the orbs as you wish. Its reported to be a console port and one that has had no PC love at all. It shows.
There is a nice balance on the active skills, as you can only rank them to 5 in total and you have two choices per skill, so you can have 3/2 or 0/5 as you wish. Filling all 5 'empowers' the skill, meaning it now has a more powerful effect - multiple targets instead of one or heal all the party rather than just you.
You get Passive skills as well, which are normally based on x% per rank.
Leveling is quite annoying though, it waits for the second you have finished a fight then goes to the character screen. So you cannot find a save point, then level and test a skill or anything. Its just annoying - like running into a wall.
Controls & Camera
@@@@@@@@@@@
Right click move and left click fire as usual, but you also have forward and back and lefty/right camera angles. You need them as well, as getting stuck on scenery happens a lot, getting stuck in corners happens in swarms and thats why I think the dodge roll was added. Spacebar adds a block move, while space and move rolls on that direction.
The camera is a mad thing that sweeps in and out at a moments notice. Nothing becomes see through, solid objects block its viewpoint, and boss fights in a room can see you looking at the floor a few feet in front of you as the camera changes without you doing anything.
You cannot direct your team members at all. Not with their spell choices or when to do anything. They do revive you if you fall, but forget directing them at the boss or the boss's minions, depending on your strategy.
You cannot click on targets to switch - it seem to be locked to the last one you attacked and you will contain to shoot the one miles away that you first started attacking while another beats you to death at close range. This is VERY annoying during the big boss fights, as you are shooting backwards and hitting barrels and chairs rather than your intended target.
Controls are not responsive either. There have been plenty of times when I have had to mash a button to get the heal to work (and I had enough foucs to use) and sometimes the roll dodge causes you to stand still and blck instead of roll, and as you are ALWAYS doing this, you are always facing the wrong way to block something.
Loot
@@@
Loads of it, which is nice, and you can upgrade your weapons with essences you find.
Gameplay
@@@@@
On one hand its all a bit meh! to be fair, while on the other so frustrating its beyond belief. At the end of act one you have a BIG boss fight that takes place in a tiny room. In single player, you can do nothing but fire off a quick ranged attack, then roll twice, then fire off an attack, then roll twice.....all aggro is on you all the time as you let your AI partner fight the boss and you just run away. If you miss a beat, she does so much damage that you lose half your hits in one go, and her she fires something off that takes away the other half. You have to roll as this is quicker than running, and if you dont roll she (as everyone else) runs 200% of your speed and chops your face off. If your AI party member drops in combat, you have no chance to revive her as you cannot get far enough away to spend the few seconds required to get her up again, and.....I wont say anymore about the fight, but it gets worse.
This is not difficulty levels being too high, this is being hampered by game mechanics that are just♥♥♥♥♥♥ Camera angles, confined space and mechanics all together. Take the Dragon in Torchlight - now that was a rock hard fight, and while running and kiting is a sound mechanic, that felt brilliant. This? Nah. I have tried and failed a dozen times now, but with pretty much all of the above rantings going against it already, I should go back to Assassins Creed II and finish that off.

EDIT: I also want to point out that not everything is peaches and pretty little flowers in relationships or peoples lives. Yeah some of the story accepts this abuse in some way, but there are people in this world who do, or do accept it because of certain circumstances, or because maybe they realize a person can be saved. Not everything has to be the *perfect* romance. Just my two cents.

I'm sorry, but this is the most boring visual novel I've ever played so far. I don't like it when I have unfinished games and locked achievements, but I can't do anything in this case, I just can't finish it.
Pros:
+ the art is nice (even though sometimes anathomy and proportions  are just ridiculous)
+ the voice acting is nice
+ the concept is quite good
+ there are some relatively interesting places in the plot, but...
Cons:
- ...this places are in the end of each route so you'll have to suffer for at least 3 hours to make it to them.
- the dialogues are bad. Just bad. Boring, poorly written, illogical, overflowing with Orion and guys telling protagonist, what does she think or feel right now, boring again.
- the characters are awfully plain and cliched, things they say made me cringe, a lot. Sometimes it was really painful.
- the protagonist is irritatingly passive. She hardly ever speaks. She hardly ever reacts. And it's not like she is just a kuudere or dandere type. There are countless amount of moments when somebody asks a direct question to protagonist. You expect some choices to pop up, but — nothing. The one who asked a question answers to himself and makes conclusions about what do you think or feel without your responce. Then he makes a decision about what to do then. You, the player, just feel like a wordless dog.
- the protagonist has no personality at all. Literally. I almost laughed out when one of the guys said something like: "Now when I know what it's like to be with you I couldn't bear to lose you". Well it's definitely terribly painful to lose relationships with a person who has a personality of a slice of bread.
All in all, it's a visual novel with
uninteresting story and characters. But it looks and sounds nice.

The Curious Expedition is a pixel art, rougelite, hero-management, survival-race game versus the AI. You play as one of history's famous explorers or other major culture icon that you would have learned about in high school history. You only have a limited selection to choose from when starting out but as you play the game you will unlock more. Each with their own starting bonus of some kind.
The game changes between tile based movement and text based choice options with dice roll based modifiers. Depending on the makeup of your part you will have dice with different bonuses that will aid in that endeavour.
That doesn't come without its risks, if you decide to send in the scout of your group into a cave it's entirely possible he will roll poorly and won't ever see daylight again. Robbing you not only of the loot he or she would have found but robbing you of available inventory slots that you were keeping all your current gear in. Thus encumbering your group either forcing you to give up some precious loot or run back to your ship and drop off some items. Hoping you don't run out of food before the end of your trip.
Speaking of which, to goal of each trip is to discover the golden pyramid of each country you visit. Oddly, if I am to believe the game’s idea of these pyramids. it is completely normal for 18th century explorers to have magical compasses that pointed them in the goal of their objective.
While personally i do not like the way this game handles combat. Making everything a decision based on the dice you rolled and hoping the AI rolls poorly. It was implemented just right where the payoff for either avoiding it or diving right into the fight was worth it.
I find this is a good game to pick up and play for a good 15 minutes to a half hour at time. Maybe when you're first learning its mechanics you will have some longer sessions then that. Despite the simple mechanics behind this game when you get out of the tactical level of things and look at the higher level strategy of playing through things get more complex. Once you learn everything though, games tend to go quickly.
If you want a game that has fun pixel art and has you managing a small group of heroes this game is for you. The roguelike mechanics are very lite so you do not expect huge variations on multiple playthroughs but their should be replayability for most players.
Truly a fun little game. Offers both a decent challenge and excitement factor.

A lot of people have criticized this game for being slow-paced and having only a small selection of dinosaurs to hunt.  I think it's because a lot of folks purchased this game expecting it to be like Turok - a fast paced, blood-soaked, action-shooter.  But this game plays a lot more like an open-world Resident Evil/Don't Starve with dinosaurs.  This game is about tension, about patience, and about getting scared out of your pants.  The open-world is gorgeous, and unlike most open-world games, this one seems empty - just as a real wild area would feel.  This means when you find a dinosaur or, more likely, groups of them, the impact on you and your choices and gameplay is enormous.  And having only a few species in any one area is more "realistic" anyway, a small island can't support big populations.  Each dinosaur species requires completely unique strategies and tactics to take it down, and will hunt (or not hunt) you in completely different ways.  That's much more enriching than having 500 monsters who all just bum-rush you and just need a headshot to kill them.  Yawn.
The first time you're staring at a treeline and see a pack of raptors melt out of the shadows and start stalking across the open plains, or are cresting a ridgeline and see, in the distance, a huge tyrannosaur wandering along the ridge toward you, silhouetted against the starlit sky, and you start praying to anyone who's listening that it goes the other way and never finds you. . . you'll be hooked, I promise.
I won't lie, this game is *rough*. It definitely feels like an indie game, the controls can be a bit buggy, and the AI oscillates wildly from being unutterably brilliant to "that raptor keeps running into that tree".  But in terms of pure, emotional turmoil and painting a picture of constant tension and subtle, creeping terror I've simply never ever seen in a game before, Hunter Primal is worth a shot.  So, pick this up if you want a deep adrenaline rush.  Don't pick it up if you want Call of Duty with dinosaurs.  Simple as that.
P.S. This game gives me nightmares about being hunted by dinosaurs.  That's how well it's crafted to get at your mammalian prey-instincts!

It's a platformer. Nothing you haven't seen before, nothing you won't see again. You play a small robot (with some story, but I admittedly skipped through to play the game) who has a warhead for a buddy. He gives you exposition, and tips as to how to move around in the world. Platforms, elevators, guns, bombs, grenades... Lots of stuff to go boom.
PROS:
If you like platformers, this is well worth it for the price. I think I paid around 42 cents, and that's always worth a game to me. The level designs are interesting and harken back to the golden age of 8 bit things jumping onto 8 bit things. The music is 8 bit as well, and pretty good (although gets a tad repetitive, and feels a bit like I'm stuck in a Pokemon battle). The weapons are interesting, as your three weapons do three different things. Controlling your missile buddy is a game in itself, having to manuever him through quick turns at fast speeds through maze-like structures. It feels rewarding, too, if at times too easy.
CONS:
Even without skipping the intro, I don't think there's enough telling you what you can and cannot step on. Maybe it's a little obvious, and I a little too drunk, but there seem to be several areas where you learned where NOT to jump only after jumping. Sure, the save points are frequent enough, and the gameplay itself easy enough, but still... a little direction goes a long way. The music is a bit much, especially if you're just stuck on a part and it's there thumpin' along in the background, but it's pleasant initially.
Should you get it? If you like platformers and 42 cent indie games, yeah it's worth it. I got about a half hour out of it, and I'll most likely come back to it. I consider that worth the money I paid for it, and it's not a bad little platformer.

Endless Legend is what happens if Alpha Centauri and Heroes of Might and Magic 4 had an illegitimate child that was adopted and raised by Endless Space. With this heritage it comes to little surprise that the 'just one more turn' factor is really strong in its DNA, making this game highly addicting!
In all seriousness, though, this game has the best of all of the above: the modular unit design and 3D terrain of AC, hero management and tactical combat like any good Heroes game (I just mentioned Heroes 4 above, because EL's graphical style and general vibe reminded me quite a bit of that one), and lastly the clean interface and well-executed core 4X mechanics of Endless Space.
That's not to say it's without flaws, however. While the combat system goes in a very uncommon (but very interesting) direction for a 4X game with its usage of terrain and Heores-y tactical interface, there are still a few gripes with the actual execution, reminiscent of some of the issues with Endless Space: You can only give orders to your units before the turn is executed and the more specific your orders (move there and then attack that unit), the more prone they are to failure if the enemy moves first.
There are also a few hiccups with the interface, for example I still haven't found an option to automatically adjust production queues after unit upgrades. Maybe it isn't there (although ES had an option like this) or it's just not placed in an intuitive place.
But apart from these issues, the game can really shine. The playable factions encourage very different play styles, have pretty interesting background stories that are explorable through the quest victory quest lines. Minor factions give the game a bit of a further twist and the interspersed winter periods are something extra to consider in your plannings.
All in all, this game might well be the most interesting 4X game I have played in the last years - highly recommended!

The tutorial is completely insufficient for the depth the game calls for, and though the tool tips that appear when you hover over anything are handy, there are so many actions, recquirments, and mechanics that go unmentioned and unexplained until you google them. The second thing detracting from the game for me was the unsteady state of multiplayer. The game is great fun to play with friends - its like a hardcore game of Catan and Risk and Warhammer and more all rolled into one - but connectivety issues get in the way after, reliably, 75 to 100 turns. If the connectivity issues alone were fixed, the whole thing would be perfect.

The game is set much like Diablo but without the randomly generated maps. I really wanted to like this game, I really did. Especially since so many people recommended this to me as one of the holy grails of otome games. I was very excited to try this game, but after my first playthrough I felt very confused and disappointed. So I tried another route, thinking that I just had a bad route on my first try. The second route I tried was even worse than the first. I did not like this game at all. Perhaps it was my incredibly high expectations for this game that made it such a large disappointment. But either way, the game was just not enjoyable at all.
The main problem I have with this game is the story and characters. The story is very cliche and the game sometimes moves at a painfully slow rate. The characters are so unrealistic and their actions and motives make absolutely no sense at all. Almost all of the guys are either egocentric jerks or literal psychopaths. They never apologize for their hurtful behavior. EVER. These men constantly hurt the protagonist and expect her to forgive them and welcome them with open arms without showing any remorse or guilt over their previous actions. The only way to get the "good ends" involve either forgiving them, submitting to them, apologising for things that are not your fault, or ignoring their behaviour. The routes I played just aggravated me. I hated the fact that these men treated me so poorly and I was just supposed to ignore it. This game would be great if the premise was to teach people what unhealthy abusive relationships look like. But unfortunately, that is not the case.
The protagonist has literally no personality at all. And I get that the character you play as often doesn't have as much depth as the characters you meet, but this was just ridiculous. The entire game you feel like Orion is controlling all of your emotions and thoughts-- because he pretty much is. This character has no thoughts. She simply has Orion to tell her his feelings and what HE thinks she should do in the situation.
This game was just bad. Each time I played it I became very anxious to just get it over with and finish it already. Then each time I ended a route, I felt even more annoyed than when I was playing because the endings were so awful and uneventful. It's very unfortunate that a game with such beautiful art and stellar voice acting would be cursed with such a bad plot and characters. My advice on this game is to simply steer clear.

The art and writing is really nice and a big part of what makes this game so pleasant to play. Sound design and music is very decent. Although not super historically accurate it still scratches that exact kind of itch. The way you approach your expeditions has multiple approaches, such as trying to maximize fame, maximize fortune, or just trying to survive and restore the loyalty of your crew. You also get to prepare for your expeditions depending on the climate you plan to embark on.
Combat is really cool, each member of your crew gets a certain set of dice, and during combat you get 3 rounds to roll your dice before the enemy gets to go. You then make combinations of these dice to create certain moves, in a Yahtzee kinda fashion. Or you can build your group around avoiding combat, and specializing your loadout/playstyle for that.
I also really appreciate the difficulty level. You have to make very tough and intelligent calls to survive your trip based on randomized encounters, and there are plenty of compelling greed incentives to make things spicy. RNG can really screw you but it's up to you to play that out conservatively and get your crew out with minimal damage. No matter what your expedition should have a chance at success if you play smart and plan for the future. You play a series of expeditions and have a chance to compensate for a couple disasters.
The amount of characters and starting loadouts you can choose is huge and pretty interesting, although not quite diverse enough to make any one character require that drastic of a playstyle change. This makes unlocking all of them a bit irrelevant if you aren't into completionism. The maps also get to be a bit samey, even across climates. You can tell that once you learn the systems the game will start to lose it's fresh feeling of exploration, at around the 5-8 hour mark. However the gameplay mechanics seem have enough depth to keep it interesting even after that, as a sort of roguelike text adventure.
A small technical problem I encountered is freezing after alt-tabbing the game. But of course that could be specific to my computer.
Overall a very solid game, 7.5/10 in my book. Must play for those that like text adventure/roguelike genres. I  gotta be honest I don't see myself playing it too much longer but that is no knock to the game itself. I just get bored quickly. The $15 price may be a little steep if you aren't hyped on the atmospheric, anthropology/historical side of this game. If there were more specified character loudouts, additional writing and music, and diversity of encounters I could see $15. But for $10 or $5 I'd say is a good price to buy at and very fair in my opinion.

This is a good game.  It's not fantastically polished, it's not intuitive, it's certainly not much of a survival game in the traditional sense.  That said, the game is solid, it's fantastically atmospheric and there is a very definite survival component - don't get eaten!
While I would not have asked anyone to make this game the way it is I would recommend this game, at this price, to anyone simply for the atmospheric value.  The feeling of being alone, barely armed, without explicit direction, in a tropical forest of towering, rain-lashed trees, desperately listening between the booming thunderclaps for the sound of a pernicious dromeosaurid, is masterfully implemented.  Genuinely, this feels like you're lost in Jurassic Park, except that the animals are realistic.  No six-foot, bald deinonychus masquerading as velocirapotors, but feathers a-plenty.
It appears as though bets were thoroughly hedged during the making of this game, and the design choices seem to be split between a traditional hunting game, a survival game and, perhaps, some implicit marketing for the devs' other game TheHunter.  While I would have preferred a traditional hunting game with set hunts, bag limits, licenses and an out-of-game loadout menu, or a traditional survival game with crafting and hunger elements, this game manages to get all the core action elements of stealth, shot placement and an arsenal of weapons from a hunting game and combines it with truly phenomenal scenery and atmosphere, in a surprisingly streamlined package.
I recommend playing multiplayer vs. alone - the community (who I have met ingame) are extremely nice, happy to help people out and lead the way.  The use of gear spawns around the map, as opposed to making money to buy gear which is bound to you, seems to be very successful in encouraging cooperation and sharing of toys.
Don't listen to anyone saying that the game is abandoned - it still receives updates every now and then.  It's just not top of the list of priorities of the devs.  For this price, you shouldn't expect it to be.

Been a long time player of the game from FM2005 and have played FM16 extensively as well
The 30 minute video that Miles put up before the BETA was launched was interesting and I decided to buy the game .
There may be people who term this game as a skin of FM16 but I would say its much more than that .
The game feels crisper and there have been improvements in the 3d engine . Please do not expect FIFA level graphics on the 3d engine . I am just happy that its an improvement .
The engine , hmm . Last years overpowered fullbacks are gone , gone are the times when the fullbacks would give you 15 assists per season .
Tactics of FM16 don't work in FM17 . The analysis part has hugely improved . I love the match analysis report that your coach gives you before the start of the game and also tells you about how the opposition played in the last game . It adds a new dimension to the game as you know which players to target and where majorly their goals will come from
Also the heatmap is a good indicator to show where your team is playing majorly and where it needs improvement .
The social media interaction is also pretty good I must say . It certainly isn't fantastic but its a good start . You love it when it first appears , after that its the same lines over and over again apart from a few funny ones in the middle .
I would love if they keep adding new lines of texts with smaller updates to keep this social media interaction fresh .
Training - Didn't see much of a change in the training but I would have loved to see a bit more control on them . In today's age , training methods of different managers are how they play the game . I would love to be able to do that and assess players in training and then decide on my squad on how a particular person trains that week .
The interface is pretty smooth . Smooth transitions and easy accessibility to menus which I really like .
All in all its been good so far , apart from a few bugs which will be sorted by the time the full game comes out .
I am going with 3.5/5 to the game . It isnt necessarily 16 but it just does enough to differentiate between 16 . Also nothing pathbreaking ,but you will indeed have a lot of fun playing this game .
